<a id="d-331"></a>
## D-331 — duplicate open or cohorts collapse to the most-advanced one at the merge seam; the losers' live branches are wiped and re-derive under the keeper (2026-09-01,, maintainer-approved)

**What.** The or-uniqueness gate ([I-219](30_invariants.md#i-219)) stops NEW duplicate cohorts; this decision handles the pre-merge ones. The end-of-burst `retireDuplicateOrCohorts` drain (between `drainDeadOrBranches` and `freezeResolvedOrBranches`) groups each scope's processed-or ledger entries by their canonical spelling; a group holding two or more OPEN cohorts keeps exactly one — **the one with the most statements already registered under its `_ordis_` branch scopes** (the maintainer's ordering: progress already made), ties to the byte-lex-smaller signature — and retires the rest: live branches wiped (`pendingWipeScopes`, same burst), scheduling rows erased (`orDisjunctCount` / `orPendingBranches` / `orPendingLevels` / `orStarterPick`), ledger row cleared. Frozen branches, `orBookkeeping` runs, `orRetiredDisjuncts` and all history stay.

**Why.** Two cohorts that became equi variants after both opened are one case split running twice — duplicated branch work forever, since cohort identity is exact-text (I-167) and baked into the branch scope names (no re-key possible). The maintainer's ruling: remove all except one; whatever the removed ones had derived re-derives later under the keeper. Keeping the most-advanced cohort minimizes the re-derivation.

**Rejected.** (a) Re-keying the loser's cohort onto the canonical signature — the signature is embedded in every branch scope name; renaming scopes violates the packed-key design and I-45's namespace preservation. (b) Retiring frozen branches too — a frozen branch's derivations are load-bearing for goal closure and the chapter walker (I-206); with the count row gone the loser cannot converge, so its frozen remnants are inert and harmless. (c) Gate-only (let existing duplicates run out) — sound but leaves the duplicated work in place; the maintainer chose removal.

<a id="d-330"></a>
## D-330 — SSD deload derives from the batch's backend: processor batches page by default, CUDA batches are resident-only (2026-09-01,, maintainer-directed)

**The choice.** `ProverParameters::allow_ssd_deload` defaults true and is derived at the single backend-ownership boundary in the `ExpressionAnalyzer` constructor: the effective permission is `allow_ssd_deload && phase2Backend == cpu`. A processor-routed batch therefore runs the established working-set pager and extent path exactly as before the GPU campaign, a CUDA-routed batch always runs the resident-only steward, and a config may still set the key false to pin a processor batch resident. This supersedes [D-329](#d-329)'s `allow_ssd_deload` clause (global default false); the CUDA/SSD mutual exclusion itself is unchanged.

**Why.** Resident-only was a safe global default while the full-run CUDA route was landing, but it silently removed SSD paging from processor batches whose working sets are entitled to exceed RAM; the backend, not a global default, is the natural owner of the decision (maintainer: deload allowed when the batch uses the processor — a batchwise decision).

<a id="d-329"></a>
## D-329 — batch policy owns CUDA Phase 2 and counterexample filtering while SSD deload is excluded (2026-08-30,, maintainer-authorized research architecture)

> **`allow_ssd_deload` clause superseded by [D-330](#d-330):** the key now defaults true and derives false for CUDA batches at construction.

**The choice.** `ProverParameters::use_gpu` defaults true and selects CUDA whenever `--phase2-backend` is absent; every batch may set it false for the processor route. `ProverParameters::allow_ssd_deload` separately defaults false and may also be overridden per batch. CUDA plus SSD deload is an invalid state asserted at `ExpressionAnalyzer` construction, so CUDA uses a resident-only `MemorySteward`; processor mode remains eligible for the established deload path. The selected backend also owns counterexample filtering: CUDA batches group sixteen private conjecture clones into each direct CUDA Phase 2 call and never replay those proof semantics through the processor route.

**Full-run ownership.** Incubator and main logical blocks retain their semantic task-family boundary while exact capacity measurement streams physical chunks through one persistent fixed device allocation. Structurally impossible request families and whole zero-work LBs are omitted. Within each chunk, exactly identical immutable name/rule columns share one slice, executable batch kinds select the only working/overall/local/local-delta hash-memory pairs projected, and omitted pairs retain zero-length descriptors at their fixed enum ordinals. `BytesKeyStore` maintains exact logical bytes at every mutation door so capacity measurement is constant-time in the number of keys.

**Why.** Backend ownership belongs to the batch because a complete `main.py` run mixes independently configured theorem families and counterexample filters. SSD paging and a host-snapshot CUDA route create competing state ownership and transfer boundaries; their combination is deliberately excluded until an exact GPU-aware deload protocol exists. Capacity streaming closes the shortcut route's fixed-size assumption without changing request order, doom ownership, or sealed output.

**Measured boundary.** Full CUDA runs complete all seven prover batches and both filters with 139,241 verifier checks and zero failures. Exact immutable-column sharing improves Phase 2 by only 1.12 to 1.56 times. Executable-family hash-memory selection removes only about 0.01 percent of the dominant IncubatorPeano1 aggregate entries and key bytes and is performance-neutral. The retained next architecture therefore puts universal encoded/remaining-argument maps and other evaluation-only columns behind GPU survivor detection, then retains unchanged projected columns on device by an exact generation contract. Evidence and failure history are in [`docs/GPU/gpu_main.md`](../GPU/gpu_main.md).

**Rejected for this stage.** A hidden processor fallback; GPU prover plus processor counterexample filtering; CUDA with uncoordinated SSD deload; truncation at any capacity; moving descriptor ordinals when a column is absent; or treating a hash or size match as sufficient for immutable-column sharing.

<a id="d-328"></a>
## D-328 — every production incubator batch is eligible for the statistics-driven LB split (2026-08-30,, maintainer-directed)

**The choice.** `ConfigIncubatorPeano1`, `ConfigIncubatorPeano2`, `ConfigIncubatorGauss1`, `ConfigIncubatorGauss2`, and `ConfigIncubatorGauss3` all set `lb_split: true`. The existing `isStraggler` policy remains the only decision that changes an LB from one part to the deterministic machine-core fan-out: balanced small-LB grids remain unsplit, while a measured heavy incubator LB may split exactly like a main-batch LB. CUDA capacity packing keeps every split LB's task family together, so a physical device chunk never changes the family's semantic ownership or merge order.

**Why.** Incubator mode is not a reason to prohibit splitting, and the maintainer explicitly removed the remaining configuration prohibition. The earlier four-config opt-out in [D-231](#d-231) predated full-run CUDA measurements and prevented the established straggler mechanism from acting on unexpectedly heavy incubator LBs. Eligibility is safer than predicting workload shape from the batch name: the all-integer trigger already declines work below its fair-share and setup floor.

**Boundaries.** `lb_split` remains a per-config switch and `disable_lb_split` remains the separate one-part diagnostic mode. Counterexample clones stay unsplit through the `ceFilteringActive` gate. This changes scheduling eligibility, not hashburst semantics; theorem, verifier, and deterministic-artifact gates remain mandatory, and split-versus-unsplit proof-process artifacts are compared and reported under [D-201](#d-201).

**Verification.** `test_lb_split.cpp::lb_split_config_wiring` loads all five incubator configurations and requires the flag to be true. Full-run before/after timing, theorem identity, repeated-GPU determinism, and verifier evidence are recorded in `docs/GPU/gpu_main.md`.

<a id="d-320"></a>
## D-320 — the B8 level-exact condition is removed from the `applyEquivalenceClass` commit; not-yet-known is the sole admission control on the orbit path (2026-08-31,, maintainer-approved)

**What.** The orbit commit in `applyEquivalenceClass` drops the `effectiveMaxLevel!= memoryBlock.level` refusal (introduced on B8). A rewritten product now commits exactly when it is not yet known at the deposit scope (the `intStatementLevelsMap` probe — per [I-85](30_invariants.md#i-85) the one membership control; `intEncodedStatements` is an index-less `PagedVector` whose dedupe is this probe), subject to the unchanged D-273 ancestor-scope refusal and the iteration/pattern caps. The committed run stays the inherited base ∪ pair union — no residence level is added.

**Why.** Trap-proven root cause of the 4 lost Gauss fold lemmas on the canonical-door branch (`[FOLD-ORBIT-TRAP]`): the level-2 fold LB derives AND mails the distinct spelling `(in2[2,it_0_lev_0_30,int_lev_2_1])` the level-4 restriction rule needs, but the receiving LB's canonical door rewrites the arriving non-canonical deposit to its already-known folded twin and ends it — by design, mail never delivers a non-canonical spelling below its home LB. The deep orbit regenerates the spelling, and the level-exact gate refused it (`{0,2}` ≠ 4), leaving the fold family unprovable. On the canonical-only design the orbit is the sole source of copy-split statements (the gate's own comment), so a level condition on this path contradicts the door: it forbids the orbit from materializing exactly the ancestor-fact spellings the door refuses per mail. The maintainer's ruling: the levels doctrine's "belongs shallower" reading has no enforcement place on the orbit path; known-ness is the only correct control.

**Rejected.** (a) Registering ancestor-mailed non-canonical arrivals at the receiving door — a second admission path for copies; keeping mail canonical-only preserves the single source. (b) Relaxing the gate only for products citing LB-local names — repairs the IncubatorGauss3 shape but not the fold case (all names ancestor-visible). (c) Collapsed-shape rule matching alone — much larger surface (every key probe + CUDA twins) than this theorem family needs.

<a id="d-324"></a>
## D-324 — the three settled/reformulated-head deposits in the registration drains are deleted; the compact broadcast alone re-derives the head (2026-08-31,, maintainer-approved)

**What.** The three `nextIterationInternalMail` head deposits in the post-join registration drains are removed: `updateGlobalDirect`'s reformulation-branch deposit at the reformulated chain LB, `updateGlobal`'s induction-promotion deposit of the settled head at the theorem's chain LB, and `updateGlobal`'s reformulation-branch deposit. Each drain already compacts and broadcasts the same theorem (`recordPendingCompaction` → D-76 compact via root mail), so the head re-derives at the chain LB from its own seed premises when the broadcast rule fires — with residence-honest levels `{0..chain-1}` and a standard firing origin the chapter walker resolves through the compact chain (expansion → `compilation` → theorem). `updateGlobal`'s settled-goal ERASE stays, now followed by a bare `hasWork` latch (the flag is never-deloaded logical state, I-153; the broadcast itself wakes every LB via `mailPeek`). The D-240 / D-279 disproof/settlement machinery is untouched.

**Why.** Trap-proven root cause of the branch's missing Peano row `(>[1,2,3,4,5,6](AnchorPeano[1,2,3,4,5,6])(>[7,8](in3[6,7,8,4])(in3[7,6,8,4])))` ("1+n=m ⟹ n+1=m", level-refused at registration): each deposit fabricated its level run as `{0..ky.size}` — one PAST the receiving chain LB's level universe (the LB at `accessMemory(ky)` has level `ky.size-1`). The induction-promoted composite "1+n=m ⟹ m=s(n)" deposited its head `(in2[7,8,3])` at the shared premise LB stamped `{0,1,2}`; the poison propagated through the successor-injectivity firing, the `(8 ↔ it_0_lev_1_12)` class pair, and every 8-spelled equi-product to the target's head, whose sealed `allLevelsInvolved` verdict then read lvN=3 ≠ level+1=2 and refused. `main` carries the identical three stamps but is masked by arrival order: without the canonical door the chain LB derives the head locally first with `{0,1}`, and the poisoned re-deposit is dropped by the registry's first-arrival-wins. The canonical door folds the head's spelling into the witness form early, so the poison becomes the first arrival.

**Rejected.** (a) Restamping the deposits `{0..ky.size-1}` — level-equivalent to what the broadcast firing produces anyway, but keeps a redundant second channel and its direct theorem-citing origin line (a chapter-walker aid from the era before multiple-path candidate loops, I-201). (b) Stamping `{-1}` — hides that the deposit duplicates the broadcast. (c) Making level consumers ignore levels above the receiving LB — treats the symptom at every reader.

<a id="d-327"></a>
## D-327 — the Pass-B rejection park captures the compound's levels as frame ∪ registry, not registry-lookup-only (2026-08-31,, maintainer-approved)

**What.** The it_ (algebra) rejection staging in `disintegrateExpr2` (the `pendingRejections.addRejection` block) fills the park record's level run with the merge of the frame's threaded deposit levels (`orSeedLevels`, the caller's `involvedLevels`) and the compound's `intStatementLevelsMap` row when one exists — ascending union, non-negative tier only. Previously the staging read only the registry row. The revival path is unchanged: the record's levels remain the authoritative deposit-time set; a run that is still empty means the parking compound itself was non-derived, and the `addStatement` door re-stamps `{-1}`.

**Why.** Trap-proven root cause of the IncubatorGauss3 loss on the canonical-door branch (theorem `(>[10](EnumerationSet3[2,6,7,10])!(interval[1,4,2,6,10]))`): within one arrival the kernel runs `disintegrateExpr2` — park included — BEFORE the stmts-loop's `addStatement` writes the compound's levels row, so on a fresh local deposit the registry lookup missed by construction and the record parked level-empty, while the true levels sat unused in the same function's own parameters. The revival then stamped the witness facts `{-1}`; the level omission propagated through the witness equality (`{0}`), the class pair (`{0}`), and every or4 re-split orbit product (`{0,1}`), which the B8 level-exact orbit commit gate refused at the level-2 LB (needs max = 2). The minting compact `(existence1[1,7,2,4])` had carried `{0,2}` since birth — the maintainer's inheritance semantics (an existence inherits its firing premises' levels) held everywhere except this seam. `main` carries the same `{-1}` stamps but tolerates them: its chain registers the unfolded fired head directly and picks up level 2 from the interval rules before any orbit commit is needed.

**Rejected.** (a) Sourcing the levels at revival time from the registry row — repairs the same records later but leaves the park lying about deposit-time state, and the compact's row can be gone at revival (wipes). (b) Stamping witness products with the mint LB's level — widens levels beyond consumption truth (the 2026-08-27 ruling) and changes accounting for every witness fact. (c) Relaxing the orbit commit gate for LB-local names — treats the symptom; the record's levels stay wrong for every other consumer.

<a id="d-323"></a>
## D-323 — the `performElemPhase1` entry clear of `changedClassesThisStep` is deleted; `standardProcessing` Step 7 is the tracker's sole clear (2026-08-31,, maintainer-approved)

**What.** `performElemPhase1` no longer clears `body.changedClassesThisStep` at step entry. The tracker's one clear is `standardProcessing`'s tail (Step 7), which already ran after every consumer (`applyEquiClasses` Pass 1, the deferred `cleanUpExpressions` sweep, the [I-194](30_invariants.md#i-194) recursion-products closure). A delta minted outside any `standardProcessing` call — LB seeding (`addTheoremToMemory`: variable-copy axioms, equality premises), post-join barrier deposits — now survives to the LB's next call and is back-applied to every pre-existing statement by Pass 1. Contract pinned as [I-215](30_invariants.md#i-215); regression test `equi_reshuffle.seeding_time_class_delta_survives_to_first_step`.

**Why.** Trap-proven root cause of the last Gauss gap on the canonical-door branch (the two-variable root `(>[9,10](interval[1,4,2,9,10])(in[9,10]))` and its cascades): at LB seeding the premise fact `(in[9,1])` lands in the registry (index 4), then the D-265 copy axiom `(=[9,9_copy])` creates class `{9, 9_copy}` at `main`, pushes the delta and seeds its Pass-2 waterline to the then-current registry size 8. The first step's entry clear discarded the delta before any `applyEquiClasses` ran; Pass 2 forever started at 8; the eight seeding statements were never multiplied, so `(in[9_copy,1])` never registered at `main` and everything downstream (`9+0=9ᶜ`, `0 ≤ 9ᶜ`, `9ᶜ ∈ 10`, the goal) stayed open. On `main` the loss is masked by direct rule firings deriving the copy forms redundantly; the canonical door folds those into the known base forms ([D-326](#d-326)), making the latent loss fatal. Since Step 7 runs at the tail of every `standardProcessing` call with no early return, the entry clear could only ever discard out-of-step deltas — exactly the ones that must be applied.

**The in-call window is deliberately left as-is.** A class minted after Step 4 inside one `standardProcessing` call is wiped by that call's Step 7 unconsumed — but the only producer in that window is `dischargeContradiction`'s head deposit, and every reacting role (incubator, CE filter, vacuous truth, normal premise LB) deactivates the LB in the same act, so the delta has no possible future consumer ([I-112](30_invariants.md#i-112)).

**Rejected.** (a) Seeding a new class's Pass-2 waterline at 0 — repairs only the statement-multiplication consumer; the cleanup sweep and the recursion-products closure would still never see an out-of-step class, and it duplicates Pass 1's re-scan per new class. (b) A consumed-prefix drop at Step 7 (`dropFirst(n)` at the Pass-1 fixpoint size) — closes the in-call window, but that window's sole producer deactivates its own LB, so there is nothing to close. (c) Routing the vacuous-truth head via internal mail — the depositing LB is deactivated in the same act and would never absorb it; keeping it alive one burst to absorb reworks the fire-once/deactivate contract ([I-78](30_invariants.md#i-78)) and runs a full burst on a contradictory statement set.

<a id="d-322"></a>
## D-322 — `updateEquivalenceClasses` merges every same-scope class that overlaps the merged class after the ancestor pass (2026-08-30,, maintainer-approved)

**What.** After the ancestor pass has grown the merged class with ancestor-class members (D-44), a fixpoint pass re-scans the classes at the entry's own scope: every class not merged in pass 1 that shares a member with the grown merged class is merged too — `mergeTwoEquivalenceClasses` with no equality-argument bridge picks the decoded-lex-min shared member as the bridge and carries no equality levels (the pair levels come from the two classes' own chains) — until no kept class overlaps. The merged classes are excluded from the write-back. Ancestor classes stay untouched (I-31).

**Why.** Trap-proven on the Peano batch (, LB `root → AnchorPeano → (in3[7,8,9,4]) → (in3[10,7,11,4]) → (in2[10,8,3]) → (in2[rec0,10,3])`, scope `main_boundary_ordis_(or1[1,it_0_lev_3_64,3,2])_(…)`): equality `(=[11,it_1_lev_4_280])` absorbed an ancestor class holding `{it_0_lev_3_64, it_0_lev_4_68, it_1_lev_4_236}`, while the same-scope class `{it_0_lev_3_64, it_0_lev_4_68, it_1_lev_4_1006, it_1_lev_4_236}` — which had absorbed that ancestor class before it grew — was kept because it contains neither equality argument. Pass 1 decides merge/keep by overlap with the equality's arguments and runs before the ancestor pass, so the write-back produced two classes at one scope sharing members; the `!eqArgsSubsetB` precondition of I-33 tripped on the next equality. Pre-existing on `main`; surfaced by the equality traffic the orbit products of [D-321](#d-321) generate.

**Rejected.** Widening the pass-1 test to "overlaps the merged class" before the ancestor pass (does not see ancestor-borne members); a one-shot second pass (a fixpoint merge can itself bring in members overlapping a further kept class).

<a id="d-321"></a>
## D-321 — an equivalence-class product is committed iff the statement is new in the registry; the origin map never gates it (2026-08-30,, maintainer-decided)

**What.** `applyEquivalenceClass`'s commit condition drops its `exprOriginMap` probe: a product `applied @ depositValidity` is registered when the statement-levels probe finds no row (and the max-level test holds), regardless of whether the origin map already has a row for that text. The `equality1` history emission keeps its own origin check ([I-34](#i-34), [D-48](#d-48)) — that is documentation dedup, not a proof decision.

**Why.** On the canonical-only design the deposit door folds every copy form (`X_copy → X`) and ends the deposit, keeping the raw producer line as process documentation. `applyEquiClasses` is therefore the sole source of copy-split statements (`(preorder[1,4,2,6_copy])` for the collision-pattern-exact rule keys, D-265) — the maintainer's rule: "the expression with `_copy` must be produced by applyEqui, and the results saved if they are new". Trap-proven on the Gauss lemma `(>[9](interval[1,4,2,6,9])(in[6,9]))`: four rule firings derived `(preorder[1,4,2,6_copy]) @main`, the door folded each and kept the line; the orbit of `(preorder[1,4,2,6])` then skipped the product because the text "already had an origin row", so the rule `0 ≤ x ∧ x ≤ 1 ⟹ x ∈ 9` never fired and `(in[6,9])` stayed open. The chapter [`05_equivalence_classes.md`](20_core_concepts/05_equivalence_classes.md) had always stated that the deposit is not gated — only the emission — so this also restores the documented contract (Rule 13 applied to code) and closes a standing Rule-16 violation (a proof decision routed on `exprOriginMap`).

**Kept.** The `max(levels) == memoryBlock.level` product gate and the class waterline (I-65) are untouched by this decision.

<a id="d-325"></a>
## D-325 — At the per-key origin cap the existing rows win; the class→body origin merge keeps every body row (2026-08-30) — retires the [D-49](#d-49) cap-full replacement

**What.** Every origin writer — the heap and cold `addOriginId` overloads, both `addMailOriginRecord` overloads, `MergeClassAccum::addOriginId`, and the string `ExpressionAnalyzer::addOrigin` — drops a newcomer once the key holds `max_origin_per_expr` rows; nothing is ever displaced, whatever the tags. The `updateEquivalenceClasses` origin sync (`exprOriginRunReplace`) now writes the body's existing lines first, verbatim, and dedup-appends the class lines while below the cap — a body row is never dropped behind a class row. The cap stays at 30 (history is already the largest memory consumer).

**Why.** The Peano batch's chapter export aborted on `buildStack`'s 5M-call tripwire in the `check_zero` chapter of right-distributivity. A least-fixpoint derivability pass over the exact graph the walker searches showed the goal `(in3[12,13,9,5])` had **no acyclic derivation at all** — the walker was exhausting a search that cannot succeed (191,804 of 191,814 failures on provably non-derivable nodes). Cause: the zero block collapses {2, 7, 8, 9, 13, …} into one class (canonical `13`); the canonical door rewrites every `0+X=Y` deposit to `(in3[13,X,Y,4])` with a bridge citing `(=[7,13])`; the cancellation theorem then re-derives `(=[7,13])` once per `(0+X=Y, 7+X=Y)` premise pair — 31–32 rows here, up to 128 in other LBs — every one circular for the walk. The only non-circular row a class-pair equality ever has is the `equality2` transitivity line from `mergeTwoEquivalenceClasses` (`(=[7,13]) ← (=[7,2]), (=[2,13])`, both derivable). At the 31st row D-49's "foundation displaces convenience" overwrote exactly that line: 12 of 12 class-pair equalities in the LB, one `cold-replace equality2 → implication` each (trap-measured). D-49's heuristic — non-equality rows are foundations, equality rows are conveniences — is inverted under the door.

**Trade-off.** A key that legitimately receives more than 30 distinct rows keeps its first 30 — chronological, which is what keeps the surviving set well-founded (a row's dependencies were written before it). The walker's candidate order is unchanged (`buildStack` still sorts non-equality tags first). Chapter content changes where the evicted rows return.

**Rejected.** Cap 60 (other LBs reach 128 attempts per key; the cap only moves the cliff). No cap (memory; the run-buffer constants are tied to it). A class-sibling re-route in the walker (measured inert on the previous commit). A fixpoint walker (a valid runtime idea, [OPEN-WALKER-NOGOOD](10_pipeline/04_prover.md) — not what this crash needs).

<a id="d-326"></a>
## D-326 — only the class-canonical form of a deposit is admitted; the deposit door canonicalizes under the classes at its own scope and skips a known canonical form (2026-08-28,, maintainer-directed)

- - **Context.** The IncubatorGauss3 heavy LB's phase-3 absorb offered ~106k internal-mail rows per burst; ~69k were class variants of known facts that paid the full door (`checkNecessityForEquality` sweep + `disintegrateExpr2` attempt) before `addStatement`'s `filterIterations` refused them silently with no canonical substitute (36.5k code-28 refusals). [D-301](#d-301) canonicalized only the status-3 channel, only the special tiers, at the drain. An earlier door-side attempt (, 2026-08-27) canonicalized every non-goal deposit under the classes at its scope PLUS its ancestors, equalities included, and failed its gate: 11 shortcut theorems lost (equality-head goals starved; `_orint_` seeds rewritten under a branch scope name embedding the raw disjunct; the recursion hypothesis rewritten away from `recursionHypothesisId`), a `buildStack: no origin found` abort on a bridge whose raw form had no producer line, two `origin chain termination` failures.
- **Decision (maintainer, 2026-08-28).** (1) The deposit door `addExprToMemoryBlock` rewrites every deposit except a goal (status 2) and the two equality shapes to its class-canonical form using the equivalence classes at the deposit's OWN scope only (`canonicalFormAtScope`: the scope's bucket, chooser `chooseCanonicalId` — normal > `int_` > `it_`, weak skipped; special tiers from the token scan, normal names from `collectExprTokens`; anchors stay raw by [I-53](30_invariants.md#i-53)). Rule carriers, negated compact existences and or compacts are NOT exempt. (2) Only canonical forms are admitted: a changed deposit whose canonical form is known at the scope or a strict ancestor ends at the door (plain presence — a known canonical form that was not disintegrated means the raw one would not be either; retrospective admission disintegrates parked compounds independently of this loop), releasing both ids for the or-cohort resolution signal. (3) Otherwise the canonical text proceeds: the raw text keeps its producer line (asserted present under `trackHistory`) and, for a local status, ships it to `mailOut` (the [D-286](#d-286) ship); the canonical form gets one `equality1` bridge when it has no origin row (I-34); the level run gains the applied pairs' class levels. (4) The absorb drain offers every arrival raw and stages the status-3 row from the door's returned id; `canonicalizeMailArrival` is deleted (one canonicalizer, one walk core — `forEachNonCanonicalMemberTokenCore`, with the registry filter as its `firstSpecialMemberId` instance). (5) `applyEquiClasses` keeps multiplying the registered canonical form; goal closure stays literal and still happens from the product in the same `standardProcessing` call. (6) Levels on the skip: no union, no fallback (the 2026-08-27 ruling — a known canonical form with fewer levels means the lemma was over-premised; such a pool row is a formulation finding proposed to the maintainer, never a level widening). (7) A rewrite flips the deposit to a local derivation (maintainer, 2026-08-28: "a rewrite to canonical should flip status and create all origin lines as if it is equality1"): the canonical form registers LOCAL iff at least one applied equality is a local statement of this LB (`appliedEqualityIsLocal`; the maintainer's refinement: "if one applied equality is local the canonical result is local" — a rewrite licensed only by mailed equalities keeps the arrival's locality), the raw form's producer line ships to `mailOut` whenever the row is local, and a status-3 arrival is staged as an external row only when it stayed non-local. Without it the first landing lost eight shortcut theorems — trap-proven at the induction zero block of `in[9] ∧ in[10] ∧!(9 ≤ 10) → 10 ≤ 9`: the mailed `0 ≤ 9` canonicalized onto the goal's literal text `(preorder[1,4,10,9])` as a NON-LOCAL row, the main-goal discharge (local delta only) never saw it, and the local derivation was Site-F-refused; every other loss (the trichotomy and totality or theorems, five order / cancellation lemmas) cascaded from that row. (8) The three over-premised shortcut pool rows (`in[v,N]` on the two `v1·v2 = 1` lemmas, `v1 | v2` on the divisibility antisymmetry row) were reformulated on the maintainer's instruction after landing as `proved not broadcast`; all three prove first-class afterwards.
- **Rejected.** Own scope plus ancestors (the failed attempt's rule; the seeds' scope names and the recursion identity are minted from the raw spelling, and a fresh scope's bucket is empty until an equality is admitted there, [D-44](#d-44)); canonicalizing equalities (goal closure is literal, neither shape is multiplied — an equality-head theorem would never close; the second trial's ruling); skipping only on a `fullyDisintegrated` canonical row (parity with [D-108](#d-108), fewer variants caught — rejected by the maintainer for the presence rule); cherry-picking the failed branches' code or their reformulated pool rows (the maintainer's rule: write fresh on `main`'s cores; pool edits only on the gate's finding and explicit consent).
- **Behavioural differences accepted.** A raw spelling is no longer registered next to its canonical form (Site F on the raw text, then the canonical skip); the raw mail text is now interned in the receiver's NameMap (Site F needs its id) and the drain's pre-door `encodeExpression` is gone — NameMap mint order changes under the maintainer's byte-identity waiver (deload id values only); `intExternalStatements` holds the door's canonical row; `kindById_` gains lazy fills from the door's normal-token probes (deload-observable, proof-invisible); over-premised pool lemmas land as `proved not broadcast` by design.
- **Measured.** Shortcut leg against a fresh `main` worktree built and run on this checkout's pipeline state and pool: 39 proven / 65 theorem rows on both sides, one pre-existing or-operand-order deviation; verifier 0 failures; prover 180 s vs 210 s (the first landing without the locality flip: 34 proven, 51 s — the search was starved, not faster). Full leg: recorded in the landing commit.
- **Contract.** [I-217](30_invariants.md#i-217); I-203 retired; [I-64](30_invariants.md#i-64) gains the door's raw-line ship as a sanctioned direct `mailOut` history writer; [I-205](30_invariants.md#i-205)'s entry half now reads the door's returned row.
<a id="d-319"></a>
## D-319 — CUDA growth streams canonical fixed attempt windows through cheap gates, stable compaction, and exact map probes (2026-08-29,, maintainer-approved)


- **Context.** The complete census measured 4,498,333,440 candidate attempts and single-depth peaks above 200 million, but only 2,082,812,196 attempts survived the map-independent gates. Full-depth candidate or survivor arrays were therefore outside the approved fixed-memory shape. After pooled prefixes, the short and cooperative growth kernels still owned 5.755711392 seconds, or 90.13 percent of kernel time.
- **Decision.** Stable radix passes order each live frontier by original call, run, statement path, and candidate. Exact scanned attempt spans form one canonical ordinal space. Consecutive windows of at most 16,777,216 records cover that space without gaps or overlap. Separate short-thread and 64-lane cooperative kernels write one compact attempt plus one flag for every ordinal, stable CUB selection compacts cheap-gate survivors, and a suffix-only kernel performs normalized subkey, owner, whole-key, and term probes before bounded event and child emission. All arrays allocate once; every capacity asserts; physical append order remains non-semantic because downstream tokens reconstruct canonical order.
- **Why.** Windows retain complete candidate coverage while bounding materialized attempts to 256 MiB and survivor indices to 64 MiB. Stable ordinal compaction removes map work for every cheap-gate rejection without making the chosen window size observable.
- **Rejected.** One allocation for a complete depth; truncating at the window boundary; dynamic or unified-memory growth; unordered atomic survivor queues; processing only the first window; processor replay; and using physical event or child arrival as proof order.
- **Measured.** A direct four-record fixture crosses both a ten-attempt and nine-attempt depth and matches the observation route. The clean production route passed all 1,559 tests, 9,994 verifier checks with zero failures, and all 311 artifact hashes. Growth ownership is 812,965,447 bytes and complete fixed device ownership is 1,275,332,748 bytes. Complete Phase 2 improved from 9.42072 to 8.54877 seconds; exact device work is 5.72042443 seconds. The post-change Systems profile attributes 4.098578580 seconds to survivor probes, cooperative cheap gates, prefix preparation, and short cheap gates together, so this milestone is exact and faster but does not yet satisfy the final two-times gate.
- **Contract.** [I-214](30_invariants.md#i-214); [I-213](30_invariants.md#i-213); [I-212](30_invariants.md#i-212); [I-211](30_invariants.md#i-211); [`09d_gpu_cookbook.md`](20_core_concepts/09d_gpu_cookbook.md); [`docs/GPU/gpu_rt2_plan.md`](../GPU/gpu_rt2_plan.md).

<a id="d-318"></a>
## D-318 — CUDA growth builds one measured pooled prefix per live node and selects short and long work in stable frontier order (2026-08-29,, maintainer-approved)


- **Context.** After exact filter-class sharing, the short and cooperative growth kernels jointly owned 5.755711392 seconds, or 90.13 percent of all kernel time. Both reconstructed the same normalized prefix and gate summaries while scanning candidate positions. A complete observation-only census measured simultaneous maxima of 14,074,478 payload values, 4,369,164 normalization variables, and 951,515 secondary variables across one live frontier.
- **Decision.** A preparation kernel builds one 32-byte `DeviceGrowthPrefix` header per live node plus exact slices in three fixed global pools. The retained capacities add 25 percent headroom and round upward to 262,144-value blocks: 17,825,792 payload values, 5,505,024 normalization variables, and 1,310,720 secondary variables. The header stores the three offsets and bounded lengths plus hypothesis, scope, and mandatory-term summaries. Two fixed flag arrays and stable CUB selection produce ascending original-frontier indices for the short and cooperative kernels. Those kernels read the same immutable prefix and fold only the appended expression suffix. Pool placement order is never a semantic or ordering key; every pool and selection boundary asserts.
- **Why.** Prefix work belongs to a node, not to each candidate lane. Sharing one measured node-level representation removes duplicate reconstruction without widening the 56-byte frontier record, while stable selection preserves the established physical frontier traversal at the boundary to existing atomic ledgers.
- **Rejected.** Inline maximum-size prefixes in every frontier row; rebuilding a prefix independently in each candidate kernel; dynamically sized or unified-memory pools; truncation or processor replay on overflow; and atomic-arrival short/long index compaction. The first atomic compaction run matched every reported semantic count through 40 GPU passes but later stopped at `removeOwnerFromRun`; stable frontier-index selection passed the complete route.
- **Measured.** The retained route passed all 1,559 native tests, 9,994 verifier checks with zero failures, and all 311 artifact hashes. The observed live maxima exactly repeated the sizing census. Growth ownership is 405,840,199 bytes and complete fixed device ownership is 868,207,500 bytes. Complete Phase 2 measured 9.42072 seconds, 0.01974 seconds slower than the accepted 9.40098-second filter-class run; this slice is a correctness prerequisite for bounded candidate windows, not an independent speed gain.
- **Contract.** [I-213](30_invariants.md#i-213); [I-212](30_invariants.md#i-212); [I-211](30_invariants.md#i-211); [`09d_gpu_cookbook.md`](20_core_concepts/09d_gpu_cookbook.md); [`docs/GPU/gpu_rt2_plan.md`](../GPU/gpu_rt2_plan.md).

<a id="d-317"></a>
## D-317 — exact duplicate Phase 2 filter calls share one CUDA predicate-and-compact span while every original call ordinal remains distinct (2026-08-29,, maintainer-approved)


- **Context.** The retained CUDA route counted and emitted the same statement rows independently for every processor-order filter call. An exact live census over the approved five-field signature found 24,229 calls but only 8,853 classes: duplicate calls caused 81,440,131 of 89,618,957 examined rows, or 90.874 percent. Filtering owned 1.813 seconds of the 10.0993-second control, so this was the first production slice of the approved bounded signature-and-candidate redesign.
- **Decision.** `Phase2FilterScheduleArena` interns the exact tuple `(logical block, memory kind, iteration ceiling, whole-key widening, statement count)` in a fixed open-address table, preserves first-occurrence class order, and stores one class index for every original call. `CudaPhase2FilterSortBuffer` uploads both columns, runs count, exclusive scan, stable compact emission, and radix sorting once per class, then expands the class count and offset back to every original call. The retained sort key is `(class ordinal, decoded-name rank, statement index)`. Growth reads only the low statement-index field from that shared class span; every event, growth position, duplicate-removal boundary, and final ordering token still carries the original processor call ordinal.
- **Why.** Exact calls have identical frozen inputs and therefore identical first-8,192 stable filter results. Sharing the immutable result span removes predicate replay without coalescing the semantically distinct generator-call sequence.
- **Rejected.** Hash-only class equality; merging original call ordinals; copying a compact row list once per duplicate call; a host-computed semantic verdict; dynamically growing class or mapping storage; and a processor fallback when a capacity or identity contract fails.
- **Measured.** The production route reduced retained filter rows from 8,815,888 per-call rows to 827,746 class rows. Complete Phase 2 fell from 10.0993 to 9.40098 seconds, the device route from 7.3168369 to 6.5884318 seconds, and the enclosing route from 9.4220125 to 8.7148406 seconds. The run retained 19,194,381 accepted events, 841,301 unique requests, 9,994 verifier checks with zero failures, and all 311 artifact hashes exactly. Fixed filter ownership grew by 65,536 bytes for the original-to-class map; complete fixed device ownership is 729,788,029 bytes.
- **Contract.** [I-212](30_invariants.md#i-212); [I-211](30_invariants.md#i-211); [`09d_gpu_cookbook.md`](20_core_concepts/09d_gpu_cookbook.md); [`docs/GPU/gpu_rt2_plan.md`](../GPU/gpu_rt2_plan.md).

<a id="d-314"></a>
## D-314 — evaluation-only projection columns transfer from fixed pinned staging while the host builds the Phase 2 schedule (2026-08-29,, maintainer-directed)

- **Context.** Eight projection shards reached 9.9825 seconds, only 0.0649 seconds above the strict historical two-times gate. Twelve shards saturated. The retained CUDA profile measured about 0.38 seconds of host-to-device traffic, while the filter, growth, and ordering kernels read only fifteen of the projection's twenty-four columns. The remaining nine columns first become necessary at evaluation.
- **Decision.** `CudaPhase2ProjectionBuffer` owns a nonblocking CUDA stream and 31,219,712 bytes of fixed page-locked staging for rule-string records/bytes, reverse-map views/entries/slots/key bytes/owners, plain-data run values, and metadata bytes. `beginPhase2Upload` copies the fifteen early columns synchronously, copies the nine evaluation-only used prefixes into staging, and queues those nine transfers. The prover starts this operation immediately after projection and builds the task/filter/growth schedules while it is pending. After the small task upload, `finishPhase2Upload` joins the stream before filter, so every kernel still sees all twenty-four exact used prefixes. The ordinary `upload` door remains a begin-plus-finish wrapper, and the all-column checksum twin covers both doors. Fixed device ownership stays 729,721,629 bytes; this step stages dependencies but does not yet reduce transferred bytes.
- **Why.** Dependency staging overlaps transfer with host scheduling without changing device residency, kernel inputs, proof decisions, or observable order. Dedicated staging keeps the projection builders on ordinary pageable memory; registering their live vector allocations slowed later projection passes. Joining before the first kernel prevents copy-engine traffic from competing with growth.
- **Rejected.** Page-locking the live projection vectors; overlapping projection copies with semantic kernels; omitting columns merely because one current kernel does not read them; unified memory; dynamic host/device allocation; a processor fallback; cross-process persistence for the current disjoint-pass shortcut.
- **Measured.** The live-vector/kernel-overlap experiment remained exact but regressed complete Phase 2 from 10.1734 to 10.8707 seconds. Fixed staging plus schedule overlap then measured 9.74343 and 9.46378 seconds in consecutive complete CUDA shortcuts. These are 2.036 and 2.096 times faster than the strict 19.835229-second historical reference, and 2.073 and 2.134 times faster than the fresh 20.1945325-second control. Both runs retained 9,994 checks with zero failures and all 311 paths, lengths, and SHA-256 hashes byte-identical to the control. The accepted build passes all 1,558 native tests.
- **Contract.** [D-313](#d-313); [I-211](30_invariants.md#i-211); [`09d_gpu_cookbook.md`](20_core_concepts/09d_gpu_cookbook.md); [`docs/GPU/gpu_rt1_plan.md`](../GPU/gpu_rt1_plan.md).

<a id="d-315"></a>
## D-315 — long CUDA frontier spans distribute candidate positions across one block while short spans retain one thread per node (2026-08-29,, maintainer-directed)

- **Context.** The landed Phase 2 CUDA route assigned one thread to each compact `DeviceGrowthNode`. Prefix hoisting reduced complete CUDA Phase 2 to about 20 seconds, but the exact growth kernel still owned about 13 seconds and each node scanned every later filtered position serially. A complete observation-only census on the RTX 4070 Laptop GPU counted 18,940,682 live nodes and 4,498,333,440 candidate attempts. Spans of at least 256 positions contained 68.7134% of attempts across 35.0923% of nodes; transfers were only about 0.5 seconds and the two shortcut passes had disjoint logical-block sets.
- **Decision.** Keep the 56-byte frontier node and the existing one-thread path for spans below a measured cutoff. A warp-compacted, frontier-bounded index list names long nodes. After its used count is read, one CUDA block owns each long node: thread zero builds the normalized prefix and request-gate summaries once in shared memory, 128 lanes scan disjoint candidate positions, and a segmented byte-map reader hashes and compares the canonical header, shared prefix, and lane-local appended-expression suffix without copying the prefix into every lane. Production initially uses a 256-position cutoff and disables census collection; tests use a lower explicit cutoff to exercise both routes. Both kernels append to the existing bounded event/frontier ledgers, whose atomic order stays non-semantic until the existing canonical reconstruction.
- **Why.** Candidate work, not transfers, was the measured bottleneck. The adaptive split gives the long serial spans candidate parallelism without inflating both million-row frontiers with normalized payloads or wasting a full block on the short tail. A fixed list preserves process-owned startup allocation and makes overflow an assert.
- **Rejected.** A full normalized-key payload per frontier node; copying the shared prefix into every lane's local stack; one block for every node including short spans; unified memory or dynamic device allocation; selective upload as the first optimization; processor reconstruction or fallback.
- **Measured.** The first cutoff-256 route reduced fresh complete CUDA Phase 2 from 20.1945325 to 15.1108074 seconds and exact device time from 15.2917872 to 10.1747262 seconds. Census plus kernel attribution then selected cutoff 64 with 64 lanes: complete Phase 2 is 12.4757739 seconds, exact device time 7.5260573, prover 116.023, and overall 120.89349; the compacted-node peak is 552,505. The verifier reports 9,994 checks with zero failures and all 311 retained artifacts are byte-identical at both milestones. Native `sm_89` resource use is 53 registers, 1,280 stack bytes per lane, and 2,016 shared bytes per cooperative block. The cutoff-64 kernel reaches 65.57% occupancy, 46.72% compute, 2.11% DRAM, and 99.90% L2 hits. This is a retained intermediate, not the campaign's two-times completion gate.
- **Contract.** [D-313](#d-313); [I-211](30_invariants.md#i-211); [`09d_gpu_cookbook.md`](20_core_concepts/09d_gpu_cookbook.md); [`docs/GPU/gpu_rt1_plan.md`](../GPU/gpu_rt1_plan.md).

<a id="d-316"></a>
## D-316 — independent logical blocks build fixed host projection shards in parallel and merge by exact offset rebasing (2026-08-29,, maintainer-directed)

- **Context.** After adaptive growth, host construction of the 24-column pointer-free projection consumed 3.9306738 of 12.4757739 Phase 2 seconds. Transfers consumed only 0.376 seconds, and the shortcut has no in-process projection-reuse hits, so residency or dirty upload could not close the measured seam.
- **Decision.** Twelve process-owned `Phase2ProjectionArena` shards claim logical blocks through the existing steward window and build each block independently. `Phase2ProjectionArena::appendShard` bulk-copies every used column prefix into the upload arena and rebases descriptor offsets, name/rule bytes, all byte/reverse/plain-data view and entry offsets, open-addressed slot indices, blob records, reverse owners, runs, mandatory keys, and metadata. The caller then restores descriptor order by original projection index. Physical slices may follow worker ownership, but the descriptor order consumed by tasks and sealing is canonical. Every arena reserves the established global ceilings at process startup; an overrun asserts and no hot append reallocates.
- **Why.** Logical-block projection reads frozen block/analyzer state and writes disjoint arenas. Keeping the established serial builder inside each shard minimizes semantic change, while one directly twinned merge door proves every pointer-free reference instead of duplicating the 700-line builder as indexed writes.
- **Measured.** The four-shard route reduced projection to 1.6821862 seconds and complete Phase 2 to 10.6506 seconds. Eight shards then reached 1.3315546 seconds projection and 9.9825 seconds complete Phase 2, a 2.023-times acceleration over the fresh 20.1945325-second control but 0.0649 seconds above the stricter historical 9.917614-second gate. Twelve shards lowered projection only to 1.3033454 seconds, raised merge to 0.4433709, and measured 10.1734 seconds complete Phase 2; host shard scaling is therefore saturated. The direct all-column merge twin passes inside 1,558/1,558 unit tests; every full verifier reports 9,994 checks with zero failures, and all 311 paths, lengths, and SHA-256 hashes are byte-identical at all three milestones. The next measured seam is route traffic rather than more host arenas.
- **Contract.** [D-313](#d-313); [I-211](30_invariants.md#i-211); [`09d_gpu_cookbook.md`](20_core_concepts/09d_gpu_cookbook.md); [`docs/GPU/gpu_rt1_plan.md`](../GPU/gpu_rt1_plan.md).

<a id="d-313"></a>
## D-313 — FTA shortcut Phase 2 has explicit processor and CUDA backends; CUDA owns semantic request work after stump discovery and never falls back (2026-08-28,, maintainer-approved)

- **Context.** Phase 2 request generation and evaluation are branch-heavy, provenance-bearing, and order-sensitive, but the statified MPU 0.1 shape exposes fixed-capacity pointer-free projections, split work items, and a canonical firing-record boundary. The maintainer requested an initial FTA shortcut port that keeps the processor path selectable, retains provenance, and can be evaluated after implementation.
- **Decision.** `main.py --shortcut --phase2-backend cpu|cuda` selects the route explicitly; processor is the default and CUDA is rejected outside shortcut mode. A split logical block still runs the processor stump producer to discover its disjoint expression branches. After that boundary the CUDA route owns projection, batch filtering, normalized-key frontier growth, request ordering and deduplication, evaluation, generated expressions, provenance, marker payloads, canonical firing-record order, doom-prefix reduction, and exact per-task submatch counts. The host downloads bounded used prefixes, seals the already-decided records, and passes them through the same `applyFiringRecords` deposit door. Device, capacity, launch, and contract failures assert; none invokes the processor evaluator.
- **Why.** The parallel processor oracle remains available for exact A/B testing while the CUDA implementation can exploit bulk independent work without weakening proof history or exposing host pointers. Keeping the final deposit door common makes every observable order and provenance effect comparable at one boundary.
- **Rejected.** Automatic processor fallback after a CUDA failure; processor re-evaluation to reconstruct provenance; theorem-only device output; using whole-prover time as a Phase 2 measurement; changing the three-phase barrier model.
- **Measured.** The first complete CUDA shortcut executed 48 device passes, passed 10,038 proof-graph checks with zero failures, and produced all 311 retained artifacts byte-identically to the processor baseline. The first whole-prover and overall totals were slower; the performance gate now measures the complete Phase 2 scheduler window explicitly and keeps end-to-end shortcut time as the usefulness gate.
- **Contract.** [I-211](30_invariants.md#i-211); [`09d_gpu_cookbook.md`](20_core_concepts/09d_gpu_cookbook.md); [`docs/GPU/gpu_plan.md`](../GPU/gpu_plan.md).

<a id="d-312"></a>
## D-312 — only the canonical form of a compact implication enters hash memory; the request-generation indexes and the originals chains carry full owner lists so a rule's removal is exact; removal re-enumerates the install's own keys (2026-08-28, authored, maintainer-directed)

- - **Context.** Compact implications (`(implication<N>[args])`, [D-309](#d-309) / [D-310](#d-310)) are statements: registered, mailed, multiplied by `applyEquiClasses`, and expanded into hash-memory rules by `addExprToMemoryBlock`. Nothing kept the RULES canonical: a compact expanded before its arguments joined an equivalence class kept firing under stale names, every raw variant that arrived by mail was expanded too, and the end-of-burst `sanitizeHashMemory` ([D-69](#d-69) — `it_/int_`-only, expanded-text keyed, whole-map scans) was inert in practice. Removing a rule exactly was impossible: the whole-key set, the subkey map and the remaining-args index carried no owner accounting ([D-302](#d-302) / [D-303](#d-303)), and `eradicateImplicationFromLB` scanned every `encodedMap` and every chain to find what to drop.
- **Decision (maintainer, plan approved 2026-08-28).** (1) Compacts stay multiplied as statements (hash fodder), but **only the canonical form of a compact is ever added to hash memory**: a `compactCanonicalAt` / `canonicalizeCompact` predicate over the classes visible at the compact's scope, a shared reconcile step `ensureCanonicalExpansion` (K non-canonical and expanded → remove K's rules; K* not expanded → expand K* with an `equality1` row citing K and the fired pairs), run at two sites — the door (`addExprToMemoryBlock`: a non-canonical arrival registers as a statement and expands its canonical form at once if hash memory lacks it) and a new `applyEquiClasses` hook `applyEquivalenceClassToCompactImplications` (a class that formed or grew later removes the stale rules and installs the canonical ones in the same round). (2) **Full owner lists**: every entry of `normalizedEncodedKeys`, `normalizedEncodedSubkeys`, the new `remainingArgsOwners` edge map and `originals` carries the sorted-unique list of the rules that installed it (`RuleOwner` = packed `(originalImplicationId, validityId)`); a removal deletes one owner, an owner-less entry is erased once per apply per container (`eraseEmptyRuns`). Under `allow_multiplication` the owner an entry carries is the multiplication COPY, and two rules can multiply into one copy text (found by the full leg on IncubatorGauss1: heads `(preorder[u_1,u_4,1,u_2])` / `(preorder[u_1,u_4,u_2,1])` both become `(preorder[u_1,u_4,u_2,u_2])` under 1→u_2), so the same principle is applied one level up: `copyOwners` lists the rules per copy, a removal delists the rule and a copy leaves hash memory only with its last rule. Reference counts were rejected: they are exact only if install and removal enumerate identically and cannot say which rule a stale entry belongs to; the list asserts it. The D1-flood storage [D-302](#d-302) / [D-303](#d-303) avoided (thousands of owners under one short subkey) is accepted for exact removal. (3) **Re-enumeration**: removal finds a rule's keys by running the install's own key enumeration (`addToHashMemory` / `makeNormalizedKeysForAdmission` under a remove policy) — no stored back-map; the owner-presence assert on every visited entry is the tripwire that the derivative-key qualification reads only the rule text, the operator config and the compiled registry (verified by reading `ordisRouteQualifies`, `ordis2DemandSlotQualifies`, `inputSlotDemandSlotQualifies`, `implicationIsQualified`). (4) The `encodedMap` LMVs of removed rules are dropped by one batched compaction per instance per apply (a set-predicate twin of `eradicateEncodedMapForImpl`), never per key. (5) `sanitizeHashMemory`, `eradicateImplicationFromLB`, `chainStillReferencedCold` and `expandedImplications` retire; a per-LB carrier index `compactExpansions` (compact → its expanded texts and install kind) replaces the last.
- **Landing.** Step by step on the branch: (1) the owner lists (`RuleOwnerRec`, `addOwnerToRun`, `addWholeKeyOwner`, `addShortSubkeyOwner`, `mergeSubkeySignatures` with the (owner, signature) pairs, `remArgsEdgeKeyInto`, `insertRemainingArgsNormKeyBatch` with the edge owners, `originals` as an owner-run map; install behaviour otherwise unchanged); (2) the remove policy (`RuleIndexOp` on the shared enumeration, `removeOwnerFromRun` / `removeWholeKeyOwner` / `removeSubkeyOwner` / `removeRemainingArgsOwner` + `ReverseArgsIndex::removeEdge`, `decomposeImplicationForInstall` shared with the door, `removeRuleFromHashMemory` — the drop set staged by the enumeration copy by copy through `RuleIndexOp::dropSet`, found by the full leg: a multiplied rule installs one text per surviving partition and a multiplication that emits no copy installs nothing ([G-69](50_gotchas.md#g-69)) — `eradicateEncodedMapWhere` + `eraseOwnerlessEntries` = `finishRuleRemovals`; no production caller yet); (3) the carrier index `Memory::compactExpansions` (tags 816..819; `appendCompactExpansion` at the install door beside the `expandedImplications` mint, `removeCompactExpansion` over every instance still holding the rule, `finishCompactRemovals`; swept by `wipeSubtree`) — `expandedImplications` is KEPT as the hashburst dump's section source (Rule 14), the two are held in step; (4) the canonical gate at the rule-install loop (`installExpandedImplication` = the door's per-implication body; `isCompactImplicationSpan`, `canonicalizeCompact`, `compactExpandedHere`, `expandCanonicalCompact`); (5) the hook `applyEquivalenceClassToCompactImplications` in both `applyEquiClasses` passes with `finishCompactRemovals` after the fixpoint; `sanitizeHashMemory` / `eradicateImplicationFromLB` / `PendingSanRec` / `SanPairRec` deleted (I-46 retired, I-141's hash-memory half retired).
- **Behavioural differences accepted.** Rule installs mint the copy text into `ruleInterner` before the chain ids (ids never sorted by, I-84); the four owner-run maps add per-LB memory (measured in the landing commits); the hashburst dump stays byte-identical (owner lists are never printed); theorems and the verifier verdict are the gate.
- **Measured.** Gate on the main-tip baseline, same machine: full leg (`main.py`, every batch) 778 s wall vs 806 s, 63 theorems identical, verifier 16247 checks / 0 failures (baseline 16137 / 0 — check-count deltas are not a theorem signal); shortcut leg 64 theorems identical, prover 205–231 s across the landing chains vs 291.7 s; 1541 unit tests. The three full-leg defects (a zero-copy multiplication, the per-owner visited set, a copy shared by two rules) surfaced only on the `allow_multiplication` batches (IncubatorPeano2, IncubatorGauss1) — the shortcut leg never removes a multiplied rule. Per batch (prover seconds, baseline → landing): IncubatorPeano1 140.1 → 115.1, IncubatorPeano2 11.8 → 14.0, Peano 66.5 → 56.9, IncubatorGauss1 61.8 → 91.3, IncubatorGauss2 13.3 → 25.8, IncubatorGauss3 114.6 → 102.5, Gauss 172.2 → 162.5 (sum 580 → 568). The two `allow_multiplication` Gauss batches are slower — an OPEN RT question (the per-copy owner writes on three instances, or hook removals that now actually run there); not yet measured to the leaf.
- **Contract.** [I-210](30_invariants.md#i-210); [I-49](30_invariants.md#i-49) (revised), [I-100](30_invariants.md#i-100) (revised), [I-154](30_invariants.md#i-154) (revised); I-46 retired.

<a id="d-311"></a>
## D-311 — `ordisMerge`'s convergence ships every branch derivation's history to `mailOut` before the per-branch removal erases the branch rows from the per-step delta (2026-08-27, )

- - **Context.** `fillMailOut` ships origin rows only for statements that are still in `intLocalEncodedStatementsDelta` when it runs ([I-64](30_invariants.md#i-64)). `ordisMerge`'s convergence step 2 removes the converged expression from every branch scope with `removeExpressionFromMemoryBlock(state=0)`, which erases those branch rows from the delta. A cohort releases its branches one at a time ([I-174](30_invariants.md#i-174)), so the LAST branch always converges in the very step it derives the expression — its `equality1` row is written, then its delta row is erased, and the mail pass never sees it, while the `or convergence` row citing it (a same-iteration deposit at the parent scope) does ship. The earlier branch's row shipped in the burst it derived, so a descendant that walks the mailed convergence row resolves the first branch and fails on the last one: `buildStack: no origin found`. Trap-proven on IncubatorGauss3 — producer `(EnumerationSet2[2,6,10])`, cohort `(or2[2,repl_lev_1_1,6])`, all 96 converged `(preorder[…])` rows, walker = the contradiction child `__contradiction__(interval[1,4,2,7,10])`; the child's own `orBookkeeping` was empty at every burst and every trap on its local writers stayed silent, so the rows could only have come by mail. The producer's own map held the origin all along (the producer's own chapter would export). Latent since the convergence removal existed; exposed here because the existence-implication compacts (D-310) changed the child's derivation path so that its export walks this parent history.
- **Decision.** Ship first, drop second — the [D-286](#d-286) contract applied to the second delta-dropping site: before each `removeExpressionFromMemoryBlock` in step 2, `ordisMerge` calls `copyOriginRowsToMailOut(addExpression, branchValidity)`. History-only; no proof-flow change; a sanctioned [I-64](30_invariants.md#i-64) writer.
- **Rejected.** (a) A per-step origin delta walked by `fillMailOut` instead of the statement delta — systematic, but bookkeeping at every `addOrigin` site (rejected once already under [D-92](#d-92)). (b) Keeping the delta row through the removal — the delta also feeds request generation and the equi-class waterline repair, a semantics change for a provenance bug.
- **Behavioural differences accepted.** Descendants' origin maps gain the branch-derivation rows of every converged cohort (more `equality1` rows in mail); artifacts that already resolved are unchanged, the IncubatorGauss3 export resolves.
- **Measured.** Recorded in the landing commit.
- **Contract.** [I-64](30_invariants.md#i-64) (amended writer list), [I-26](30_invariants.md#i-26); gotcha [G-67](50_gotchas.md#g-67).

<a id="d-310"></a>
## D-310 — an existence's two negation rules (`left → !right`, `right → !left`) are compiled once as `(implication<N>[u_…])` compacts on the existence's registry entry, and negated-existence disintegration emits those compacts as product statements that expand into the rules (2026-08-27, authored, maintainer-directed)

- - **Context.** `disintegrateExprCore2`'s negated-existence block built the two rules `left → !right` and `right → !left` as expanded full-bind text on the spot (the bound variable replaced by a fresh `startInt` integer) and inserted them straight into hash memory. The rules had no compact identity, so nothing could rewrite them the way equivalence classes rewrite statements. The maintainer's design: mirror [D-309](#d-309) literally — the rules live as compacts on the existence's binary entry and the disintegrator instantiates them.
- **The choice.** `LogicalEntity::implications` now serves existence entities too. `compileExistenceImplications` — called at the `!(>` mint in `compileCoreExpressionMapCore` (registry-reuse and fresh-mint branch alike; the `preMintReducedOrs` seam completes an existence loaded from a binary written before the field and asserts every other two-element existence complete) — builds each rule with `reconstructImplicationFullBind` over the registry elements (head negated with double-negation cancellation, I-175), renames the bound variable through `renameLastRemoved` — the registry stores it as `1`, the very token `compileImplicationToCompact`'s `u_` strip produces from `u_1`; without the rename the bound variable and the first token merge and the compact loses an argument — and compiles it through `compileImplicationToCompact` + `prefixArgumentsWithU`; `expectedExistenceImplicationCount` (2 for the `[left, right]` shape, 0 otherwise) is the shared completeness formula. The disintegrator resolves the inner existence through the registry (`compiledEntity` on the inner core, category `existence`, two elements) — never through the prepared instruction, which `prepareIntegrationCore`'s polarity guard leaves empty for a negated compound — and substitutes `u_p → instance argument p` positionally into each compact, inserts it as a child statement of the negated existence, stamps it with the `expansion` origin the rule used to carry (citing the negated existence; paired `mailOut` write per D-274) and hands it to `prepareIntegrationCore` + `disintegrateExprCore2`, whose implication branch expands it into the rule and records rule ← `expansion` ← compact. No `startInt` is consumed there any more: the rule's bound variable is the registry placeholder, exactly as for every mailed theorem compact (`renamingChain` remaps a changeable that overlaps a `u_` name).
- **Finding on the way.** The former block's recognizer probed the prepared instruction for the positive existence; since (2026-08-04, the polarity guard) that instruction is empty for every negated compound, so the block was unreachable: a trapped full run showed 19 negated existences admitted to disintegration (all Peano, all `!(existence3[…])`), every one with an empty instruction, the block firing 0 times, and no `A → !B` rule anywhere in hash memory — unnoticed because the only artifact consumer (the chapter of `¬∃m(m+1=n) → n=0`) closes by direct contradiction against the derived positive existence. See [G-68](50_gotchas.md#G-68).
- **Rejected.** Carrying the bound variable as a compact argument filled with a fresh integer at instantiation — the compact would be a statement about one specific value while its expansion binds it universally, an unsound expansion step. Extending `prepareIntegrationCore`'s `pi_lev_` minting to implication entities — changes every mailed compact's expansion, out of scope.
- **Behavioural differences accepted.** Chapters gain one `expansion` row per rule (compact ← negated existence, rule ← compact); the rule's bound variable is the registry placeholder instead of a fresh integer and the `startInt` sequence shifts; `implication<N>` numbering shifts (two entities per existence, minted at the existence's mint); verifier check counts rise; the compacts are registered statements — mailed at main, installed at descendants, rewritten by `applyEquiClasses`. Gate = `theorems.txt` against the `main` baseline, verifier 0 failures.
- **Verifier (I-16, maintainer consent via the approved plan).** `check_expansion`'s negated-existence branch expands a compact row through `_expand_implication_compact` before the two shape comparisons; the rule row (rule ← compact) already passes the general implication case.
- **Measured.** Recorded in the landing commits.
- **Contract.** [I-209](30_invariants.md#i-209).

<a id="d-309"></a>
## D-309 — an or's K mutual-exclusion and subset-exclusion rules are compiled once as `(implication<N>[u_…])` compacts on the or's registry entry, and or disintegration emits those compacts as product statements that expand into the rules (2026-08-27, authored, maintainer-directed)

- - **Context.** `consumeOrLeavesCohort` built every K rule and subset-exclusion rule as expanded full-bind text on the spot, per or instance and per burst. The rules had no compact identity, so nothing could rewrite them the way equivalence classes rewrite statements. The maintainer's design: the rules live as compacts on the or's binary entry and the disintegrator instantiates them.
- **Decision (maintainer, plan approved).** (1) `LogicalEntity::implications` — the K-rules in leaf order, then the subset-exclusion rules in the disintegrator's `sel` order — written over the or's OWN `u_` tokens; each entry is an ordinary implication entity of the same binary, its argument order the projection from the implication's signature positions onto the or's tokens. Compiled through the mail-broadcast compaction door (`compileImplicationToCompact`: strip `u_`, `excludeRepetitions("implication")`, restore `u_`). K-rules at every or mint (`findOrMintOrOperator`; both `!(&` branches of `compileCoreExpressionMapCore`); subset-exclusion compacts in `preMintReducedOrs` after its closure walk — the reduced heads exist only then, and minting them eagerly at the or's mint would renumber `or<N>`. The binary writes the key only when non-empty; an or loaded without it is completed at the first seam (the constructor loads the binary before `coreExpressionMap` exists). (2) `consumeOrLeavesCohort` instantiates each compact positionally (`u_p` → instance argument p, repeated arguments legal) and hands it to `prepareIntegrationCore` + `disintegrateExprCore2` as a product statement — a child of the or's key: the compact registers at the parent scope (mailed at main, rewritten by `applyEquiClasses` like any statement — the maintainer's explicit choice), and the implication branch expands it into exactly the rule the on-the-spot construction produced. (3) Provenance: `compact ← disintegration ← expanded or`; `rule ← expansion ← compact`. The verifier's or branch expands a compact row through its binary entry before the K / subset-exclusion checks (I-16 consent given).
- **Out of scope (maintainer).** The negated-AND De-Morgan door (`!(op[args])`, body an AND) has no or entity and keeps the on-the-spot K rules. The only door firings in the current artifacts are `!(strictOrder[…])` heads — GL's own or written as `!(&…)`, not a compiled `(&` definition negated later; a compile-time or per and-entity would trip `kMaxReducedOrLeaves` (`NaturalNumbers` has 13 conjuncts) and renumber every `or<N>`. Revisit when a compiled `(&` definition is negated and disintegrated.
- **Behavioural differences accepted.** Chapters gain one `expansion` row per rule; verifier check counts rise; `implication<N>` numbering shifts for later mints; a dedup hit against an earlier-registered implication keeps that entity's first-seen premise order (I-52), as the mail round-trip already did; descendants receive the compacts by mail and install the rules; the compacts are equi-class-rewritten on this branch. Gate = `theorems.txt` against the `main` baseline, verifier 0 failures.
- **Measured.** Recorded in the landing commits.
- **Contract.** [I-208](30_invariants.md#i-208).

<a id="d-307"></a>
## D-307 — the two rejected-map equi-class hooks walk only the class validity's keys through a per-apply validity-bucket index and are skipped in a round that follows a round without drops; the rejected maps are asserted insert-free inside an apply (2026-08-26, authored, extracted onto, maintainer-directed)

- - **Context.** The IncubatorGauss3 phase-3 measurement (`.rt/burst_phases.log`, burst 6 of the `(EnumerationSet3[2,6,7,10])` LB, 72 s of a 77 s burst in phase 3): `applyEquiClasses` 63.7 s, of which `applyEquivalenceClassToRejectedMap` 31.9 s and `applyEquivalenceClassToRejectedMapIntegration` 27.7 s — 581 class-visits (407 delta, 174 Pass-2, over 18 fixpoint rounds), each decoding, interning and sorting the WHOLE map (57,555 / 58,094 keys) before skipping every key whose validity differed from the class validity. The statement loops took 3.4 s, rewrite enumeration + commit 0.9 s. The keys sat in 16 validities, 27,188 of 27,593 in four branch scopes.
- **Decision (maintainer, "Go").** Three bookkeeping changes, no semantics: (1) filter first, sort only the hits; (2) a transient `RejectedValidityBuckets` per map per `applyEquiClasses` call ([`memory.hpp`](../GL_Quick_VS/GL_Quick/src/memory.hpp)), built lazily at the first hook use from the packed `(templateId, validityId)` keys, plus per-argument postings `(validity, argument id) → keys` over the decoded flat templates — so a hook iterates only the keys at its validity that name one of the class's non-canonical members (a flat template changes under the substitution iff an argument IS such a member, `replaceKeysScratch`'s token-boundary contract; the substitution test re-checks every candidate); (3) the round skip — each hook returns its drop count, and a fixpoint round in which a map's hook dropped nothing is followed by a round in which every class that ran that hook skips it (delta entries pushed mid-round never ran and still run).
- **Why the order is preserved.** The former emission order was the whole-map (template, validity) lex sort restricted to the hits; within one validity that is the template lex order of the hits, which the new walk sorts explicitly (the `sameIterationInternalMail` channel is a canonical set anyway, so the sequence was never observable).
- **Why the skip is exact.** A hit needs a key at the class validity whose template changes under the class. Inside an apply the rejected maps never gain a key — hook drops and the admission hooks' revivals only erase, every insert rides mail absorbed outside the apply (I-37) — and the class snapshots are fixed, so a round without drops proves the next round hits nothing. `HashMap::insertEpoch` (bumped by `mint` on a miss, `resetToFresh`, `bulkLoad`) is asserted unchanged across every round and at every `ensureBuilt` — the Rule-19 tripwire for an unenumerated insert path.
- **Measured.** Burst 6 of the same LB, dump byte-identical: with the validity buckets alone the two hooks went 31.9 + 27.7 s → 16.5 + 11.8 s (the per-key substitution test over ~14 k same-validity keys per visit remained); the argument postings remove that walk — numbers in the commit that lands them.
- **Out of scope, recorded.** The other five hooks keep the whole-map walk (about 1 s at the same burst; same scaling law — the bucket index applies unchanged when they matter); I-37's drop-and-mail re-entry of the rewritten park is untouched; the closure-fact flood that grew the maps 8x in one burst is a separate, semantic question.
- **Contract.** [I-207](30_invariants.md#i-207).

<a id="d-308"></a>
## D-308 — the two rejected-map equi-class hooks re-key a park in place under the canonical key with an `equality1` row per rewritten product, and keep drop + mail only for a park whose rewritten product is demanded right now (2026-08-26, authored, extracted onto, maintainer-directed)

- - **Context.** Measured on IncubatorGauss3, main burst 6 (`.rt/burst_phases.log`, grid-wide over the six swept LBs; wall 45 s, phase 3 43 s): the two hooks dropped 44,735 + 45,236 of ~57k parks and mailed each rewritten compound; before each mail `resetResentExpressionRegistries` scanned the whole statement table (62,848 rows, 26k calls, 21.2 s), and the absorb re-disintegrated the 47,507 mailed compounds (22.8 s) only to park the same products again under the canonical names — 44 of the 56 CPU seconds of phase 3, nothing learned. The admission maps already re-keyed in place (D-106).
- **Decision (maintainer, "Go").** Every hit (a key at the class validity whose template changes under the class) is handled by one of two routes, decided per compound. *Not demanded:* re-key in place — key, renamed form, compound, concrete constituent and siblings rewritten with the same token-boundary substitution, levels = the parked run ∪ the fired pairs' levels (D-280; the integration record has no level run, its revival keeps looking the compound's levels up), inserted under K' through `updateRejectedMap` / `updateRejectedMapIntegration`, K erased, nothing mailed; for the product and each sibling whose text changed one `equality1` history row at the park scope (source = the pre-rewrite text at that scope, justifiers = the pairs that fired on it), into `exprOriginMap` and the mail-out origin column; `mutatedThisBurst` set. *Demanded right now:* the former drop + mail path (D-63 / D-64) for the whole compound, so the absorb's Pass B — caps, cascade to co-witnesses, `checkForEquivalence`, flag-5 relay — decides exactly as before.
- **Site-F parity.** Before re-keying, a park whose rewritten compound is already LOCAL at the park scope or KNOWN at a strict ancestor (`isLocalEncodedStatement`, `ancestorKnown` without self), or whose compound did not change, is dropped — exactly the fate the mail path gave it (the absorb's Site F refused the re-sent compound; an unchanged compound was never re-sent). Measured necessity: without it the Peano batch kept parks the old path dropped, revived them (old witness names next to the known compound's own products), phase 1 of burst 11 absorbed +40k statements and one LB's request-generation grow search (5,955 statements in its universe) never finished.
- **The demand probe.** The side-effect-free superset of Pass B's admission test on the rewritten key: algebra — a regular (non-ordis) admission entry under K' at the park scope or a strict ancestor (`lookupTemplateKey` + `admissionRunHasRegularValue`, the D-243 rendezvous probe, over owned scratch copies of `NameMap::strictAncestorSpans`), or `isAllowedAsOperatorInput` on the rewritten product with the marker-slot witness; integration — the bare K' in `admissionSetIntegration` or the `u_`-form K' in `admissionMapIntegration` at the park scope (what `isAdmittedIntegration` reads, without its inserts). A superset is enough: a product the probe calls demanded but Pass B refuses is re-parked under K' by the absorb.
- **Provenance.** `rewritten product ← equality1 ← pre-rewrite product ← disintegration ← compound`; `check_equality1` is syntactic and the pre-rewrite product's `disintegration` row is its foundation. The revival door's one-dependency self-source row is skipped by the chapter walker (a cycle) in favour of the complete row.
- **What changed around it.** The three `insertEpoch` asserts (round end of `applyEquiClasses`, `RejectedValidityBuckets::ensureBuilt`) are gone — inserts inside an apply are legal; the index stays a per-apply snapshot (K' visited at the next apply; a K' equal to a key dropped earlier in the apply is reached through that key's stale posting). I-37 revised; I-207 revised; D-106's "rejection keeps drop + mail" clause superseded for the undemanded case.
- **Behavioural differences accepted.** Proof state differs from the pre-change dump: a re-keyed park is revived by the next admission key gain instead of re-parked a burst later, and keeps its witness name (the mail path re-minted every witness at generation 0). Gate = full pipeline (`theorems.txt` against the `main` baseline, verifier 0 failures), not the dump.
- **Measured.** Recorded in the commit that lands the change and the follow-up burst-6 measurement.
- **Contract.** I-37, I-207.
