<a id="d-306"></a>
## D-306 — a resolved `_ordis_` branch FREEZES (its subtree leaves the request universe, nothing is erased); a goal-less LB opens, parks and releases no or branch (2026-08-25,, maintainer-directed)

- - **Context.** Under the sequenced release ([D-250](#d-250), [I-174](30_invariants.md#i-174)) a branch that deposited a `toBeProved` goal releases its successor but keeps working forever: its statements — and those of every scope minted below it — feed request generation in every later burst of the LB, although the branch has already contributed everything its cohort can use. The wipe ([D-242](#d-242)) is reserved for refuted branches and cannot serve here: a resolved branch's rows are cited by `orBookkeeping`, the convergence history and the chapter export. Separately, LBs whose goal registry is empty for life (the `try_contradiction` / `try_contradiction_negated_head` reductio blocks seed status 0 only) opened cohorts whose branches could never resolve by goal — the B3 "frozen by construction" pattern.
- **Decision.** Two rules, both LB-local. **(1) Freeze.** A live branch is RESOLVED when every `intToBeProved` key whose scope is the cohort parent or one of its ancestors up to `main` (the branch's chain) is `known` at the branch scope or a strict ancestor (`ancestorKnown`, self included — the ancestor clause covers goal deposits Site F refused as ancestor-known, [I-187](30_invariants.md#i-187)); zero chain goals resolve vacuously. The end-of-burst sweep `freezeResolvedOrBranches` (`performElemPhase3`, after `drainDeadOrBranches`, before `drainPendingOrReleases`) evaluates every live branch (`Memory::orLiveBranches`, registered by `ordisMerge` on the branch's first deposit) and moves the resolved ones into `Memory::frozenOrBranches` — a one-way latch until discharge. The single consumer is `filterIntEncodedStatements`: a statement whose scope is a frozen branch or any descendant of one leaves the request universe from the next `generateEncodedRequestsStatic` call on (generator and stump producer share the filter, so the split partition, [I-156](30_invariants.md#i-156), is preserved). Nothing else changes: no registry row, `orBookkeeping` entry, `known` row or history line is erased; deposits into a frozen scope are still accepted (they may complete a convergence already booked); the reached goal is NOT erased — it closes on the normal path when the converged expression lands at the parent scope. The release trigger (first goal match) is unchanged; freezing is the stricter "all chain goals" condition, evaluated per burst so a goal closed elsewhere later completes it. **(2) No goals, no or branches.** In `consumeOrLeavesCohort` an LB with an empty goal registry (any scope; evaluated at every open attempt) neither opens nor parks a cohort — the flat K / subset-exclusion rules still land; `drainPendingOrReleases` releases nothing for such an LB (the staging drops). A goal-less registry never regains a goal (goals register only from the LB's own head at status 2), so the drop is final.
- **Consequences.** (a) A frozen branch derives nothing new, so a LATER convergence on an expression it never deposited cannot happen through it — `_ordis_` convergence is over expressions deposited before the freeze; the maintainer's intended trade. (b) Reductio LBs open no cohorts. (c) The doom line / split statistics see a smaller universe (intended). (d) Two persistent-arena pod sets (`pendingDeadOrBranches` twins): no deload tag, no dump section (Rule 14 untouched), no `MEM_MEASUREMENT` row.
- **Rejected.** Wiping the resolved branch (breaks the convergence history and `check_or_convergence`); freezing at the first goal match (the maintainer chose "all chain goals"); a per-deposit filter at the doors (the branch must keep accepting deposits); a deloadable `LbMemory` set (the phase-2 reader must never hit a residency assert — the persistent arena is always resident, [I-108](30_invariants.md#i-108)).
- **Measurement (2026-08-25; one run per side, same host, `RT_MEASUREMENT` 0).** Reference = `main` (, , ); branch = (, ). **Every artifact byte-identical**: `theorems.txt` shortcut 64 / full 63 lines unchanged; verifier 9713 (shortcut) and 122318 / 16054 / 138372 (full) checks, 0 failures on both sides. Runtime: FTA shortcut prover 113.34 → 109.29 s, wall 119.81 → 113.31 s; full pipeline wall 723.62 → 683.26 s (−5.6 %) — Gauss 163.91 → 158.76, Peano 49.69 → 46.18, IncubatorPeano1/2 114.84 / 10.58 → 105.68 / 9.99, IncubatorGauss1/2/3 54.50 / 10.71 / 118.31 → 54.14 / 11.15 / 114.61. Nothing slower beyond noise; the proofs are the same proofs with less request generation behind them.
- **Tests.** `tests/test_memory.cpp`: `ordis_merge_registers_live_branch`, `freeze_resolved_or_branches_all_chain_goals_known`, `freeze_resolved_or_branches_chain_scope_and_latch`, `filter_int_encoded_statements_excludes_frozen_subtree`, `generate_encoded_requests_static_skips_frozen_subtree`; `tests/test_rejected_ordis.cpp`: `ordis_no_goals_neither_opens_nor_parks`, `drain_pending_or_releases_goalless_lb_releases_nothing`; the six cohort-opening fixtures gain a main goal.
- **Where.** `memory.hpp` (`orLiveBranches`, `frozenOrBranches`), `memory.cpp` (`dischargeStatementContent` reset, `filterIntEncodedStatements`), `prover.hpp` (`ordisMerge`, the sweep declaration, `filterIntEncodedStatements` declaration), `prover.cpp` (`freezeResolvedOrBranches`, `performElemPhase3`, `consumeOrLeavesCohort`, `drainPendingOrReleases`), tests. New invariant [I-206](30_invariants.md#i-206); amends [I-174](30_invariants.md#i-174), [I-108](30_invariants.md#i-108), [I-187](30_invariants.md#i-187).

<a id="d-303"></a>
## D-303 — the whole-key index is a bare key SET: no owner record of any kind, no scope wipe; the subkey map keeps only its u_-signature record (2026-08-25,, maintainer-directed)

- - **Context.** The maintainer's design for this campaign was explicit from the start: Part 2 = "permanent removal of structures and code dealing with the values of normalized keys" — the whole-key map becomes a presence set, exactly as the subkey map did in [D-302](#d-302). [D-304](#d-304) deviated from that: it kept a value (the deduped owner scope vids) so the scope wipe's drop-on-empty could survive, on the agent's reasoning rather than a measurement. The maintainer rejected the deviation ("now normalized keys r just a set?" — no; "why the fuck did u diverge?"). This entry executes the design as stated.
- **Decision.** `normalizedEncodedKeys` is `TypedColdSet<NormKey>` — key bytes only (deload facets Lengths + Bytes at `base+5..6`; the former value facets `base+7..9` are a hole; the `MEM_MEASUREMENT` facet table drops its three value rows). Install door `ensureWholeKeyPresent(set, n, data, len)`: `encodeNormKeyInto` + an idempotent `mint`, no read-modify-write. The probe `wholeKeyPresent` is unchanged (a bare lookup; `normKeyLookup` is now a template over both cold containers). `OwnerSet` loses `ownerScopes` and is the subkey map's record alone — `{hasLooseOwner, uSignatures}`; the empty record is five bytes (`ensureEmptySubkeyRecord`), `OwnerSetBlob::uSigOffset == 1`, `Codec<OwnerSet>` codes no id run. `mergeOwnerRecordCore` and both `mergeOwnerScope` doors are gone; `mergeSubkeySignatures` is the one blob-native signature merge. **No scope wipe of any normalized-key index:** `Memory::wipeSubtree` steps 10b (`wipeOwnerSetMapForClosed`) and 10c (`wipeRemainingArgsForClosed` + the `ReverseArgsIndex` rebuild it drove) are deleted with both helpers; the rule registry (`encodedMap`, step 10a) is still wiped. The hashburst dump's two sections are retyped (maintainer consent, Rule 14): `normalizedEncodedKeys` prints lex-sorted `key=…` rows (`N keys, set`), `normalizedEncodedSubkeys` prints `key=… | loose=<0/1> | sigs=<n>` rows.
- **Soundness.** A stale whole key (its installing rules all closed) still emits its request; the firing site `checkLocalEncodedMemoryStatic` looks the key up in the wiped `encodedMap`, misses, and `continue`s — a defined skip, no assert, no firing ([I-49](30_invariants.md#i-49), [I-79](30_invariants.md#i-79)). A stale remaining-args entry produces a candidate whose `encodedMap` lookup misses the same way. Nothing else reads either index.
- **Memory.** A whole key costs its key bytes and nothing else (no blob index, no record); a subkey costs five bytes below three premises. The D1 flood (16.7k owner ids under one key) is gone entirely, as is the NameMap's interned copy of every expanded implication text.
- **Memory, measured (2026-08-25; `MEM_MEASUREMENT` 1, `main.py --shortcut`, one run per side, 45 iteration samples, peak at sample #5 on both; evidence `.worktree/nk_mem_{before,after}/.rt/_memory_FTA.log`, runs  — 9713 checks, 0 failures on both). Before = `main` (the last commit before the subkey campaign, [D-302](#d-302)); after = `main` (this decision landed).** Peak attributed 960.50 → 933.50 MiB (−27.0 MiB, −2.8 %): container content 296.33 → 289.34 (−6.99), derived hash indexes 127.17 → 126.60 (−0.57), block + page slack 537.00 → 517.56 (−19.44 — slack follows content). Per container at the peak sample, `overallHashMemory` 74.39 → 70.60 MiB: `normalizedEncodedKeys` 10.79 → 9.29 (its value facets `blobPool` 1.14 + `runStarts` 0.18 + `blobStarts` 0.18 are gone; the key `bytes` 7.30 + `lengths` 0.18 are what a set costs), `normalizedEncodedSubkeys` 20.68 → 18.38 (`blobPool` 3.14 → 0.85 — the D-302 signature-only record), `encodedMap` and `remainingArgsNormalizedEncodedMap` unchanged; the three transient instances shrink in proportion (`workingMemory` 10.91 → 10.74, `localHashMemory` 9.33 → 9.06, `localHashMemoryDelta` 5.02 → 4.99). `LbMemory` direct members 271.21 → 267.95 (−3.26: the NameMap no longer interns every expanded implication text; `validityNodes` 2.66 → 2.45). The shortcut carries no pathological template subkey, so the D1-class flood (a 262 KB record under one key) is not in this sample; what the sample shows is the structural floor — a normalized key now costs its bytes and nothing else.
- **Measurement (2026-08-25; `RT_MEASUREMENT` 0, one run per configuration, typeperf-bracketed; reference = the D-302 `clean` runs of `main`; evidence , the `frame_timing_*.jsonl` ledgers, the `cpu_trace_*.csv` traces and `cpu_chart_*.html` charts).** FTA shortcut: prover 107.46 → 109.42 s (Part 1: 111.60), wall 112.79 → 114.84 s. Full pipeline: wall 681.54 → 663.39 s (−2.7 %); Gauss prover 197.26 → 193.98 s; Peano 59.97 → 59.02; IncubatorPeano1/2 107.13 / 10.89 → 99.80 / 10.20; IncubatorGauss1/2/3 65.52 / 15.28 / 113.57 → 63.55 / 15.00 / 113.47 — nothing slower, the wipe's removal shows on the incubators. Every artifact byte-identical to the reference: `theorems.txt` (main, incubator, shortcut) and both `global_theorem_list.txt`; proven counts 518 / 79 / 77 / 102 / 24 / 4 / 19 and 39; verifier 9713 / 16054 / 122318 / 138372 checks, 0 failures. Verdict: stale keys cost nothing measurable; the bare set is at least as fast as every record shape before it and stores nothing.
- **Tests.** `whole_key_present_reads_presence_only` (set door + probe, idempotent mint), `hashmemory_clear_*` (mint into the set), `ownerset_blob_view_field_readers` / `owner_set_blob_roundtrip_wide_id` / `codec_owner_set_round_trip` (signature-only record, five-byte empty record), `merge_subkey_signatures_raw_blob_matches_record_usignature`, `empty_subkey_record_inserts_once`; deleted: `merge_owner_scope_raw_matches_owning`, `merge_owner_scope_rmw`, `merge_owner_scope_wide_vid_roundtrip`, `whole_key_and_subkey_records_are_disjoint_projections`, `wipe_owner_set_map_filtered_matches_heap_oracle`, `wipe_remaining_args_pruned_matches_heap_oracle`.
- **Where.** `memory_infra/hash_memory.hpp` (the set + 2 facets), `infra/mem_tracker.cpp`, `memory.hpp` (`OwnerSet`, `OwnerSetBlob`, `Codec<OwnerSet>`; the two wipe helpers deleted), `memory.cpp` (install sites; `wipeHashMem` 10b/10c deleted), `prover.hpp` (`ensureWholeKeyPresent`, `wholeKeyPresent`, `normKeyLookup`, `mergeSubkeySignatures`), `infra/hashburst_dump.cpp`, `memory_infra/reverse_args_index.hpp` (doc), `tests/test_memory.cpp`. Supersedes [D-304](#d-304); rewrites [I-49](30_invariants.md#i-49), [I-100](30_invariants.md#i-100), [I-143](30_invariants.md#i-143), [I-154](30_invariants.md#i-154).

<a id="d-304"></a>
## D-304 — the whole-key owner record is the deduped set of owner SCOPES; the composite owner ids, the D-105 / D-119 predicates, `ownerKeyAccepts` and the rule-dimension split plumbing are deleted (2026-08-25,, maintainer-directed)

- - **SUPERSEDED the same day by [D-303](#d-303).** Keeping the owner scope set for the wipe was the agent's deviation from the maintainer's stated design (a bare set); the scope set, the wipe and their code are deleted there. The deletions listed below stand.
- **Context.** [D-305](#d-305) measured the whole-key owner record's runtime value at the emission gate: none (Gauss prover 197.26 → 195.73 s, every artifact byte-identical). The record — loose byte + one 8-byte `(implId, scopeVid)` composite per installing rule + the u_ signatures — then had exactly one production reader left, the scope wipe (`wipeOwnerSetMapForClosed`), whose drop criterion "every owner's scope vid is closed" is a function of the owner SCOPE set alone. The maintainer's direction: retype the dump decoder and delete every useless structure and line of code.
- **Decision.** `OwnerSet::partitionIds` (`std::set<int64_t>`) becomes `OwnerSet::ownerScopes` (`std::set<NameId>`): a whole-key record stores the DISTINCT scope validity ids of its installing rules — one `NameId` per scope, however many rules share it — with the loose byte set and NO signature; a subkey record stores the loose byte + signatures and NO scope (both shapes asserted at install in `mergeOwnerRecordCore`). `Codec<OwnerSet>` and `OwnerSetBlob` are retyped (`scopeCount` / `scopeAt`, a 4-byte run). The whole-key install door is `mergeOwnerScope(map, n, data, len, scopeVid)` (raw door + owning-key oracle), a scope-only door over the shared `mergeOwnerRecordCore`; `addToHashMemory` / `makeNormalizedKeysForAdmission` pass `ownerVid` and no longer mint the expanded implication text into the NameMap (that mint served only the composite). The wipe reads `scopeAt(i)` directly and rewrites a partial record at `bl − 4·dropped`; its `droppedKeys` is byte-identical to the composite form's. Deleted outright: `ownerKeyAccepts`, both `ownerSetHasComparable` overloads (D-105 retired), both `partitionAccepts` overloads, `makePartitionId`, the `g_splitProcessID` / `g_splitCount` thread-locals and the `processID` / `splitCount` parameters of `performElem2` / `ExecTask` / the CE-filter call (D-119 retired — production never left `splitCount == 1`; the expression split is the only split), the two heap `mergeOwnerRecord` oracles and the raw `mergeOwnerRecord` door, `OwnerSetBlob::rdI64` / `partitionCount` / `partitionId`, `installAdmissionMarkerVariants`' `partitionId` parameter. The hashburst dump's owner-set section is retyped with the maintainer's explicit consent (Rule 14): a row prints `scopes=N | {v=<scope>, …}` (lex-sorted decoded scope names) instead of `owners=N | {impl(v=scope), …}`.
- **Memory.** A whole-key record shrinks from `9 + 8·owners (+ signatures)` bytes to `9 + 4·distinct scopes`; the D1 flood (16.7k main-scope owners under one key, ≈134 KB) becomes 13 bytes. The NameMap no longer holds an interned copy of every expanded implication text.
- **Measurement.** Pending — shortcut and full pipeline against the `clean` reference (and the Part-1 `nk_p1` runs), filled in after the runs; `theorems.txt` byte-identity is the gate.
- **Tests.** `merge_owner_scope_raw_matches_owning` (blob-native door == owning oracle; dedup, interior insert), `merge_subkey_signatures_raw_blob_matches_record_usignature` (subkey door == `recordUSignature` + codec oracle over a merge sequence), `merge_owner_scope_rmw`, `merge_owner_scope_wide_vid_roundtrip`, `whole_key_present_reads_presence_only`, `whole_key_and_subkey_records_are_disjoint_projections`, `produce_expression_stumps_are_deterministic` (the "identical across parts" form retired with the rule dimension); retyped: `ownerset_blob_view_field_readers`, `owner_set_blob_roundtrip_wide_id`, `codec_owner_set_round_trip`, `wipe_owner_set_map_filtered_matches_heap_oracle`; deleted: `ownerset_has_comparable_validity_prune`, `ownerset_blob_partition_accepts_matches_set`, `ownerset_blob_has_comparable_matches_value`, `makepartitionid_nonnegative_large_id`, `owner_key_accepts_lookup_and_prune`, `make_partition_id_packs_and_is_injective`, `partition_accepts_filters_by_residue`.
- **Where.** `memory.hpp` (`OwnerSet`, `OwnerSetBlob`, `Codec<OwnerSet>`, `wipeOwnerSetMapForClosed`), `prover.hpp` (`mergeOwnerRecordCore`, `mergeOwnerScope`, `mergeSubkeySignatures`, the `performElem2` signature), `memory.cpp` (the install sites), `prover.cpp` / `filter.cpp` (`ExecTask`, the `performElem2` calls), `infra/hashburst_dump.cpp` (`dumpOwnerSetMap`), `tests/test_memory.cpp`, `tests/test_lb_split.cpp`. Retires [I-70](30_invariants.md#i-70), [I-80](30_invariants.md#i-80), [I-159](30_invariants.md#i-159); rewrites [I-49](30_invariants.md#i-49) clause 1, [I-100](30_invariants.md#i-100), [I-143](30_invariants.md#i-143).

<a id="d-305"></a>
## D-305 — the whole-key record probe reads key presence only; no production probe reads an owner-set value (2026-08-25,, maintainer-directed)

- - **Context.** After [D-302](#d-302) the subkey record carries no owner ids and its growth probe reads only the u_ signature; the whole-key map `normalizedEncodedKeys` — the request generator's emission gate — still stores the full owner record per key (loose byte + one 8-byte `(implId, scopeVid)` composite per owning rule + the u_ signatures), and its four record probes read it through `ownerKeyAccepts`: scope comparability ([D-105](#d-105)), LB-split residue ([D-119](#d-119)), u_ signature ([D-120](#d-120)). Two of the three are inert on every production path — the residue check short-circuits at `g_splitCount == 1`, which `proveKernel` and the CE filter never leave, and the scope check returns at once for `main`-scope requests — so the live whole-key value read is the u_-signature check alone: exactly the subkey situation D-302 measured (presence-only 3.2× slower on Gauss, the signature alone at reference speed). The whole-key owner record is the remaining memory flood of the D1 investigation (16.7k owner ids under one key); its runtime value at the emission gate was never measured.
- **Decision (Part 1, this entry).** The four whole-key probe sites switch to `ExpressionAnalyzer::wholeKeyPresent` — `normKeyLookup!= 0`, no scope fold, no blob peek: the full-key half of `filterIntEncodedStatements`, the stump-alone and grow-node record probes in `generateEncodedRequestsStatic`, and the terminal pre-stump probe in `produceExpressionStumps`. Installs (`mergeOwnerRecord`), the wipe (`wipeOwnerSetMapForClosed` and its `droppedKeys` feed into the remaining-args index, [I-154](30_invariants.md#i-154)) and the hashburst dump are untouched, so the stored record and the dump bytes are unchanged; `ownerKeyAccepts` stays as the retained value-reading form with no production caller.
- **What changes observably.** The emitted request set widens to every structural whole-key match: a request an owner's u_ signature (or, off `main`, an incomparable owner scope) would have pruned now reaches the firing site `checkLocalEncodedMemoryStatic` and fails there. The submatch tally `g_growthMatchCount` is untouched (bumped by the subkey growth probe alone), but emitted requests are burst work, so split decisions and early-exit stop points can shift; `theorems.txt` is the gate. Soundness unchanged: every value-accepting hit is a presence hit ([I-70](30_invariants.md#i-70), [I-79](30_invariants.md#i-79)).
- **Measurement (2026-08-25; `RT_MEASUREMENT` 0, one run per configuration; reference = the D-302 `clean` runs of `main`; evidence , the `frame_timing_*.jsonl` ledgers, the `cpu_trace_*.csv` traces and their `cpu_chart_*.html` charts).** FTA shortcut: prover 107.46 → 111.60 s (+3.9 %; the pre-D-302 reference was 111.11), wall 112.79 → 115.28 s. Full pipeline: wall 681.54 → 680.73 s; Gauss prover 197.26 → 195.73 s; Peano 59.97 → 59.30; IncubatorPeano1/2 107.13 / 10.89 → 104.07 / 10.81; IncubatorGauss1/2/3 65.52 / 15.28 / 113.57 → 65.46 / 18.20 / 114.10 — every leg inside run-to-run noise. Every artifact byte-identical to the reference: `theorems.txt` (main, incubator, shortcut) and both `global_theorem_list.txt`; proven counts 518 / 79 / 77 / 102 / 24 / 4 / 19 and 39; verifier 9713 / 16054 / 122318 / 138372 checks, 0 failures. Verdict: the whole-key owner record buys no measurable runtime at the emission gate; the D-120 signature's runtime value lives at the subkey growth probe ([D-302](#d-302)), not at the whole-key record probe.
- **Follow-on (Part 2, maintainer's call on the number).** Permanent removal of the whole-key value machinery. The wipe's drop criterion is "every owner's scope vid is closed" — a function of the owner SCOPE set alone — so a deduped run of owner scope vids reproduces `droppedKeys` byte-identically while the impl-id half (which served only the inert D-119 residue and the dump) goes; presence-only holds reference speed (measured above), so the u_ signatures go too and the record shrinks to the loose byte plus the deduped owner scope vids — done in [D-304](#d-304).
- **Where.** `prover.hpp` (`wholeKeyPresent`, next to `ownerKeyAccepts`), `memory.cpp` (the four record-probe sites), `tests/test_memory.cpp` (`whole_key_present_ignores_owner_values`).

<a id="d-302"></a>
## D-302 — the subkey growth probe reads key presence only; the owner-set value prunes run at the whole-key probe alone (2026-08-25,, maintainer-directed)

- **Context.** Every grow node of the request generator probed `normalizedEncodedSubkeys` through `ownerKeyAccepts`: a key lookup followed by three reads of the key's owner-set value — scope comparability ([D-105](#d-105)), LB-split residue ([D-119](#d-119)), u_-literal signature ([D-120](#d-120)). All three are pure prunes the firing site re-checks ([I-70](30_invariants.md#i-70), [I-79](30_invariants.md#i-79)), and two are inert in production: the residue check short-circuits at `g_splitCount == 1`, which the main path never leaves, and the scope check returns at once for `main`-scope requests. The value payload is what floods memory — the D1 investigation found 16.7k owner ids plus 3.6k signatures under one subkey — while its runtime benefit was never measured.
- **Decision.** The subkey growth probe becomes `ExpressionAnalyzer::subkeyPresent`: the same `Codec<NormKey>` byte probe, verdict = `lookup!= 0`, no scope fold, no blob peek. Four sites switch — the subkey half of `filterIntEncodedStatements`, the stump-alone and grow-node growth probes in `generateEncodedRequestsStatic`, and the growth probe in `produceExpressionStumps`. The four whole-key probes (`normalizedEncodedKeys`, the emission gate) keep `ownerKeyAccepts` with all three prunes, so the emitted request set is unchanged.
- **What changes observably.** More grow nodes are visited (every present subkey continues the search), and the submatch tally `g_growthMatchCount` — bumped on the growth probe's verdict — counts presence hits. The tally is the doom-line coordinate ([I-191](30_invariants.md#i-191)) and the straggler split statistic ([I-160](30_invariants.md#i-160)), so split decisions and early-exit stop points can shift; `theorems.txt` is the gate.
- **Measurement (2026-08-25; `RT_MEASUREMENT` 0, one run per configuration; evidence , the `frame_timing_*.jsonl` ledgers, the `cpu_trace_*.csv` traces and their charts).** FTA shortcut: prover 111.11 → 112.92 s (+1.6 %, inside run-to-run noise), wall 114.87 → 118.38 s. Full pipeline: wall 685.08 → 1083.46 s, and the whole delta is Gauss — prover **172.50 → 558.47 s (3.2×)**, per-burst `dt` 2× in the early bursts and 3–5× in the heavy induction bursts (burst 27: 15.7 → 80.8 s); Peano 61.74 → 59.52 s and the five incubator batches within ±17 s. Every artifact byte-identical on both sides (`theorems.txt` main + incubator, both `global_theorem_list.txt`), verifier 9713 / 16054 / 122318 / 138372 checks with 0 failures, proven-theorem counts identical — the wider tally changed no split decision that reached a proof. Verdict: the FTA shortcut is indifferent to the subkey value prunes, Gauss is not — on Gauss they carry a 3× factor of the grow search. Which of the two live prunes (D-105 scope comparability, D-120 u_ signature) carries it is unmeasured.
- **Follow-on.** The proposed deletion of the subkey owner-set value (a presence set) is the maintainer's call in the light of the Gauss number; the measurement says the value is not free to drop — whatever record survives has to keep the prune that carries the Gauss effect.
- **Variant 2 (maintainer-directed, 2026-08-25): u_ control alone.** To find which prune carries the Gauss factor, the growth probe becomes `subkeyUSatisfied` — presence plus the D-120 u_-signature check only; scope comparability (D-105) and the split residue (D-119) stay off at the subkey probe (`subkeyPresent` is kept as the presence primitive over the shared `subkeyLookup`). **Measured (2026-08-25, same protocol, evidence  + ledgers + CPU traces):** full wall 678.13 s (reference 685.08, Part 1 1083.46); Gauss prover **174.99 s** (reference 172.50, Part 1 558.47) — the per-burst `dt` tracks the reference burst for burst; Peano 60.21, incubators within noise; FTA shortcut prover 105.07 s (reference 111.11, Part 1 112.92). Artifacts byte-identical, verifier identical (0 failures). Verdict: the D-120 u_-signature check is the WHOLE Gauss effect; the scope-comparability read (D-105) and the partition read (D-119) at the subkey probe buy nothing measurable on any batch. A subkey record therefore needs its `hasLooseOwner` byte and its u_-signature set; its owner ids serve request generation no more.
- **Variant 3 (maintainer-directed, 2026-08-25): the u_ check from three premises on; shorter subkeys are presence-only on BOTH sides.** The pathological owner set is the one- or two-premise subkey (one template premise shared by every ground instance: one signature per instance, scanned linearly). `kSubkeyUCheckMinElements = 3`: `subkeyUSatisfied` reads the signatures only for subkeys of at least three premises, and the two install sites (`addToHashMemory`, `makeNormalizedKeysForAdmission`) give a shorter subkey an EMPTY owner record through `ensureEmptySubkeyRecord` (nine bytes: loose byte set, zero ids, zero signatures; a present key is left untouched — no read-modify-write). Such a key carries no owner accounting, so `wipeOwnerSetMapForClosed` keeps a zero-owner key verbatim (dropping it would lose firings) and it lives until the map's `resetToFresh`. **Measured (2026-08-25, same protocol, evidence  + ledgers + CPU traces):** Gauss prover **198.27 s** (reference 172.50, u_ at every length 174.99, presence-only 558.47) — the heavy induction bursts run a uniform 15–30 % slower than the reference, not the 3–5× of presence-only; full wall 693.12 s (reference 685.08); Peano 60.19, incubators within noise (IncubatorGauss1/2 72.86 / 17.91 vs 84.41 / 22.41); FTA shortcut prover 106.77 s (reference 111.11). Artifacts byte-identical, verifier identical (0 failures). Verdict: the signatures of the one- and two-premise subkeys prune early but carry only ~15 % on Gauss; the ≥ 3-premise signatures carry the rest of the 3× factor. The short subkeys can store nothing at a ~15 % Gauss price, or keep their signatures to hold the reference speed.
- **Final implementation (maintainer-accepted Variant 3, 2026-08-25).** The subkey record is exactly what its growth probe reads. Below `kSubkeyUCheckMinElements` (3) premises: the empty record (`ensureEmptySubkeyRecord`). From three on: the loose byte + the set of distinct u_ signatures, installed through `mergeSubkeySignatures` — a door over the shared `mergeOwnerRecordCore` that never inserts an owner id (asserted); `mergeOwnerRecord` is the whole-key door with the id. The subkey map carries no owner accounting and is no longer scope-wiped (`wipeHashMem` wipes the whole-key map only; `wipeOwnerSetMapForClosed` asserts a non-empty owner run). The probes share one `normKeyLookup`; the presence-only `subkeyPresent` is gone. [I-49](30_invariants.md#i-49) rewritten accordingly. The hashburst dump's subkey section keeps its format (`owners=0 | {}` per subkey now — derived content). **Measured (2026-08-25, same protocol,  + ledgers + CPU traces):** full wall 681.54 s (reference 685.08); Gauss prover 197.26 s (the accepted +15 %), IncubatorGauss1/2 65.52 / 15.28 s (reference 84.41 / 22.41 — the install-side saving), Peano 59.97, the rest within noise; FTA shortcut prover 107.46 s (reference 111.11). Artifacts byte-identical, verifier identical (0 failures). Squashed to `main` on the maintainer's instruction.
- **Where.** `prover.hpp` (`normKeyLookup` / `subkeyUSatisfied` / `kSubkeyUCheckMinElements` / `ensureEmptySubkeyRecord` / `mergeOwnerRecordCore` / `mergeOwnerRecord` / `mergeSubkeySignatures`, next to `ownerKeyAccepts`), `memory.cpp` (the four growth-probe sites, the two subkey install loops, `wipeHashMem` 10b), `memory.hpp` (`wipeOwnerSetMapForClosed`), `tests/test_memory.cpp` (`subkey_u_satisfied_reads_signature_only`, `merge_subkey_signatures_is_owner_record_without_ids`, `empty_subkey_record_inserts_once`, `produce_expression_stumps_are_identical_across_parts_and_deterministic`).

<a id="d-299"></a>
## D-299 — the algebra admission-key cleanup is deleted, not gated (2026-08-22,, maintainer-directed)

- **Context.** When an algebra admission key matched and its head fired, `cleanAdmissionMap` erased the key and recorded it in `consumedAdmissionKeys` forever — the direct erase plus the [D-62](#d-62) canonicalization closure over every same-scope key with the same canonical form. On 2026-08-18 the whole cleanup was switched off behind one entry gate (`D-300`,) as the smallest possible experiment. The full-pipeline A/B came back **runtime-flat** (1171.32 s → 1171.59 s overall, every leg inside noise) with the verifier airtight and no theorem gained or lost by the switch. That experiment's own exit criterion was: if runtime stays flat, remove the machinery.
- **The cost it was carrying.** Consumption is permanent, so an admission key that is also an induction implication's premise cursor dies at its first match. A match arriving before its cursor exists parks, revives once, consumes the key, and the implication can never advance through that slot (the C6 Gauss-fold investigation, state doc Step 12). The closure widened the same hazard across a whole equivalence class.
- **Decision.** Delete the machinery outright rather than keep an off switch: `cleanAdmissionMap` and its four call sites, the `consumedAdmissionKeys` cold set with its facet / dump section / subtree-wipe erase and all six reader gates, and `canonicalizeUnderClasses`, which nothing else called. An admission key now stays live for its LB's lifetime and is removed only by the canonicalization re-key of `applyEquivalenceClassToAdmissionMap` or by the subtree wipe.
- **Why deletion beats a gate.** A permanently-false switch is dead machinery that still has to be read, statified, deloaded and dumped, and its inert reader gates read as live contracts. The disable experiment already proved the behaviour identical.
- **What this retires.** [I-41](30_invariants.md#i-41) (the canonicalization closure), [I-71](30_invariants.md#i-71) (admission / consumed mutual exclusion), [G-31](50_gotchas.md#g-31) (do not add the cleanup to integration revival), and the consumption half of [D-62](#d-62). [I-22](30_invariants.md#i-22) survives with its asymmetry gone: no path erases an admission key on use, on either side.
- **Facet number.** The set's deload facet at `base+31` is left permanently unused rather than renumbering the band, so every other facet keeps its tag.
- **Contract.** [I-200](30_invariants.md#i-200).
- **Where.** `prover.hpp`, `prover.cpp`, `memory.cpp`, `memory_infra/hash_memory.hpp`, `infra/hashburst_dump.cpp`.

<a id="d-295"></a>
## D-295 — the obligatory stump retires from every batch; the containment grow becomes the generator's only mandatory-ingredient mode (2026-08-22,, maintainer-directed)

**Context.** [D-298](#d-298) folded batches 2 and 3 onto the containment grow and left batches 1, 4 and 5 on the pairing merge. An RT measurement run on the branch point (shortcut, 6657 bursts) put batch 1's surviving merge second in the profile behind the folded grow — 11.8% of attributed burst time, enumerating 680,490 (base candidate x stump) pairings per run across 4,693 calls. Batches 4 and 5 are the same shape together under 0.2%. Two modes also keep two owner-set maps alive that only the stumped record probe reads.

**Decision.** Move all three batches onto mandatory-containment terms, then delete the obligatory stump outright, so the generator has ONE mandatory-ingredient mode. The batches keep their separate calls — each reads a different rule registry, which drives the key length, the target map and every owner probe — and only the stump becomes a term: batch 1 names `intLocalEncodedStatements`, batch 4 names `intExternalStatements`, and batch 5 names the whole statement universe, which is the search universe itself, so its requirement is vacuous and it passes an EMPTY term list instead.

**Why the emission set is preserved.** The same downward-closure argument the fold rested on, applied per registry: the subkey map of any `HashMemory` is closed under subsets because `addToHashMemory` installs every subset of every rule's premise set into it, so a whole key accepted by that registry's `normalizedEncodedKeys` has every prefix of its ascending order reachable, and the merge's per-pair viability pre-filter and its key-minus-one record probe are both implied by the whole-key probe at the finished candidate. Batch 5's term names the grow universe, so every non-empty candidate satisfies it; an empty term list is the same predicate stated without the per-candidate mask test.

**The split-stump consequence.** The containment mode was previously used only against `overallHashMemory`, the registry `produceExpressionStumps` itself grows over, so every split-stump element was guaranteed to be in the consumer's filtered universe and the code asserted it. Against a narrower registry that guarantee is gone: the batch may hold no rule that could use a given statement. The run now skips such a stump before the seed frame, which is exactly the verdict the stumped modes reached one probe later at the subkey gate — see [I-156](30_invariants.md#i-156)'s narrower-registry qualifier for the proof that the whole subtree is empty. Found by the assert firing on the first batch-1 run, not by reading.

**The empty-term-list consequence.** Batch 5 makes "no mandatory ingredient" a prover input for the first time, and the generator had encoded "termless" as "this is the counter-example filter" in two places. Both are wrong now and both were corrected rather than relaxed. The two entry assertions that inferred an unsplit LB from a termless call are gone from the generator and their statement now sits at the CE call site, the one caller for which it holds. The stump-alone probe branched on the presence of terms, which would have sent a termless SPLIT batch down the base-candidate path and into a merge with no stumps — emitting nothing; it now keys on the stump length, exactly as the depth-first record site already did.

**What the deletion removes.** With no caller passing a stump, five parameters, the stump-preparation, seed and merge phases, `Stump`, `makeMandatoryEncodedStatementLists1Static`, `BaseCandidate`, `preEvaluateFromEncoded` (the merge was its last caller), and the already-dead `ThreadArenas` / `TypedArena` go. The grow depth becomes `maxKeyLength`, `alsoAcceptFullKeys` becomes constantly true, and the three-way target-map choice becomes `normalizedEncodedKeys`. This supersedes [D-200](#d-200): its whole `stumpLen` axis is gone, and with it D-200's open question about the merge's `base ++ stump` tie order, which no longer exists.

**Gate — content identity.** The theorem set is the gate, and it never moved. NINE FTA `theorems.txt` files were captured on this host across the campaign — the pre-edit baseline, all four steps, both full-pipeline runs, a final shortcut, and a fresh branch-point run — and all nine are the SAME FILE, md5, 63 lines. The branch-point capture is the load-bearing one: the code this campaign replaced and the code that replaced it emit a byte-identical theorem file.

Unit tests 1507/1507 through step 2, then 1506/1506 from step 3 (one fewer because the seed-phase dealing test is deleted with the phase it tested). Verifier on the shortcut: 9822 checks / 0 failures from step 1 onward, against the branch point's 9635 / 0.

Full-pipeline determinism pair, both runs on the final code: 138,351 checks / 0 failures each, per-batch saves 1036 / 156 / 204 / 49 / 8 each, FTA theorem file at the same md5. The theorem artifacts are not tracked in git, so those save counts are compared against the branch-point commit message rather than against a file regenerated on this host.

The verifier check-count delta (9635 -> 9822) is chapter-level and lands at step 1 — the same effect the fold recorded. Emission order changes, so the capped origin map records a different candidate per expression and `buildStack`'s ordered pick changes with it; the merge's `base ++ stump` stable sort also placed a name-tied stump element after its base, which the ascending-position grow does not reproduce (the sensitivity `D-200` had flagged as an open question). No theorem is gained, lost or altered — but the proof GRAPHS are not byte-identical, and that is a functional change to the artifacts even though it is not one to the mathematics.

**Gate — runtime.** The host's power supply failed during the campaign and was reattached afterwards, so the per-step timings taken that morning are NOT a usable series: the same RT instrumentation measured -0.95 s of overhead at 09:15 and +10.50 s at 10:09, impossible as a real effect and larger than the whole campaign delta. Those figures are discarded. The gate below is a clean like-for-like pair, both runs taken after the power fix, on the same host minutes apart:

| shortcut | branch point | after | |
|---|---|---|---|
| prover | 117.664 s | 102.048 s | **-13.3%** |
| overall pipeline | 122.393 s | 107.565 s | -12.1% |
| verifier | 9635 / 0 | 9822 / 0 | |
| FTA `theorems.txt` | `be4eca74…` | `be4eca74…` | identical |

Corroborated by iteration counts, which a drifting clock cannot touch: batch 1's 4,693 merge calls and their 680,490 base-candidate-times-stump pairings are gone outright, while the grow enumeration is essentially unchanged (batch 2+3 iterations 2,581,720 -> 2,569,615, batch 1 1,144,231 -> 1,136,500, requests fired 294,686 -> 292,715, all within 0.7%). The merge was pure connect cost and removing it removed no search.

Step 4's own win is memory and deload volume rather than time: two `TypedColdBlobMap` instances and their ten deload facets leave every one of the four `HashMemory` slots per LB, and `addToHashMemory` stops doing two conditional owner-record merges per installed subkey.

**Cost.** Batch 1's grow now runs to full depth instead of stopping one element short, and batches 4 and 5 pay a wider filter now that `alsoAcceptFullKeys` is true for them — the 13.3% is what survives both. The submatch tally loses the merge's contributions again, so the LB-split trigger sees a smaller total; `min_split_work` is left where the fold set it until re-derived at the new scale.

<a id="d-296"></a>
## D-296 — the grow search builds each candidate from its predecessor, not from scratch (2026-08-21,, maintainer-directed)

- **Context.** After the mandatory-containment fold the FTA shortcut is prover-bound and the grow search inside `generateEncodedRequestsStatic` is ~92% of the prover's CPU. An ETW sampled profile of the gated run split that interior for the first time: the two `ownerKeyAccepts` probes 56.87%, `requestGatesPass` 13.93% (self 88.9 core-seconds plus 74.3 in the `productsOfRecursionIds` probes it drives), `makeIntNormalizedKeyFromEncoded` 10.41% (146.0 core-seconds, the second-largest self-time symbol in the binary), the `candPtrs` refill 7.57% (106.7 core-seconds). The middle three are ~455 of 1559.6 core-seconds and every one of them re-derives work that did not change.
- **The observation.** Inside one stack pop the first `top.count` premises are fixed and only the appended one walks the positions. Both remaining per-node computations are monotone under that suffix append. The normalized key renumbers arguments in first-appearance order, so the prefix's key is a strict PREFIX of the child's and appending mints only slots the prefix had not used. The request gates are order-free conjunctions, so each collapses to a summary a premise folds into one at a time — including the hypothesis scope check, whose re-scan ("is every premise at the hypothesis scope, or a main-scope anchor?") is exactly "the distinct scopes of the non-exempt premises are a subset of the hypothesis scope", decidable from a saturating count plus one scope id.
- **Decision.** Prepare the prefix once per pop and redo only the appended premise per position, across all three: the premise pointer array (plain loop-invariant code motion), the key (`NormKeyBuildState` + `buildIntNormalizedKeyPrefix` + `appendExprToIntNormalizedKey`), and the gates (`RequestGateState` + `foldPrefixIntoRequestGates` + `foldExprIntoRequestGates` + `requestGateStateAccepts`). Each position rewinds the carried counters before folding.
- **Factored, never duplicated.** One per-expression body each, called by both the whole-candidate entry and the resume path. `makeIntNormalizedKeyFromEncoded` and `requestGatesPass` keep their signatures and delegate, so no second implementation of the key language or the gate rules exists to drift.
- **Rejected.** Carrying the prefix state in the `StackItem` so a child inherits its parent's instead of rebuilding at pop. It buys nothing — the per-pop rebuild is O(prefix) once and amortizes over the whole position loop, so the recovered fraction is the same whenever the loop visits more positions than the prefix is long — and it would grow each DFS frontier entry from ~50 bytes to over two kilobytes on the byte-bump arena tier.
- **Measured.** Prover on the FTA shortcut 151.55 s → 139.24 s (pointers) → 134.19 s (key) → 129.13 s (gates): **−22.4 s, −14.8%**. Proof artifacts byte-identical to the branch baseline at every step; verifier 9635 checks / 0 failures throughout. About 40% of the addressable region; the rest is depth-bound, since the per-node saving is roughly (count − 1)/count and a pruned DFS is heaviest at the shallow levels.
- **Not touched.** The two owner probes, 57% of the generator. A whole key is hashed and byte-compared once per node however it was built, so an incremental build changes no probe count.
- **Where.** `prover.hpp` (`NormKeyBuildState`, `appendExprToIntNormalizedKey`, `buildIntNormalizedKeyPrefix`, `RequestGateState`, `resetRequestGateState`, `foldExprIntoRequestGates`, `foldPrefixIntoRequestGates`, `requestGateStateAccepts`, and the two delegating entries); `memory.cpp::ExpressionAnalyzer::generateEncodedRequestsStatic` (the per-pop preparation and the per-position rewind). Contract: [I-202](30_invariants.md#i-202). Tests: `test_request_key_build.cpp`, `test_request_gates.cpp`. Plan: [`runtime_ideas.md`](runtime_ideas.md) idea 1.

<a id="d-297"></a>
## D-297 — the chapter walker skips a last-resort fallback whose rows cannot survive (2026-08-21,, maintainer-approved)

- **Context.** With the prover at ~136 s, the chapter export was 36 s of a 182 s gated FTA shortcut — 20%. The RT dissection landed the same day pinned it on one chapter: a single `check_induction_condition` walk making **4,605,957 recursive `buildStack` calls to emit 297 rows**, with counters that are exact powers of two (131,072 cyclic skips = 2^17, 131,071 backtracks = 2^17−1, **262,143 fallback emits = 2^18−1**). Multiplying the fallback emits by the average subtree they walk reproduces the whole call count, so essentially every call was inside a last-resort fallback. The export was also at 96% of `buildStack`'s hard 5,000,000-call abort tripwire — a liveness hazard one ladder rung away.
- **The observation.** `buildStack`'s last-resort fallback emits the front origin and recurses over its entire dependency subtree, then returns false. But a frame that returns false into a **parent's candidate loop** has every row it pushed removed by that parent's `stack.resize(stackSnap)` — the mark was taken before the parent emitted, so it is strictly below anything the child produced — and every `covered` insertion undone by the journal rollback beside it. That fallback's only consumer is the truncation.
- **Decision.** `buildStack` gains a defaulted `rowsSurviveOnFailure` parameter, and skips the whole fallback block when it is clear. Exactly one call site passes `false`: the candidate-loop recursion, the one caller that truncates on a false verdict. The two contradiction tail calls and the fallback's own dependency walk **inherit** the flag (the first because its verdict becomes this frame's verdict, the second because this frame ignores the verdict and never rolls back). Top-level callers take the `true` default, so `findEnds` and the direct unit-test callers are untouched.
- **Why it is output-preserving.** The skipped block always ended in `return false`, so the verdict is unchanged. Its three side effects — rows on `stack`, keys in `covered`, entries in `g_buildStackPath` — are respectively truncated by the parent, rolled back by the parent's journal, and inserted-then-erased symmetrically inside the block itself. Nothing reads any of them between the fallback and the parent's rollback, because the frame returns immediately. The degraded-chapter shape the fallback exists to produce is preserved exactly: rows still survive for the top-level call (whose caller ignores the return), for everything below it reached only through the fallback's own dependency walk, and for a contradiction twin that inherited a surviving frame's fate.
- **Rejected.** Chapter-level parallelism (measured dead — one chapter is 98.4% of the export, so perfect parallelism buys 39.7 s → 39.1 s). Prefetching the export's LB working set from SSD (measured dead — zero reloads). Memoized derivation replay and the bottom-up Knuth-1977 settle: both still open, both bigger; the settle additionally changes chapter content unless its cost tie-break reproduces the D-49 preference order, so it costs a verifier re-baseline this does not. See [`runtime_ideas.md`](runtime_ideas.md).
- **Where.** `visualizer.cpp::ExpressionAnalyzer::buildStack` (the parameter, the four recursive call sites, the skip block); `prover.hpp` (declaration). Contract: [I-201](30_invariants.md#i-201). Test: `test_theorem_usage_graph.cpp::fallback_skipped_when_rows_cannot_survive`.

<a id="d-298"></a>
## D-298 — the request generator's pairing merge retires; one containment-controlled grow covers batches 2 and 3 (2026-08-21,, maintainer-directed)

**Context.** The C_RT investigation's RT aggregate (permanent instrumentation, `.rt/_aggregate_<tag>.log`, shortcut measurement run 2026-08-21, 13340.6 burst-seconds attributed) put 80.6% of all burst time in ONE region: batch 3's pairing merge, and a further 3.5% in batch 2's. The merge is a raw cross product — every recorded base candidate against every mandatory (local, mail) stump, 6.8M bases at 1.58 ms each — and its whole interior is connect cost: the duplicate scan, the `base ++ stump` sort, `preEvaluateFromEncoded`, and the emit-dedup, which an ETW profile of the same window showed as the single hottest function in the process. Firing itself measured 0.03%.

**Decision.** Stop merging. The generator gains a mandatory-containment control — a list of terms, OR-ed, each term an AND-group of statement views (`MandatoryTerm`, [`memory.hpp`](../../GL_Quick_VS/GL_Quick/src/memory.hpp)) — and grows candidates to a whole key, checking at the finished candidate whether the mandatory ingredients are inside it. Batches 2 and 3 fold into ONE such call: they already read the same rule registry (`overallHashMemory`) and the same statement universe (`intEncodedStatements`), differing only in what they oblige a request to contain. Term 1 is the fresh local delta; term 2 is a mail arrival AND a local statement. Membership becomes one bit per filtered statement, computed once per call from a `(originalId, validityId)` interner over the filtered universe; the search prunes a position as soon as no term can still be completed, neither within the remaining depth nor from the suffix of the sorted list ahead of it.

**Why the emission set is preserved.** The subkey map is closed downward — `addToHashMemory` installs every subset of every rule's premise set — so for a whole key K accepted by `normalizedEncodedKeys`, every subset of K is a growable subkey and every prefix of K's ascending order is reachable. The merge's two extra probes are therefore implied: its per-pair viability pre-filter is a subkey probe on a 2-subset of K, and its recordable-base probe asks whether K minus the stump is a key-minus-`k`, which K's own whole-key acceptance answers. The request-shape gates (`requestGatesPass`) are monotone in the set — hypothesis-scope count, distinct secondary variables, and length all only grow — so an intermediate node of a passing request passes too. The ascending-order search gives each subset exactly one path ([I-156](30_invariants.md#i-156)), so the dedup-collapsed request SET matches while the duplicate work does not: a request carrying both a fresh local statement and a fresh arrival used to be emitted by both batches, with the per-call `seen` blind across them.

**The staging repair this forced.** The fold searches `intEncodedStatements`, so a mail arrival must have a registry row to be reachable. It did not always have one: the status-3 drain staged every arrival into `intExternalStatements` unconditionally, while `addExprToMemoryBlock` refuses some outright — measured live, the `x`-prefixed anchor-completion forms the axed-variable door drops ([D-234](#d-234) / [D-236](#d-236)), and positive existence compacts. Those arrivals became mandatory pair elements of emitted requests that the hashburst sink then discarded, because `BurstSink::consume`'s dependency skip refuses any request whose elements are not all in `intKnownStatements`. The maintainer's ruling: that is a leak at the staging site, not a fact about the universe. Staging now runs AFTER the registry offer and only for an arrival the registry actually holds — exact by construction, and it cannot drift from the door's refusal rules the way a duplicated shape test would. The `encodeExpression` call stays where it was, before the offer, so the NameMap mint order is unchanged.

**Gate (shortcut, measured on the committed branch against a fresh branch-point run in its own worktree).** Prover stage 972.1 s -> 132.1 s (7.4x); overall pipeline 1011.2 s -> 169.6 s (6.0x); RT attributed burst time 13340.6 -> 1325.6 burst-seconds (10.1x). `files/shortcut/theorems/theorems.txt` BYTE-IDENTICAL to the branch point (64 theorems, same order). Verifier 9635 checks / 0 failures against the branch point's 9340 / 0 — the delta is chapter-level, see below. Unit tests 1498/1498. The staged-arrival hard stop ([I-205](30_invariants.md#i-205)) does not fire, which is the positive confirmation that the purge closed the 1.8% stale-row leak; it also cut 10 s of prover time by itself, since those arrivals were producing requests the dependency skip discarded. Region by region: batch 3 merge 10746.2 -> gone, batch 2 merge 465.0 -> gone, the two grows they replace 1873.7 -> 1109.3 (folded, at full depth), batch 1 untouched at 201.7 (was 225.0) — the control. The folded grow search is now the single dominant region at 83.7%, and batch 1's surviving pairing merge is second at 9.4%, which is what step 2 removes.

**Cost.** Emission order changes, so the submatch stream renumbers: doom-line coordinates ([I-191](30_invariants.md#i-191)) and the split statistics ([I-160](30_invariants.md#i-160)) land at different values, and `min_split_work` was re-derived (20000 to 5000) because the tally no longer counts merge attempts. The run stays a pure function of proof state. Batches 1, 4 and 5 keep their obligatory stumps for now — each reads a DIFFERENT rule registry, which drives the key length and every probe, so they can never fold into 2+3; moving them onto their own containment terms is the follow-on that retires `normalizedEncodedSubkeysMinusOne` / `…MinusTwo`.

**Alternatives rejected.** Reordering the grow search's join order to put the selective premise first: the maintainer refused it during the C_RT investigation — the canonical name-sorted subkey order IS the hash engine's shared index ([I-155](30_invariants.md#i-155) / [I-156](30_invariants.md#i-156) / [I-77](30_invariants.md#i-77)). Widening the grow universe to include unregistered arrivals: it would newly reach requests that cannot fire, buying nothing and changing the emission set.

<a id="d-294"></a>
## D-294 — FTA exports complete external theorem schemas and replays global compactions in an arbitrary explicit anchor context (2026-08-20,, maintainer-approved)

- **Context.** Removing `grind` exposed four zero-argument definition-compaction rows in the generated FTA module. Each compiled target was globally quantified over an arbitrary carrier and `AnchorFTA`, but its cited earlier FTA theorem and external Peano/Gauss facts were available only at the surrounding theorem's current anchor. That interface mismatch cannot be closed by a small explicit tactic step: a current-context fact does not prove an arbitrary-context proposition.
- **Decision.** FTA theorem interfaces carry the complete universally quantified propositions of every hash-validated external Peano/Gauss theorem. Rows specialize those propositions at their current derived Peano/Gauss anchor. FTA's explicit `relationalInduction` premise is likewise a complete `AnchorFTA`-indexed schema. A zero-argument FTA compaction introduces the target proposition's arbitrary carrier, operations, constants, identity relation, and anchor, then applies the cited earlier FTA theorem at exactly that context while forwarding the same global induction and external-theorem parameters.
- **Trust boundary.** No external proof body is imported, no axiom is added, and no proof search returns. Every assumption remains visible at the generated public theorem boundary and every compaction still replays its one certificate-cited source. The change is confined to the downstream Lean renderer, generated Lean interface, validation, and documentation; GL, MPL, and proof-graph artifacts are unchanged.
- **Verification.** `tests.test_proof_export_lean` pins both the global interfaces and their current-context specializations. `lake build` checks Peano/Gauss, and `lake env lean GLExport\Generated\FTA.lean` separately checks all 79 FTA theorems and 2,835 row facts. The official release runs both kernel gates.
- **Where.** `proof_export/lean.py::_context_signature`, `_external_reference_interfaces`, `_context_application`, `_render_chapter_steps`, and the induction final composition; `tests/test_proof_export_lean.py`; `.scripts/release_public.py`. See [I-199](30_invariants.md#i-199) and [`10_pipeline/10_external_proof_export.md`](10_pipeline/10_external_proof_export.md).

<a id="d-301"></a>
## D-301 — mailed statements class-canonicalized once at the absorb drain, before both consumers (2026-08-20,, maintainer-directed)

> **Superseded by [D-326](#d-326) (2026-08-28):** the drain-side canonicalizer is deleted; the deposit door canonicalizes every non-goal, non-equality, non-anchor deposit at its own scope and the status-3 staging reads the door's returned row.

**Context.** The C_RT investigation's externalStatements-leak finding (`docs/fta_ladder/C_RT_investigation.md`): every mailed statement was consumed twice at the absorb drain — a class-disciplined registry offer through `addExprToMemoryBlock`, and a raw staging into `intExternalStatements` that request generation (batches 3/4) pairs directly. Non-canonical equivalence-class members mailed from an ancestor entered the phase-2 hashburst verbatim for one burst per arrival (measured live: burst-12 C15 hits citing members with 0 registry rows), bypassing the registry's one-representative collapse.

**Decision.** Canonicalize each status-3 arrival ONCE, at the drain, before BOTH consumers (`canonicalizeMailArrival`, [`prover.hpp`](../../GL_Quick_VS/GL_Quick/src/prover.hpp)): every non-canonical `int_`/`it_` member token rewrites to the class canonical (`firstSpecialMemberId` — lex-min `int_lev_*`, else lex-min `it_*_lev_*`); normal-name members are untouched, preserving the sanctioned theorem-term-plus-one-representative participation duality. Shape gates keep raw: equalities and negated equalities (the `addEquality` door + the I-12 expansion own them), anchors ([I-53](30_invariants.md#i-53)), the two status-3 rule-carrier shapes (`(implication…` compacts and negated compact existences `!(existence…`) whose identity belongs to [I-46](30_invariants.md#i-46), and or compacts ([I-167](30_invariants.md#i-167)); `skip_eq_classes` disables the pass. The staging push dedups collapsed rows by `(originalId, validityId)`; the registry offer receives the canonical form with the applied pairs' class levels unioned into the level run (the `{-1}` non-derived tier transparent to the union — leading marker stripped when real levels merge, restored as the singleton when every input was non-derived, per [I-182](30_invariants.md#i-182)'s never-mixed run); with `trackHistory`, the raw arrival keeps its mailed origin line and the canonical form gains one `equality1` bridge line (deps[0] = raw form, then the applied `(=[member,canonical])` justifiers), gated I-34-style.

**No duplication (maintainer directive).** The canonicalizer shares ONE sink-parameterized core with the registry's judge: `forEachNonCanonicalMemberToken` — `filterIterationsCore`'s view overload is its stop-at-first-hit wrapper (verdict, probe order, and `kindOf` lazy fills byte-identical, [I-134](30_invariants.md#i-134)), the canonicalizer its collecting wrapper. The token scan for un-interned arrivals is the factored memo-independent `buildSpecialTokenScanView` ([`memory.hpp`](../../GL_Quick_VS/GL_Quick/src/memory.hpp)), byte-identical to `tokensViewOf`'s miss build.

**Alternatives rejected.** Purging only the staging (registry offer left raw): a request fired from the canonical staged form could cite a premise form the registry never registered — the raw offer can still be swallowed by `addStatement`'s eqfilter with no canonical substitute (the C6-era gap) — a dangling-citation risk at export. Reusing the admission-key canonicalizer (the whole-member-set rewrite, since deleted): it pairs EVERY member, so a theorem term would be rewritten into the `int_` representative, and it collects no levels/justifiers for the Rule-16 history.

**Consequence.** The leak window closes — from an equivalence class at most one `int_`/`it_` member reaches a hashburst on the mail path too — and a mail arrival whose raw form is non-canonical now registers in canonical form instead of being swallowed by the eqfilter.

<a id="d-291"></a>
## D-291 — verdict-first drain order, producer-chain tiebreak, method-aware tier upgrade (2026-08-19,, maintainer-approved)

- **Context.** The tier branch's full-gate pair diverged (main-batch verifier totals 138390 vs 138412 on same input, same code) — the first genuine nondeterminism since the doom line landed. Log-only proof across three runs: the commutation-at-1 conjecture closes TWICE in the same iteration, deterministically — a level-complete record from the conjecture's chain LB and a level-poor record from its primed `__contradiction__` twin, both sealed as `UpdateGlobalDirectRec`s. The nondeterminism was the DRAIN: `updateGlobalDirectLess` ordered same-theorem records by `coreId` (the phase-dispatch worker slot — a scheduling race outcome) before the level verdict, and `appendGlobalTheorem`'s method-blind string dedup makes the first-drained record's method the registration. False record first → the theorem registered `proved not broadcast` and the first-class append was silently refused; true record first → the reverse. The comparator's own comment claimed the outcome was "order-insensitive (string dedup)" — true before the tier existed (a false verdict registered nothing), false the moment the tier made the refused path register. The losing true record still ran the full broadcast path, so the in-run proof state stayed byte-identical — only the ledger method flipped, then compressor probe 127 vs 128 → `theorems.txt` basis → next batch's externals → verifier totals, all deterministic consequences of the coin flip.
- **Decision.** Three coupled changes. (1) `updateGlobalDirectLess` orders same-theorem records by the sealed level verdict, TRUE FIRST — a level-complete closure always beats a level-poor one at the sink, matching the tier's intent (the tier is for theorems that never close level-complete). (2) `coreId` leaves the order entirely; the residual tiebreak is `compareProducerChains` — byte-lexicographic over the leaf-to-root `exprKey` chain, a pure function of proof state — because for a level-poor pair the first record's producer chain becomes the tier chapter's derivation, so a coreId residue would have made chapter content a race outcome. (3) `appendGlobalTheorem` becomes method-aware: an incoming first-class row UPGRADES an existing `proved not broadcast` row in place (method, aux columns, recorded producer; the tier's `fullTheoremList` mirror row leaves), and an incoming tier row never lands on an existing row of any method — order-insensitivity by construction, covering any residual path that registers first-class after a tier row exists.
- **Rejected.** Keeping the comparator's false-first verdict order (it deterministically hands a same-iteration pair to the tier — semantically backwards); fixing only the comparator without the method-aware sink (leaves the sink order-sensitive for any future multi-record source).
- **Where.** `prover.cpp::updateGlobalDirectLess` / `compareProducerChains` / `appendGlobalTheorem`; tests `test_memory.cpp::compare_producer_chains_is_deterministic_lb_identity` / `update_global_direct_order_verdict_beats_core_id`, `test_theorem_sink_dedup.cpp::tier_row_upgrades_to_first_class` / `tier_arrival_never_lands_on_existing_row`.

<a id="d-292"></a>
## D-292 — a doomed LB's tally leaves the straggler statistic (2026-08-19,, maintainer-approved)

- **Context.** Secondary finding of the same hunt: the burst-5 straggler line's total work `T` differed across all three runs (666524 / 666567 / 666687) while every content observable was byte-identical. An early-exited burst's parts stop at a timing-dependent overshoot strictly past the published doom line in their own streams — [I-191](30_invariants.md#i-191) protects the merged CONTENT (winner-only), not the submatch TALLIES — so a discharging LB's `lbTotalSub` is a race outcome. Folding it into `T` violated [I-160](30_invariants.md#i-160)'s letter (the split set as a pure function of proof state): a borderline straggler verdict could flip run to run.
- **Decision.** A per-iteration `lbDoomed` latch (set after each pass's join, because the per-pass `doomLines` reset would erase a pass-1 doom) excludes doomed LBs from BOTH the `T` sum and straggler classification; a doomed LB gets the unsplit default (it is discharging and never bursts again). Whether a doom trigger fires at all IS deterministic — the winning line's position is always reached by its part — so the exclusion restores the statistic to a pure function of proof state.
- **Where.** `prover.cpp::proveKernel` (the latch after the executor join; the end-of-iteration stats pass).

<a id="d-290"></a>
## D-290 — level-refused closures are recorded, never circulated (2026-08-19,, maintainer-directed)

- **Context.** The D-278 level gate refuses registration when a closure's derivation did not consume every premise level — previously a SILENT drop. The pre-split campaign surfaced that this is structural for guard variants: a degenerate branch (13b's `b=0`) collapses so hard that shared premises become redundant, so its proof legitimately skips a level and the variant vanishes — starving the merge. The same signature explains C14-forward's "stall" (its `1≤c` is redundant in the forward direction alone; its LB closed, `active_bodies=0`, nothing registered).
- **Decision (maintainer: "scope: everywhere").** In EVERY batch and mode, a level-refused closure registers as a `globalTheoremList` row with method `proved not broadcast` (producer recorded) and gets a real chapter (the ordinary direct-proof walk, chapter kind `proved_not_broadcast`). It NEVER circulates: no reformulation, no broadcast/compaction, no or-construction seeding (both seams skip the method), no compressor participation (excluded from the redundancy probe on both sides — an unbroadcast row must not subsume a first-class theorem — and protected from the survivor erase), and no `theorems.txt` row (the proved-theorems artifact stays first-class-only). Its one consumer is the pre-split merge, which may cite a tier row as a guard variant; the verifier resolves such citations through the global list like any theorem.
- **Why record at all.** The closure is a sound proof; the gate is registration hygiene (the stronger form should circulate), not a truth verdict. Recording makes a previously invisible failure class auditable and feeds the merge. Consequence accepted: chapters and check counts grow in every batch wherever refusals occurred silently before; the "category-identical" full-gate criterion retires for the landing run.
- **Where.** `prover.cpp::updateGlobalDirect` (the `registerGlobally == false` branch), the two or-seam skips, `run_modes.cpp` (compressor input + survivor erase + `theorems.txt` loop), `visualizer.cpp::generateRawProofGraph` (chapter branch), the Python pipeline's method dispatches, `verifier.py::check_theorem_goal_reached` (direct-family chapter type), `proof_export` (suffix map + direct-renderer acceptance).

<a id="d-289"></a>
## D-289 — pre-split merge: derived theorems via or elimination at the drain seam (2026-08-19,, maintainer-directed)

- **Context.** C13 (divisibility antisymmetry) needs a case split on a premise variable that no cohort opener can serve: every consumer of the `b=0` / `1≤b` disjuncts is a 2-premise rule below the demand gates, and the goal matches neither disjunct. The maintainer's standing branching method ("pre-split") applies whenever a lemma's bound input parameter must be split and the in-prover split cannot open.
- **Decision.** Prove the two guard variants as ordinary flat pool rows (guard premise INNERMOST and binder-free — the load-bearing authoring convention), then DERIVE the unguarded theorem by classical or-elimination at the phase-4 drain seam: `constructOrEliminationInRun` (immediately after `constructOrTheoremsInRun`, before the compaction drain) detects byte-identical-except-guard pairs, licenses them against a proved or theorem whose two disjuncts align with the guards under one variable bijection (literal polarity, I-175), rebuilds the merged theorem via `reconstructImplicationFullBind`, and registers it with the new method `or elimination` citing variant A / variant B in the row's aux slots and the or theorem in the `orElimCitedOrByMerged` side ledger. Licenseless pairs park on `orElimPendingPairs` and re-probe each iteration (an or theorem can mint later). k=2 disjuncts in the first build.
- **Pool model (the maintainer's explicit correction).** The full theorem is NEVER a pool conjecture — a pool copy would spin an LB the whole run for nothing, since the merge cannot fire before both variants prove. The merged theorem is a derived row exactly like or theorems; consequently NO goal closure and NO LB interaction exist at the seam. Unlike or theorems, the variants are NOT subsumed from `theorems.txt` — they stay first-class pool rows, re-proved every run.
- **Rejected.** (a) Widening cohort opening for low-premise consumers — the premise-count gates exist precisely to contain the historical RT explosion; (b) the full theorem as a pool row closed by the merge — RT waste plus a cross-LB closure channel for nothing; (c) accepting the guarded variants as the final form — the maintainer wants the full theorems on record.
- **Where.** `prover.cpp::constructOrEliminationInRun` / `findOrEliminationLicense` / `alignOrEliminationExprs`; the chapter writer's `or elimination` branch in `visualizer.cpp::generateRawProofGraph` + `TheoremUsageGraph::addEdgesFromStack`; the base-form save condition in `run_modes.cpp`. Verifier and Python-pipeline surfaces land in the follow-on commits of the same campaign. Plan: `docs/agentic_swdd/or_elimination_plan.md`.

<a id="d-288"></a>
## D-288 — untagged input-slot demand keys with an ancestor-inclusive Pass-B probe (2026-08-19,, maintainer-directed)


**The problem.** C8 (pool row 54, `d | a ∧ a + b = c ∧ d | c ⟹ d | b`) stalls at §7 of its human proof even after [D-287](#d-287) opens the `d = 0 ∨ 1 ≤ d` cohort and B9 fires (`docs/fta_ladder/C8/current_proof_state.md` Step 8). Every order/divisibility existence on the target LB has its witness MINTED by `disintegrateExpr2`, but the product — an `in3` atom with the witness at an INPUT slot, e.g. `(in3[int_lev_1_1,marker,int_lev_3_1,4])` for `x + z = y` — parks in `rejectedMap` with empty levels and is never released. Structural cause: the algebra demand language was OUTPUT-slot only. The regular admission-marker route always marks the missing premise's output arg (`installAdmissionMarkerVariants(..., outputArg,...)`), and the only input-slot marker producer was the ordis route, whose `ordisOnly`-tagged keys Pass-B is blind to by design ([I-177](30_invariants.md#i-177)). So a witness sitting at an input slot of a two-input operator had NO admission path: not the single-input standalone gate ([I-6](30_invariants.md#i-6)), not any installable untagged demand. (Output-slot witnesses — multiplication totality — and single-input-operator witnesses — the `in2` predecessor — both register; the Step-8 table is exactly this trichotomy.) An alternative repair — unconditionally widening the I-6 standalone gate to two-input operators — was tried and exploded RT (run killed at burst 6, 138,594 expressions, 129 s per sweep against a 190 s whole-run baseline): unconditional registration at every LB is the historically proven blow-up; demand-driven release is not.

**The decision (maintainer-directed).** Two deltas, both demand-side; the I-6 gate stays single-input.

1. **A fourth, independent qualification pass** in `makeNormalizedKeysForAdmission` (sibling of the [D-267](#d-267) ordis2 pass, running regardless of the regular/ordis routing): each premise input slot passing `inputSlotDemandSlotQualifies` installs an UNTAGGED marker variant via `installAdmissionMarkerVariants` — marked arg = the input-slot candidate, subkey = every other premise, anchor included. The predicate is the ordis input-slot candidate analysis on the algebra map: (1) the candidate also sits at a config input slot of the HEAD, (2) confinement — the candidate appears in no other key element, (3) concreteness — every other argument of the marked premise is bound by some other key element; plus the fan-out gate `kInputSlotDemandMinPremises` (= 4 non-anchor premises, mirroring `kOrdis2DemandMinPremises` — the D-267 RT lesson). Untagged means `isAdmitted` reads the fired keys and `revisitRejected2` wakes parked products — the full regular seam, unlike the or-cohort-evidence tag.
2. **An ancestor-inclusive Pass-B probe** — `isAdmittedIncludingAncestors`: exact deposit validity first (unchanged semantics), then the deposit scope's strict ancestors (`NameMap::strictAncestorSpans`, owned scratch copies per I-3), first hit winning, consumption at the validity that admitted. Needed because a fired key lands at `deeperOf(subkey constituents)` — for the C8 shape `main` — while the witness-minting disintegration deposits inside the released `_ordis_` branch; the exact-validity probe alone can never connect the two. Soundness is structural: the probe set is built from the deposit's own ancestor chain, so a hitting key is always at the deposit's scope or a parent of it.

**Why it closes C8 (the mental model).** Row 56 (difference transport, `d·x=a ∧ a+b=c ∧ d·y=c ∧ x+z=y ⟹ d·z=b`) qualifies at its `x + z = y` slot with candidate `z`: `z` feeds the head at an input slot, is confined to that premise, and `x`/`y` are bound by the product premises. The installed marker rule's subkey (anchor + three premises) matches facts live at `main` from the early bursts, so the marker branch fires and the [I-68](30_invariants.md#i-68) drain installs the INSTANTIATED key `(in3[int_lev_1_1,marker,int_lev_3_1,4])` at `main` — byte-identical to the marked form the branch's `x ≤ y` expansion probes with. Demand-first ordering holds (the cohort opens much later), so the witness registers instead of parking; row 56 fires in the branch; `d·z = b` matches the goal's standing integration demand; `d | b` closes in the `1 ≤ d` branch, and the `d = 0` branch's chain is available from proved material.

**Code.** `memory.cpp::inputSlotDemandSlotQualifies` + the fourth pass in `makeNormalizedKeysForAdmission`; `prover.hpp::isAdmittedIncludingAncestors`; the Pass-B call site in `prover.cpp::disintegrateExpr2`; `ExecutionParameters::kInputSlotDemandMinPremises`. Tests: `test_disintegration_allowed.cpp::input_slot_demand_slot_qualification_matrix` / `input_slot_demand_pass_installs_untagged_marker`, `test_memory.cpp::is_admitted_including_ancestors_walks_parent_scopes`.

**Risk accepted.** More marker rules install (premise-rich rules only) and Pass-B misses now walk the ancestor chain (non-minting probes, depth-bounded). Both are demand-driven and gated; RT is measured on the shortcut pool against the 190.7 s D-287 baseline.

## D-293 — the Lean export certifies each row against its own citation (2026-08-19,, maintainer-directed)


**Context.** The export emitted one named Lean fact per GL chapter row, but
1,799 of 7,622 rows closed with a bare `grind` over the entire enclosing
context, and the Peano corpus additionally closed all 617 of its implication
rows that way while its manifest already labelled them "ordered implication
elimination". A passing build therefore certified that each row followed from
something above it, not that GL's cited rule and premises produced it.

**Decision.** Implication elimination renders structurally in every corpus, and
every remaining searched row clears the uncited part of its context first.
Measured empirically before the change: with the rows deleted and all 57
definitions unfolded, `grind` alone closed 12 of 66 public Peano theorems — all
small direct ones — and failed on all 39 induction and all four OR theorems, so
Lean was never re-deriving the corpus; the exposure was per-row attribution.

**Alternatives rejected.** Restricting `grind`'s global theorem set (`grind
only`) does not touch the local context and would not have changed anything.
Leaving Peano on schema 2 was rejected because the certificate already records
the rule and premises for those 617 rows; only the renderer ignored them.

**Consequence.** 84.4% of rows are now explicit terms (was 76.4%), and all 1,190
remaining searched rows are context-restricted. The isolation immediately
exposed one Gauss row that had been closing through a route GL never recorded:
its two cited premises are scoped existence facts that GL states about one
shared witness, which the encoding had been quantifying separately. Scope
witnesses are now shared, which is what makes that row derivable from its own
citation.

**Cost.** Generated files grow by the `clear` lines. Scoped rows carry an
explicit scope-entry preamble instead of a one-line tactic.

<a id="d-287"></a>
## D-287 — an anchor-slot argument is ground for the ordis2 demand slot filter (2026-08-18, `main`, maintainer-directed)

**The problem.** C8 (pool row 54, `d | a ∧ a + b = c ∧ d | c ⟹ d | b`) stalls one atom short. B9 (`1 ≤ d ∧ x·d = a ∧ y·d = c ∧ a ≤ c ⟹ x ≤ y`, pool row 42) sits at the innermost premise LB with three of its four premises live, and the or `d = 0 ∨ 1 ≤ d` is parked in `rejectedMapOrdis2` under exactly the key it needs, `(preorder[1,4,6,9])`. The cohort never opens because `admissionMapOrdis2` is empty: no demand for that key is ever installed.

**Why it refused.** [D-267](#d-267)'s sharpened subset test requires every argument of the candidate slot to be bound by one of the rule's other NON-anchor premises. B9's slot `(preorder[1,4,6,9])` binds `9` through the two product premises and `1` / `4` through `(preorder[1,4,11,13])` — but `6`, the numeral 1, appears in no other non-anchor premise. It is an anchor slot, and the binder loop skips anchor premises by construction. A single constant in the slot therefore disqualified the whole order family of consumers.

**The decision (maintainer-directed).** An anchor-slot argument counts as bound. It is ground by construction — it names a fixed value of the anchor context (the numeral 1, the carrier set, an operator) — so no substantive premise can ever bind it, and requiring one is unsatisfiable rather than selective. The rest of D-267's filter stands unchanged: a non-anchor argument still needs a substantive binder, `ordis2KeyEligible` and the arity gate are untouched, and `kOrdis2DemandMinPremises` (= 4) still admits only premise-rich rules.

**The A14 shape stays excluded** by an explicit guard: at least one argument must come from a substantive premise, so a slot the anchor alone binds still mints no demand.

**Code.** `memory.cpp::ordis2DemandSlotQualifies`; declaration Doxygen in `prover.hpp`. Test: `tests/test_rejected_ordis.cpp::slot_qualification_matrix` — the anchor-only-argument case flips to qualifying, and a new all-anchor-arguments case pins the A14 exclusion.

**Risk accepted.** Demand installs more widely than D-267's sharpened form allowed. The RT explosion that sharpening guarded against was attributed to the missing minimum-premise-count gate, which stays in force; runtime is measured on the shortcut pool before and after.
