<a id="d-285"></a>
## D-285 — productsOfRecursionIds closed under main-scope equivalence-class membership (2026-08-18)

**Context.** The full pipeline lost both Gauss fold theorems. The from-scratch step-trace campaign (`docs/fta_ladder/C6/gauss_fold_main_proof.md` + `gauss_fold_step_match.md`, ) matched all 199 steps of main's successor-case proof against the branch: 194 exist there — including the fold integration and the induction-hypothesis firing — and exactly five are missing, one chain rooted at S49, the Σ(rec)+9 sum-witness registration. The [SUMT] A/B trap round then proved the mechanism on both sides at the marker-capture purity gate in `checkLocalEncodedMemoryStatic` (`pure` = every iteration-bearing premise argument ∈ `productsOfRecursionIds`, where products of recursion are the names built by eating the induction implication's premise cursors): main's sum demand is captured pure because its id-image premise cites main's locally-built, cursor-admitted witness; the branch's only surviving id-image instance cites the flag-5 relay's ancestor-minted witness — mailed in, never admitted locally, hence not a product of recursion — so every capture is refused, no demand is ever staged, and the parked sum witness sleeps forever. The gate operates correctly on both sides; the defect is the displacement: a mailed foreign witness-form became the sole surviving instance of induction-built content (the branch's own pure twin was removed by the class/door canonicalization handling).

**Decision (maintainer-designed).** A name proven equal to a product of recursion is one: at the single-threaded `standardProcessing` seam, immediately after the `applyEquiClasses` fixpoint, `enrichProductsOfRecursionFromChangedClasses` walks `changedClassesThisStep` and, for every MAIN-scope class holding at least one `productsOfRecursionIds` member, mints every other member into the set. Write-side closure was chosen over a read-side class probe in the purity check to keep the phase-2 hot path at a plain `contains` probe. Non-main scopes are excluded — a conditional (hypothesis / boundary) equality must not enrich the LB-global set.

**Known limitation** (documented in [I-194](30_invariants.md#i-194)): a member that joins `productsOfRecursionIds` only after its class's last change of a step is not retroactively closed over — acceptable because both mint sites fire on the induction cursors before the relevant classes form.

## D-300 — the algebra admission-key cleanup is switched off behind one entry gate (2026-08-18,, maintainer-directed)

- **Context.** The C6 Gauss-fold investigation traced a lost theorem to admission-key consumption: `cleanAdmissionMap` erased a key the moment its head fired, and the [D-62](#d-62) canonicalization closure extended that erase over every same-scope key with the same canonical form. Consumption is permanent, so a key that is also an induction implication's premise cursor dies at its first match and the implication can never advance through that slot (state doc Step 12).
- **Decision.** Rather than redesign the cleanup, switch the whole thing off behind ONE entry gate — the smallest change that answers the only open question: what is the machinery actually buying? Nothing else moved.
- **Measured.** The full-pipeline A/B came back runtime-flat — 1171.32 s → 1171.59 s overall, every leg inside noise — with the verifier airtight and no theorem gained or lost by the switch.
- **Exit criterion, stated up front.** If runtime stays flat, delete the machinery rather than ship a permanently-false switch: an off switch is dead weight that still has to be read, statified, deloaded and dumped, and its inert reader gates read as live contracts.
- **Not on main.** The gate itself never merged; the branch stands as the experiment's record.
- **Superseded by [D-299](#d-299) on 2026-08-22**, which took that exit and deleted `cleanAdmissionMap`, the `consumedAdmissionKeys` cold set and `canonicalizeUnderClasses` outright. Contract: [I-200](30_invariants.md#i-200).

<a id="d-286"></a>
## D-286 — canonicalization-dropped delta rows ship their origin history before the drop (2026-08-17)

**Context.** The chapter export aborted on `buildStack: no origin found` for `(=[it_0_lev_1_192,2]) @main` at a born-parked induction-zero LB (C6 state doc Step 10, trap-proven). The mechanism: `cleanUpExpressions`' `filterIterations` sweep drops statements carrying a non-canonical equivalence-class member from `intLocalEncodedStatements` AND `intLocalEncodedStatementsDelta`, and the sweep runs earlier than `fillMailOut` in the same phase-3 `standardProcessing` call — so a statement registered and dropped within one burst is never walked by any mail pass, and neither its statement nor its origin rows ever reach `mailOut`. Meanwhile `applyEquivalenceClass`'s `equality1` rewrite rows citing that statement DO mail (the emitter's citation-closure assert checks only the LOCAL origin map, legitimately). A receiver that cannot re-derive the cited statement — an induction-zero block that only catch-up-absorbs mail — holds a permanently dangling citation. The gap is pre-existing; the flag-5 relay's witness minting at level-1 LBs (D-284) created its first exposed instance.

**Decision (maintainer-approved P2).** For each delta row the sweep drops, `cleanUpExpressions` calls the existing `copyOriginRowsToMailOut` (all scopes, same cap expression as the `fillMailOut` delta loop) BEFORE the drop. The statement itself stays unmailed — the canonicalization policy (non-canonical statements do not propagate) is unchanged; only the row's origin history travels. This restores the closure invariant the mail origin mirror is built on: every dependency cited by a shipped origin row has its own origin rows shipped. The copy is process documentation, never a proof input (Rule 16 / [I-44](30_invariants.md#i-44)).

**Alternatives rejected.** Full ship-before-drop (statement + origins) would mail non-canonical statements — a canonicalization-policy change with unknown blowup; an export-side `buildStack` parent-chain fallback would resolve only receivers whose ancestors happen to re-derive the citation and leaves the producer-side closure gap open.

**See also.** [I-26](30_invariants.md#i-26) (amended), [I-58](30_invariants.md#i-58) (the sweep's levels/known retention), [`20_core_concepts/03_mail_system.md`](20_core_concepts/03_mail_system.md), `docs/fta_ladder/C6/current_proof_state.md` Step 10.

<a id="d-284"></a>
## D-284 — parent-level mail pass + flag-5 disintegration relay (2026-08-17)

**Context.** C6 (sum closure of divisibility) stalled 51/52 behind four co-sufficient gates (`docs/fta_ladder/C6/current_proof_state.md`): the sum-witness existence head fires at the level-2 LB but carries two distinct `int_lev` witnesses and the mail shape gate categorically refused multi-token expressions (Gap B); witness admission demand is LB-local and unplantable at the deriving LB (Gap C); a mailed positive existence never disintegrates at the receiver (Gap D); and the demand LB cannot fire a mail rule on an all-mailed premise set (Gap A). Every earlier ladder row escaped because its witness-bearing compact was the LAST premise, disintegrated locally at the goal LB.

**Decision (maintainer design).** Two parts. **(1) Parent-level mail pass:** an expression whose `int_lev` tokens all carry a level strictly below the LB's own level is mailable unconditionally — such names arrived by ancestor mail and every ancestor deposit reaches all deeper descendants directly, so they are known below by construction (the prior refusal of mail-arrived premises was a bug; it broke the `allGood` transitive-mailability chain for heads fired over mailed premises). **(2) Flag-5 relay:** when a local (status-0/1) disintegration leaves an existence group without any admitted witness, the highest such compact (uncovered group whose enclosing group is covered, or the top compound) is mailed with statement flag 5 ("external, may be disintegrated") on a side column; a receiver runs it through `disintegrateExpr2` with witness minting (new door status 5), registers the carrier itself NON-local (never re-forwarded), registers admitted products LOCAL (mailable, batch-2/5-visible), and never re-stages a relay from a status-3/5 disintegration (delivery already reached all descendants — no cascade).

**Consequence.** The deriving ancestor fires the witness rule (one premise is always local at the deepest-minting LB), the head relays down, and the demand-holding descendant mints its own witness against its parked marker — Gaps B, C, D each get a door and Gap A is bypassed. Mint volume stays bounded: relays exist only for parked compounds, products stay demand-gated at every receiver, generation caps unchanged.

**See also.** [I-195](30_invariants.md#i-195), [`20_core_concepts/03_mail_system.md`](20_core_concepts/03_mail_system.md#the-shape-gate-allowedformail), [I-26](30_invariants.md#i-26), [I-57](30_invariants.md#i-57), [I-171](30_invariants.md#i-171).

<a id="d-283"></a>
## D-283 — the split stump is a search NODE, not a membership filter (2026-08-14)

**Context.** The LB expression split dealt a producer's stumps into `logicalCores` buckets, and a bucket's run attached its stump to every freely-grown candidate for the two owner-set probes. A request belonged to the bucket whose stump it CONTAINED. Containment is not exclusive: a candidate set `K` contains one stump per element (the producer stops at level 1 whenever the filter yields at least `kStumpsPerBucketTarget * logicalCores` statements, which is the normal case), so `K` was re-derived once per element — the split inflated total work by the mean accepted-candidate size.

**Measured on the FTA shortcut list (44 conjectures, 32 logical cores), hash burst 25:**

| | wall | phase-2 CPU-s | submatches | parallelism |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| split (containment) | 64.6 s | 1368 | 3 458 177 | 24.9 |
| unsplit | 67.3 s | 189 | 1 283 571 | 2.8 |

8.9x more parallelism spent paying 7.25x more work, for 1.23x wall clock. The inflation factor was confirmed against a direct measurement of mean accepted-candidate size, per LB, to within 4.2%. It grew through the run as keys got larger — 1.00x at burst 3, 1.59x at 10, 1.96x at 17, 2.69x at 25 — and it capped the split's ceiling at `logicalCores / meanSize`.

**Decision.** A stump NAMES A NODE of the same depth-first search. The run seeds its stack with the stump as the growing candidate and its cursor past the stump's last filtered-list position, then grows it exactly as the unsplit search grows any node. A run owns that node's SUBTREE. Since the search extends only in ascending position, every candidate has one path from the root, so the stumps' subtrees are disjoint and cover the unsplit enumeration exactly: the split becomes a PARTITION and generates the identical request set, once each. Termination is structural (children push `start = i + 1`, so a run cannot climb out of its subtree).

**Result on the same list.** Overall runtime 218.9 s to 128.97 s (1.70x). Burst 25 65.5 s to 25.2 s, its submatch total exactly the unsplit 1 283 571. 45 theorems, verifier 0 failures, check count matching the unsplit path.

**Alternatives considered.** Cross-bucket request dedup (pays memory and a synchronisation point to remove work that never needed doing); affinity dealing so overlapping grow trees land in one bucket (shrinks the overlap, cannot remove it); bounding bucket count by predicted efficiency (caps the loss instead of fixing it).

**Consequence.** Load balance changes character and is now the binding constraint. Subtree size falls steeply with list position, so buckets are inherently uneven where the retired scheme made every bucket grow the whole universe. On burst 25 the busiest bucket runs about 2x fair share and the split-ineffective report fires. Round-robin dealing already spreads each bucket's draw across the whole sorted list; dealing by descending predicted subtree size is the next lever.

**See also.** [I-156](30_invariants.md#i-156), [I-155](30_invariants.md#i-155), [I-157](30_invariants.md#i-157), [I-158](30_invariants.md#i-158), [D-109](#d-109), [D-201](#d-201), [D-202](#d-202), [D-203](#d-203).

<a id="d-282"></a>
## D-282 — the burst early-exit works for split LBs: a doom trigger publishes its deterministic stream position, every part stops at that line, and the merge takes the winning part's chain alone (2026-08-13,, user-designed)


**The problem.** [I-76](30_invariants.md#i-76) disabled the burst early-exit ([D-121](#d-121)) whenever an LB ran as more than one part, because siblings bailing on a shared boolean stop flag cut each other at timing-dependent points — the firing set, and with it the proved-theorem set, depended on scheduling. The escape clause was "the skipped requests are wasted-once-doomed, so the suppression costs nothing"; the B10 RT investigation falsified that at scale (`docs/fta_ladder/B10_RT_investigation.md` §4): burst 26 of the B10 shortcut ground 877 k submatches across 32 buckets for 16.6 s AFTER its goal had already fired, where the single-part control finished in 0.77 s — ~15.8 s of pure wasted-once-doomed work per such burst, recorded as fix lever 4 ("deterministic staged doom-stop for split blocks").

**The design (user-proposed, refined together).** The user's core insight: if only ONE part's output merges, the sibling parts' timing-dependent bail points stop mattering — they shape wall-clock, never output. The original proposal picked the winner among parts that early-exited within an X-millisecond margin by natural (invocation) order; the margin was replaced during analysis because margin MEMBERSHIP is itself wall-clock (whether a slower part exits inside the window varies run to run, so the winner — and the merged bytes — would too; the same wall-clock ban [I-160](30_invariants.md#i-160) records for the split trigger). The deterministic replacement measures the margin in each part's own progress instead of milliseconds:

1. **Publish.** A part whose fired head trips `burstDeactivates` publishes `(its own submatch counter, its invocation ordinal)` onto the LB's shared external doom line — one packed `int64` atomic, lowered only by CAS-min, so near-simultaneous triggers both publish and the lexicographic minimum survives regardless of arrival order.
2. **Stop.** Every part stops once its OWN counter lies strictly past the line's position (strictly — a position-tie trigger from an earlier ordinal must still get published). A part earlier in its stream than the line keeps working up to it: that catch-up is exactly the run-length that makes the winner well-defined without wall-clock.
3. **Merge.** The finalize hands `applyFiringRecords` ONLY the winning part's chain; the losing chains are freed unread (the I-135 drop-unread path). The winner's chain is its deterministic stream prefix up to its own trigger; the losers' chains end wherever the line caught them, which is why they must not merge.

The winner is provably the first part in (trigger position, invocation order) whose uninterrupted stream contains a doom trigger — a pure function of proof state: the line's position never drops below the winning position, so the winner can never be cut before its own trigger. Soundness rides D-121's existing guarantee that `burstDeactivates` mirrors the phase-3 discharge exactly (never over-exits, [D-222](#d-222)): the LB discharges regardless, so every culled record — the winner's tail and the losers' whole chains — is wasted-once-doomed. An unsplit LB is its own winner (ordinal 0, full chain), so single-part behavior is unchanged, and the CE filter / incubator run single-part as before. `g_isMultiPart` had no reader left and is deleted; [I-76](30_invariants.md#i-76) and the early-exit half of [I-159](30_invariants.md#i-159) are superseded by [I-191](30_invariants.md#i-191).

**Accepted consequences.** A split LB that dooms mid-burst now records FEWER incidental derivations (only the winner's pre-trigger records instead of every part's full output) — the proof graph gets leaner on exactly those LBs and verifier check counts shift, the same acceptance shape as D-121's original −732; `theorems.txt` must stay byte-identical and two same-config runs must stay byte-identical throughout. The end-of-iteration split statistic sees the culled (smaller) submatch totals — deterministic, and irrelevant to the doomed LB itself (it discharges) while shifting other LBs' fair-share bar deterministically.

**Verification (final, 2026-08-13).** Unit tests 1456/1456 (`doom_line_packing_and_cas_min`, `burst_sink_stops_on_the_doom_line_for_every_part`, `phase2_finalize_merges_only_the_winner_on_a_doom_line`). Shortcut RT on the 46-row pool: prover wall 228.89 → 211.56 s (−17.3 s); the baseline's 18.7 s `swept=3` doomed split burst vanishes from the burst timeline while every other heavy burst reproduces within noise; 45/46 saved on both sides (row 29's close-without-register by design) and every tracked shortcut artifact byte-identical. Full pipeline: every tracked artifact byte-identical to the branch point (theorem files, incubator pools 1036/156/204/49/8, compressor outputs); verifier airtight — incubator graph 122317/0 unchanged, main graph 16387 → 16371 (−16 net, the anticipated winner-only-merge reshaping of incidental derivations in the untracked proof graph: implication −5, expansion +4, disintegration +3, task formulation −2, equality2 +1, symmetry −1, theorem citations −3, definition-set/origin-chain −3 each, origin −7), total 138688/0. Determinism gate (maintainer-directed criterion): two sequential full runs with EVERY verifier category line identical across both graphs and zero tracked-artifact churn in both.

<a id="d-281"></a>
## D-281 — retain the anchor and leave normalization unchanged

**Context.** Derivative admission rules are extracted from actual rules by selecting one non-anchor premise as missing and keying on the retained premises. Dropping an actual rule's anchor erased which anchor slot a variable in a retained premise referred to, allowing a request with the same alpha-shape but a different anchor-slot relationship to match.

**Decision.** Every regular, `ordisOnly`, and `ordis2Demand` derivative extracted from an anchored actual rule retains the anchor premise. The anchor itself is never selectable as missing. All eligibility counts and binding qualifications keep their existing non-anchor semantics; only the installed derivative key gains anchor context. The ordinary normalizer processes that complete key unchanged.

**Alternatives rejected.** Pinning anchor literals during normalization and converting anchor variables in subkeys to `u_` both duplicate information already expressed by retaining the anchor, add request-side asymmetry, and widen the change into normalization and persisted key semantics. Retaining context is sufficient because normalization preserves equality classes.

**Consequence.** Correctly alpha-renamed anchored requests still match. Rebinding a retained premise from one anchor slot to another produces a different key. Unanchored rules use the identical extraction and normalization behavior they had before.

**See also.** [I-193](30_invariants.md#i-193) and [`20_core_concepts/02_hash_engine.md`](20_core_concepts/02_hash_engine.md#two-encodedmap-insertion-sites-head-lmvs-vs-marker-lmvs).

<a id="d-280"></a>
## D-280 — the parked-map equi-class rewrite hooks union the fired pairs' levels into the mailed deposit (2026-08-13,, maintainer-approved)


**The problem.** The four parked-map equi-class rewrite hooks (`applyEquivalenceClassToRejectedMap` / `...RejectedMapIntegration` / `...RejectedMapOrdis` / `...RejectedMapOrdis2`) mailed the rewritten compound with ONLY the pre-rewrite form's level run; the justifying equalities went into the `equality1` history record but their levels were dropped — violating the chapter's own design principle ("a fact derivable through equality at level L is itself at level L"), which the main `applyEquivalenceClass` sink honors by merging `r.extraLevels` from the class's `intEqualityLevelsMap`. A pre-existing accounting defect, invisible while the twin route registered level-blind; the levels-gate campaign exposed it: B5's complement twin converged with collision union `{0,1,2}` at level 5 — the derivation chain went `!(=[it_30,2]) ← equality1 ←!(=[it_30,it_82]) {0,1,2} + (=[it_82,2]) {0,1,3,4,5}` with the child stored as `{0,1,2}`, so the reductio's genuinely-consumed product levels 3,4 never reached the colliding pair and the verdict refused a legitimate proof (with B7/B10 starving downstream: B5's broadcast rule is the ordis2 demand that opens their or0 cohorts). Traced mechanically: dump ancestry walk of the colliding pair (maintainer-directed method) plus the `[CLASS-PAIRS]` probe proving the STORED pair levels full `{0,1,3,4,5}` — convicting the union-skipping deposit, not the stamping.

**The decision.** In all four hooks, build the deposit run in a stack buffer: the parked run (`insertLevelSorted`, `{-1}` tier transparent) unioned with `clss.forEachLevel(packEqPairKey(fromId, toId))` for every substitution pair that ACTUALLY fired on the compound (same fired-pair detection as the `equality1` justifier tail; ids via non-minting `nameMap.lookup`, asserted interned). **A fifth site turned out to be the live producer of the B5 leak** (the first acceptance run still saved 40, and the fresh trace's new `intEqualityLevelsMap` dump section proved the pair full `{0,1,3,4,5}` from dump #8 while the narrow row appeared at #14): the I-12 negated-equality expansion `applyEquivalenceClassToNegatedEquality`, whose `emitNew` deposited each substituted variant through `addStatement` with only the SOURCE negation's run. Fixed the same way — `emitFromClassesAt` collects the justifying pair's stored levels from the class view (`eqc.forEachLevel(packEqPairKey(aId|bId, mid))`, stack copy) and threads them through `emitScratch` → `emitNew`, which merges them into the deposit run. The pre-levels-only forwarding of the two pre==post revival doors (`emitIntegrationRevivalToInternalMailIn` production callers, ordis revival) is untouched — no rewrite, nothing to union. The rule-rewrite sanitize path (`sanitizeHashMemory` family, old-rule levels forwarded) is deliberately NOT widened in this change — rule installation levels have their own semantics (I-51 mail emptiness, firing-time propagation); flagged as an open question rather than changed blind.

**Verification (final, 2026-08-13).** Unit `prover.apply_equi_rejected_mails_union_of_pair_levels` (parked `{0}` + pair `{1,3}` → mailed `{0,1,3}`). Acceptance ladder all green: 44-pool Saved 43 (row 29 the designed sole refusal; B5 twin `union={0,1,2,3,4}` verdict=1; census 0; verifier 5980/0); 46-pool Saved 45 (census 0; 6628/0; corrected row present, over-premised absent); full pipeline 138704/0 airtight with the theorem delta REVIEWED AND ACCEPTED by the maintainer — the fix RECOVERED `1·a=a` (a pre-existing silent G-46-class casualty of the dropped levels) and deterministically swapped the registered orientation of `0+a=a`; zero losses, all incubator batch counts byte-equal (1036/156/204/49/8), Gauss and rung-1/2 families intact. Determinism gate: two full runs, 5,298 artifact files byte-identical, verifier tallies identical.

**See also.** [D-278](#d-278) (the exposing change), [I-37](30_invariants.md#i-37) (drop+mail discipline), [I-88](30_invariants.md#i-88) (class pair-levels), `docs/agentic_swdd/20_core_concepts/05_equivalence_classes.md` steps 6/4.

<a id="d-278"></a>
## D-278 — the levels gate moves from goal discharge to global-list registration, on every route including the twins (2026-08-13,, maintainer-directed)


**The problem.** Problem 2 of the B10 §7b resolution: `allLevelsInvolved` guarded the whole non-recursion discharge in `dischargeToBeProved`, so a goal whose head arrived with a legitimately narrow level run could never close — a naturally-produced over-premised conjecture holds its LB chain active forever (the B10 undead chain). Meanwhile the contradiction-twin route emitted with NO level accounting at all, so the same over-premised row still registered through the level-blind twin — the gate's artifact-fidelity purpose (an emitted implication must have consumed every premise level) was enforced on the wrong axis in both directions.

**The decision (maintainer-directed, both halves in one change).**

1. **Closure is level-free.** `dischargeToBeProved`'s non-recursion MAIN branch drops `allLevelsInvolved` from its gate: theorem-bytes construction, record seal, goal-row erase, scope-wipe mint, and twin retirement run on `isProved && MAIN` alone — mirroring the recursion branch, which always had this shape (closure unconditional, the level bit riding `updateGlobalTuples` to `updateGlobal`'s promotion gate).
2. **Registration is level-gated on every route.** `UpdateGlobalDirectRec` carries a sealed `bool allLevelsInvolved`; `drainUpdateGlobalDirect` forwards it into `updateGlobalDirect(…, registerGlobally)`, which runs the two `deactivateUnnecessary` lifecycle walks and then returns BEFORE every registration surface (reformulation, `appendGlobalTheorem`, broadcast, compaction staging, mail merge) when the verdict is false. The D-240 settled-goal seed deposit stays unconditional for non-vacuous primed records. `dischargeContradiction`'s primed branch now seals its own verdict: union of the colliding pair's level rows, EXCLUDING the twin's own level (the assumed seed's tier), against the same count-based full-run test — the theorem's premise chain occupies levels `0..twin.level-1` in all three twin geometries, so one formula covers them. Seal-time computation from the twin's resident rows was maintainer-picked over a drain-time parent-side head-row probe, which misses whenever the head was never derived at the parent (every ordinary disproof) and can dangle across end-of-burst sanitize.

**Accepted consequences (maintainer-stated).** (i) A later level-complete re-derivation no longer triggers registration through the erased goal row — the narrower theorem is the conjecturer's to restate. (ii) An over-premised conjecture proves-but-does-not-register on EVERY route: shortcut pool row 29 (the `in[9,1]` over-premise) becomes the standing close-without-register reproduction case, the corrected one-premise-level row is appended (row 46) so the theorem itself stays provable, and B11's row 45 returns — a 46-row pool registers 45 BY DESIGN. (iii) Twin refutations (disproofs) are level-gated identically; a full-run theorem-set delta from a premise-subset reductio is a stop-and-report to the maintainer, never a silent acceptance.

**Verification (final, 2026-08-13).** Units `prover.level_poor_goal_closes_without_registering` / `prover.level_complete_goal_seals_registration_verdict` / `prover.contradiction_twin_seal_carries_level_verdict`. The first acceptance attempt FAILED (Saved 42 of 45 on the 46-pool; B5/B7/B10 lost) and exposed the pre-existing equality1 level-propagation defect fixed by [D-280](#d-280) — see that entry for the diagnosis chain. With both changes in: 46-pool Saved 45 (over-premised absent, corrected present, census 0, verifier 6628/0); full pipeline 138704/0 airtight, theorem delta accepted (+`1·a=a` recovered, one orientation swap, zero losses); determinism gate byte-identical across two full runs.

**See also.** [D-279](#d-279) (fix 1 of the same three-problem resolution), I-192 in [30_invariants.md](30_invariants.md#i-192), [I-51](30_invariants.md#i-51), [I-165](30_invariants.md#i-165), `docs/fta_ladder/B10_RT_investigation.md` §7b.

<a id="d-279"></a>
## D-279 — the settled-goal drain closes the PROOF direction: a contradiction-twin proof erases the parent's MAIN goal with success semantics (2026-08-12,, maintainer-directed)


**The problem.** [D-240](#d-240)'s drain settled only the DISPROOF direction (seed == parent MAIN goal); a complement twin's seed — `negate(goal)` — was the documented "defined no-op", on the assumption that normal closure (broadcast re-fire → `dischargeToBeProved`) retires a proved goal. The B10 RT investigation (`docs/fta_ladder/B10_RT_investigation.md` §7) proved the uncovered quadrant twin-PROVES × head-LEVEL-POOR: a contradiction-scope proof can deposit the goal's head with a legitimately narrow level run (row 29's `!(strictOrder[1,4,9,10])` arrives at `(=[9,10])@main` with `levels={2}` — the reductio never consumes the level-1 typing premise), the `allLevelsInvolved` gate then never fires, the theorem emits level-free through the primed twin, and nothing retires the local goal row — the goal's LB chain stays active to batch end (4 undead blocks on the 44-row pool, every I-48 sweep refusing forever).

**The fix.** In `ExpressionAnalyzer::drainDisprovedGoals`, per seed, alongside the existing disproof probe: probe `negate(seed)` (the emitted theorem's head, I-165) against the parent's MAIN goals, non-minting. On a hit the goal SUCCEEDED — erase the goal row and stage the goal-embedding MAIN scope roots (the same three shapes as the disproof branch, single-sourced in the shared `forEachGoalScopeRoot` lambda) on `pendingWipeScopes` + `intValidityNamesToFilter`, and nothing else: no origin erase (Rule 16 / I-44 — a proved goal's history stays like any proved statement's), no gate/cohort erase, no closed-subproof exception (those are disproof-only scrubbing of a dead goal's machinery). Emission and twin retirement already happened at the deposit seam (`drainUpdateGlobalDirect` → `deactivateUnnecessary`). With the row gone, the same iteration's `deactivateRecursively` retires the now-goal-less LB chain bottom-up (I-48).

**Deliberate non-actions.** No change to `dischargeToBeProved`'s level gate (Problem 2 of the §7b resolution, a separate fix), no walker changes, no emission from the drain (the theorem is already global), and the disproof branch is untouched.

**Verification.** Unit `prover.drain_settles_proved_goal_via_negated_seed` (both seed orientations; gates + origins survive; sibling goal untouched). Branch acceptance (measured, deterministic across two trap-free reruns): shortcut 44/44, main batch fully inactive at batch end (final burst `active_bodies=0`; the census trap measured 0 vs baseline 4 before its removal), verifier airtight, theorem file byte-identical across runs; full pipeline airtight with byte-identical theorems and identical per-batch pool counts. One sanctioned count shift: `operator registry consistency` drops by the spontaneous compact names the wiped dead machinery no longer mints (shortcut 206→200; full 1732→1729, registry merges `IncubatorPeano2 +162→+161`, `Peano +143→+141`) — every other verifier category identical.

**See also.** [D-240](#d-240) (the disproof direction + deposit seam), [I-165](30_invariants.md#i-165), [I-48](30_invariants.md#i-48), `docs/fta_ladder/B10_RT_investigation.md` §7b.

<a id="d-277"></a>
## D-277 — buildStack's D-51 twin switch requires the twin to hold a record (2026-08-12,, maintainer-picked Option A)


**The problem.** Both D-51 contradiction-fallback sites in `buildStack` switched into a `__contradiction__` twin unconditionally. A twin primes per unproved head (`try_contradiction` / `try_contradiction_negated_head`) and may run without ever converging — such a twin holds no discharge record for the head. Switching into it is never a resolution: the twin's entry finds no origin, its self-guard blocks re-entry, and the entry-side `no origin found` assert kills the export. B10 (strict reflection, `a·c < b·c ⟹ a < b`) hit this on its first acceptance run: the origin log legitimately contains a recorded-history cycle (head ← `≤∧≠⟹<` rules ← `!(=[9,12])` ← disintegration ← definitional conjunction ← expansion ← head), the walker entered it through the D-49-first cyclic candidate, the degraded last-resort emit recursed unfiltered back into the head, and the head's post-loop fallback switched into its never-converged reductio twin — asserting one backtrack level below ~30 perfectly acyclic `contradiction` records for `!(=[9,12])@main` (the or0[9,12] `=`-branch refutations) that the unwind would have reached. Diagnosis trail: three trap runs, full write-up in `docs/fta_ladder/B10/current_proof_state.md`. The D-276 admissibility check was exonerated (zero involvement).

**The decision (maintainer-picked Option A, minimal).** A resolution guard, `ExpressionAnalyzer::contradictionLbHoldsRecord`: before either fallback site switches, probe that the twin actually holds ≥1 origin record for the lifted `(proved, validity)` — read-only reload (D-158), lift within the twin, non-minting key probe (I-91), non-empty run; the exact mirror of `buildStack`'s entry-side origin check. Record present → switch exactly as before. Record absent → the fallback does not apply: the entry site falls through to the loud assert (a genuine provenance gap stays loud, Rule 19), the post-loop site falls through to the degraded front-emit + `false` return so callers backtrack to their remaining candidates. Strictly fewer LB switches than before, never more; runs that exported before are untouched (the guard only changes runs that previously died on the assert).

**Rejected (Option B, offered as companion).** D-49 demotion of disintegration-from-own-compound candidates — ordering/performance only, not required for correctness once the guard lands; not implemented.

**See also.** D-51 (fallback + cycle filter), D-49 (candidate order), D-236/D-224 (twins prime per head and may retire unconverged), [I-165](30_invariants.md#i-165), `docs/fta_ladder/B10/current_proof_state.md`.

<a id="d-276"></a>
## D-276 — verifier check + buildStack admissibility for inter-chapter theorem-usage cycles (2026-08-12,, user-directed)


**The problem.** Statements carry multiple origins precisely so the chapter exporter's stack builder can pick a non-cyclic derivation, and the D-51 path-stack filter defeats cycles *within* one chapter — but a `theorem`-tagged origin is recorded with an empty dependency vector, so a used theorem is a foundation leaf and cycles *between* chapters were never controlled. Live consequence: the mirrored Peano inequality pair (sources 24/25, processed chapters 58/59) each proved solely by one application of the other; every per-chapter check passed; one of the two shipped in `theorems.txt`. D-275's Lean export had to exclude exactly these two sources.

**The decision.** Two layers, verifier first (user-fixed order; the failing verifier on the then-current artifacts was the check's definition of done).

1. **Verifier: `theorem usage termination`** — a global meta-check in `run_verifier` (pattern: `check_operator_registry_consistency`) that literally builds the directed theorem-usage graph (node = chapter-owning theorem, edge A → B = "A's chapter cites B", edges from `theorem` rows plus non-locally-originated citation cells resolved with the `origin` check's fallback ladder) and runs the same WHITE/GRAY/BLACK depth-first cycle detection as the chapter-local `origin chain termination`; one record per theorem, failure = on a cycle. See the [`theorem usage termination` meta-check](10_pipeline/08_verifier.md#theorem-usage-termination-meta-check).
2. **buildStack: online cross-chapter admissibility** — the sequential chapter-export loop maintains a per-export `TheoremUsageGraph`; while building the chapter of theorem T, a candidate origin tagged `theorem` citing U is admissible only if U does not already reach T in the committed graph (U = T included); inadmissible candidates are skipped exactly like path-cyclic ones, falling through to backtracking → contradiction-LB fallback → degraded last-resort emit (which the new check then flags). Edges commit per chapter after its file is written (`writeStackIndexed`), including the synthetic-chapter citation channels (`reformulated from`, `incubator back reformulation`, `or theorem`). All of T's edges start at T, so committed-graph acyclicity plus the reaches-check keeps the graph acyclic with no rollback during backtracking.

**Why this shape.** Emission order is theorem-*discovery* order, not usage order — 81 legitimate forward citations exist in the main graph, so a linear "only cite earlier theorems" rule would be far too strict. The online reachability check bans exactly the citations that would close a cycle, and chapter granularity is complete: chapters connect only through theorem-citation leaves, so global derivation acyclicity = per-chapter acyclicity (D-51) + theorem-usage-graph acyclicity.

**Outcome (2026-08-12 full-pipeline run).** The cycle is eliminated: the surviving mirror's chapter derives its theorem genuinely (symmetry-of-inequality + equality chains from an `implication11` rule disintegrated out of the anchor's `NaturalNumbers` definition), the other mirror — never in `theorems.txt`, alive only as the circular chapter's dependency — is correctly pruned from the processed graph (93 distinct theorems, was 94). Verifier: main graph 16639 checks / 0 failures (`theorem usage termination` 93/0, was 92/2), incubator 122333 / 0 (1455/0), grand total 138972 / 0 — airtight. `theorems.txt` byte-identical across the fix. The degraded-emit contingency (a cycle member with no alternative origin) did not materialize. A full determinism rerun reproduced every artifact byte-identically (raw + processed proof graphs, theorems, GL binaries, HTML exports, incubator equivalents — 5,028 files hashed on both sides) with identical verifier tallies.

**Lean follow-through (2026-08-12).** The full Peano corpus now exports with ZERO exclusions: selection `peano_full_66` (sources 0–65, 66 theorems / 144 chapters / 3,276 rows) builds its certificate and passes the pinned `lake build` — retiring D-275's forced exclusion of the cycle members. Two latent `proof_export` defects surfaced and were fixed on the way, both pre-dating this campaign: `_constructed_or_definition`'s FTA-era refactor demanded literal negation premises in the parent walks (the blind-`!` consumer bug [I-175](30_invariants.md#i-175) forbids — the shipped full-65 certificate was generated by the earlier cancellation-correct code and never rebuilt), and the schema-2 corpus writer asserted a NON-empty exclusion list (a contingent leftover of the cycle era). The FTA dependency pins were repaired the same day: `fta_shortlist_42.json` repinned to the tracked dependency-certificate bytes (the tracked FTA certificate carried the same stale pins, proving the dependency certificates were regenerated after the FTA export and never repinned), the tracked FTA certificate + modules regenerated from the live shortcut graph (whose manifest reproduced the pinned sha byte-identically), and the full tracked `lean_export` re-passed `lake build` — the whole 19-test export suite is green on a pristine checkout again.

**Family migration (2026-08-12, same day).** The whole schema-3 chain moved onto the post-fix manifest: `gauss_main_29` now selects sources 66–94 and pins `peano_full_66`; `fta_shortlist_42`'s Peano dependency moved to `peano_full_66` with the one-row index shift applied (required indices, adaptation rows); `lean.py` generalized its hardcoded Peano corpus id into `PEANO_CORPUS_IDS` (context application + manifest coverage). The re-rendered tracked project — 66 Peano + 29 Gauss + 46 FTA = 141 public theorems, 6,202 named row facts — passes the pinned `lake build` with zero admissions. `peano_full_65` stays tracked as a frozen historical corpus that nothing pins.

**See also.** [I-190](30_invariants.md#i-190), [I-67](30_invariants.md#i-67), D-51, D-275.

<a id="d-275"></a>
## D-275 — export the acyclic Peano and Gauss main proof graph to Lean using ordinary predicates (2026-08-11,, maintainer-directed)

**The problem.** The Isabelle attempt could represent the Peano theory with an
ordinary carrier, but Isabelle's proof-method and resource limits prevented the
complete certificate from checking. The proof graph also contains a known
two-theorem prior-reference cycle at sources 24 and 25 that cannot be repaired or
trusted during export.

**The decision.** Reuse the backend-neutral certificate frontend and add a Lean
4 backend. Schema 2 owns the complete acyclic Peano base; schema 3 hashes that
certificate as a dependency and extends it with all Gauss main sources. Encode
the GL object theory over one abstract carrier `α`: sets
are predicates, binary and ternary operations are relations, and compiled GL
definitions remain propositions. No GL term becomes a Lean type and no
term-indexed family is generated. Lean's own dependent kernel remains the host
foundation; the ordinary-type constraint applies to the exported GL theory.

Every certificate row is emitted as a named Lean fact and receives one manifest
disposition. Direct, OR, and induction theorems are emitted in the certificate's
acyclic order. Induction typing, zero, and step chapters become private helpers;
the public theorem accepts relational induction as an explicit proposition
premise rather than declaring an axiom. Generated source is rejected if it
contains `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom`, `opaque`, or `unsafe`.

Gauss integration scopes are ordinary universally quantified implications.
Their internal parameters are closed at the recorded boundary, and a
disintegrated existence carries one explicit existential witness bundle through
the dependent row facts. The eight Gauss reformulated-statement theorems use the
GL well-defined-output contract constructively: a validated non-recursive set or
binary-relation definition is inhabited by a comprehension or relation lambda,
the defining predicate is proved by unfolding, and the cited theorem is applied
to that concrete output. This adds no GL existence axiom and no dependent GL
type family.

**Cycle boundary.** The complete exported corpus is source indices 0 through 66
except 24 and 25: 65 theorems, 143 chapters, and 3,247 rows. The selection records
both exclusions and the renderer asserts that they are the only exclusions. No
cyclic theorem is emitted, assumed, or replaced. The Gauss extension is sources
67 through 95 with no exclusions: 29 theorems, 33 chapters, and 1,511 rows. Its
thirteen Peano citations are pinned by the dependency certificate hash, and the
combined theorem graph is asserted acyclic.

**Why Lean.** Lean's kernel accepted the complete ordinary-predicate Peano
translation with theorem replay and explicit induction specializations. This
removes the Isabelle resource failure. Lean also accepts the Gauss integration
and existence patterns once they are represented as ordinary quantified
propositions and constructive predicate witnesses, without changing the GL
object-theory encoding or weakening the cycle boundary.

**Code.** `proof_export/certificate.py`, `proof_export/lean.py`,
`proof_export/export_lean.py`, `lean_export/GLExport/ProofSupport.lean`, and
`tests/test_proof_export_lean.py`.

**See also.**
[I-189](30_invariants.md#i-189) and
[`10_pipeline/10_external_proof_export.md`](10_pipeline/10_external_proof_export.md).

<a id="d-274"></a>
## D-274 — a rule installed from an external-mail carrier gets a local `expansion | carrier` history row at the receiving LB (2026-08-11,, maintainer-picked)


**The problem.** Rules travel to descendant LBs as external-mail carriers (compact `(implication<N>[…])` statements per [I-54](30_invariants.md#i-54), and negated compact existences) and are installed and FIREABLE at the receiver — but the receiver's `exprOriginMap` held no history row for the reconstructed rule: the carrier's own row arrives with statement mail, while the reconstruction's `disintegration` row exists only at the LB that originally derived the rule. A local firing citing the rule then leaves the chapter walker with nothing to resolve (`buildStack: no origin found`). The gap is old but was MASKED by the x-copy leak: the leak's x-fed chains locally re-derived exactly these rules inside every induction sub-LB, writing local origins as a side effect. Every leak-fix variant unmasked it (three distinct crash sites, all the same shape: rule origin at the ancestors, negated-AND origin mail-merged, rule row absent at the firing sub-LB).

**The decision (maintainer-picked over a walker-side cross-LB ancestor fallback).** Rule-16 origin maintenance on the prover side, in two halves matching the two rule-transport shapes:

1. **Receiver-side install write** — the status-3 branch of `addExprToMemoryBlock`'s implication-install loop writes `reconstructed ⟵ expansion | carrier` into the receiving LB's map for every rule recovered from a mailed carrier (`parameters.trackHistory`-gated like every history write). Local installs (status 0/1) keep their disintegration-path history writes — no duplicate rows.
2. **Producer-side paired mail writes** — the or-disintegration rule emissions (the K mutual-exclusion implications and the D-269 subset-exclusion rules) gain the paired `addMailOutOrigin` mirror next to their local `disintegration` origin writes. These rules are flat hash rules — never statements, never in `intLocalEncodedStatementsDelta` — so the retired transitive history shipper's replacement doctrine ("statements ship via the delta loop; doc-only records get paired writes") had orphaned exactly this class: a descendant receiving a fired head by mail held a citing row whose rule ingredient it could not resolve. The antecedent `expandedOrSignature` record was already pair-mailed, so the receiver's chain closes at one added row per emitted rule.

**Verification.** Shortcut acceptance no longer asserts at chapter export; verifier airtight; no walker-side change.

<a id="d-272"></a>
## D-272 — recursion subtrees mint the axed set but never register the axed-anchor statement (2026-08-11,, maintainer-decided after a same-day pivot)


**The problem.** The x-copy leak (`docs/fta_ladder/B_RT_investigation.md`, maintainer verdict 2026-08-11: x-names must stay confined to the anchor context). `prehandleAnchor` early-returned on `isPartOfRecursion` LBs ABOVE both the `intAxedVariables` mint and the child recursion, so induction subtrees kept permanently empty axed sets and the `addExprToMemoryBlock` containment door was a no-op there. The parent's x-anchor statement rode statement mail into the stub and registered unchecked; ordinary anchor rules then bred x-facts internally. Trap attribution (42-row shortcut): exactly ONE external mail arrival — `(AnchorFTA[1,2,3,4,5,x6,7,8])`, status 3, warm-up — and 704 subsequent internal implication registrations; end state 553/7 700 statements + 282/1 884 rules citing `x6` in B5's rec2 sub-LB, with 122 x6 items exported via `mailOut`.

**The decision.** Set-only containment with a maintainer-decided anchor-numeral exception: the walk covers recursion subtrees (mode threaded down via the `axedMode` parameter) and mints the axed names there, arming the door; the x-substituted anchor statement and its `anchor handling` history line register only OUTSIDE recursion subtrees. Induction sub-blocks therefore hold no x-citing statement, rule, or firing at all — the mailed ancestor form is refused because every descendant's trace-accumulated axed set is a superset of its ancestors'. **The exception (maintainer, same day, overriding the no-exemptions default):** a block-#1 recursion root whose goal — the theorem head, queued verbatim at creation — cites a `(1)`-typed anchor slot value leaves its whole subtree UNTOUCHED (no mint, no registration): the mailed ancestor form registers at the inert door and the historical premise-completion machinery runs there. Rationale: pure set-only un-proves the unit-product row B3 (the pool's anchor-numeral-headed rows 37/38), whose pre-fix induction chapters cite ZERO x-content — the x-machinery is search-dynamics scaffolding there, so the statement-with-armed-door middle ground is provably near-inert (every x-anchor firing's head cites an x-slot and dies at the armed door) and only the full pre-fix dynamics restore the proof. Block-#2 `_induction_` side-chain roots always stay set-only — their synthetic `(=[digitArg,zero])` goal cites the zero numeral by construction, and their chapters are x-free.

**Rejected alternative — uniform treatment (implemented first, same day, then abandoned).** Registering the statement in recursion subtrees too ("every LB identical") was tried first: it preserved the premise-completion firings but crashed the shortcut acceptance at chapter export — `buildStack: no origin found` for an x-FREE derived rule (`(>[]!(=[u_10,u_2])(existence11[u_1,u_10,u_3]))` at `main`, LB `(in2[rec2,10,3])`). Trap probes showed the rule fireable at the sub-LB with its provenance rows living only at the ancestors (`(in[10,1])` / `(in3[9,10,6,5])`): a pre-existing rule-transport provenance gap that the leak's local x-fed re-derivation had masked by writing a local origin, and that the uniform variant's surviving firings kept exercising. The set-only variant also removes those firings' inputs from the sub-blocks, is strictly better for runtime (no premise-completion population in the monster induction blocks), and matches the confinement verdict most literally.

**Verification.** Unit tests `test_axed_anchor_exception.cpp::prehandle_covers_recursion_lb_and_subtree` / `prehandle_registers_statement_outside_recursion` / `door_armed_on_recursion_lb_after_prehandle`; 42-row shortcut acceptance (42/42, verifier airtight, zero x6 in the induction sub-LB dump) + full-pipeline `theorems.txt` set identity.

<a id="d-273"></a>
## D-273 — the ancestor-known contract enforced at every registration door, refusal keeps the or-release signal, descendant copies swept (2026-08-11,, maintainer-directed)


**The problem.** The B-theorem shortcut blow-up (`docs/fta_ladder/B_RT_investigation.md`): the induction sub-LBs of B5/B7/B8 hold thousands of statements byte-identical at a scope AND a descendant `_ordis_` branch scope, and phase 2's grow search is super-linear in that population. The contract "an expression offered at a scope whose ancestor already knows it must not be added" already existed as Site F — but only at the `addExprToMemoryBlock` entry. The trap run (2026-08-11 baseline, 618 s / 42 rows) attributed the violations to the exact-key-gated doors behind it: `applyEquivalenceClass`'s commit (28 950 of 82 954 registrations ancestor-known), `addNegatedEquality` (1 506 / 8 746), `addStatement`'s disintegration products (267 / 170 468), `addEquality` clean.

**The decision (maintainer: "clean permanent solutions, not a heap of exemptions"; parent-scope row always wins, and the parent is whatever ancestor holds the row — never hardcoded `main`).** One predicate, every door, no shape exemptions:

- `gl::ancestorKnown` is the single definition of the scan (self-inclusive for Site F and the firing mirror; strict-ancestors for the door gates). Gates at `addStatement` (covers the equality pair doors via I-180's sole-gateway rule), `applyEquivalenceClass`'s commit block (refusing the equality1 history line too — no history for a row that never exists), and the negated-equality expander's `emitNew` (pre-gated so the refused variant is neither deposited nor pushed to `newStatements`). All gates `compressor_mode`-skipped, matching Site F.
- **Refusal keeps the I-174 resolution signal.** The sequenced release is deposit-driven (`ordisMerge`'s goal probe); a refused branch deposit whose expression matches an open parent-chain goal must still resolve its cohort, or the next pending branch never releases (a stall the entry-level Site F refusal could already cause latently, in the nested configuration where the goal sits shallower than the knowing scope). `stageOrReleaseForRefusedDeposit` runs `ordisMerge`'s probe on every refusal, entirely non-minting.
- The enabler is D-271: with the negated-equality expander scope-symmetric, an ancestor row fully substitutes for a descendant copy for EVERY consumer (request generation, contradiction probes, goal closure, or-convergence, equi-class application), so no exemption is needed.
- The branch-first residue (ancestor row arrives after a legitimately-registered descendant copy; `NameMap` has no child index, so no deposit-time descendant check is possible) is handled by the end-of-burst sweep `sweepAncestorKnownRows` — the campaign's companion piece landing with the waterline repair in the removal door.

**Rejected alternative.** Exempting equality/negated-equality shapes from the dedup (the conservative first proposal): rejected by the maintainer — the load-bearing branch copy was a symptom of the expander's scope asymmetry, and the exemption would have preserved the asymmetry forever.

**Verification.** Per-door unit tests (predicate directions, descendant-copy refusal, equality-pair refusal, equi-class product refusal + D-33 deposit control, refusal-side release staging); campaign acceptance: no `theorems.txt` row lost on the 42-row shortcut A/B and the full pipeline, verifier 0 failures, statement-list census cut in the B5 dump, super-linear wall-time payoff.

<a id="d-271"></a>
## D-271 — negated-equality class expansion covers the descendant direction, product at the class's scope (2026-08-11,, maintainer-directed)


**The problem.** `applyEquivalenceClassToNegatedEquality` walked classes at the negation's own scope and strict ancestors only, and `applyEquiClasses` Pass 1's expander pre-gate (`classAtOrAbove`) matched that directionality. A negation known at an ancestor scope was therefore invisible to a class at a descendant (`_ordis_` branch) scope — the ONE consumer for which an ancestor-scope statement row could not substitute for a descendant-scope copy. That asymmetry blocked the ancestor-known dedup campaign (`docs/fta_ladder/B_RT_investigation.md` handoff): dropping a branch-scope copy of `!(=[a,b])` would have silently lost every rewrite the branch's class would have produced from it. The maintainer rejected a shape exemption ("clean permanent solutions, not a heap of exemptions") — the asymmetry itself is the bug.

**The decision.** Make the expander scope-symmetric with `applyEquivalenceClass`'s [D-33](#d-33) rule. The class walk covers all three directions; the emitted sibling inequality deposits at `deeperOf(negation scope, class scope)`: own-scope and ancestor-scope classes emit at the negation's scope (unchanged), descendant-scope classes emit at the class's scope. Descendant class-bucket validities walk in decoded-lex order ([I-84](30_invariants.md#i-84)). Pass 1's pre-gate widens to the full three-way comparability. Pass 2's equality-shape skip stays: arrival covers new-negation × existing-class in all directions, Pass 1 covers changed-class × existing-negation in all directions — complete pairing, no third moment needed. The citation probe ([D-227](#d-227)) gains the negation's own scope between the class scope and the shared ancestors (descendant case), keeping the deepest-first resolution order. The one-sided expansion rule ([I-12](30_invariants.md#i-12)) is untouched — it governs equality sides, not scopes.

**Verification.** Unit tests `equi_reshuffle::negated_equality_arrival_expands_via_descendant_class` (arrival direction: class at branch first, negation at main later → variant at the branch only, citation at the branch) and `equi_reshuffle::apply_equi_classes_expands_negation_via_later_descendant_class` (Pass-1 direction: negation at main first, class forms at branch later → variant at the branch only). Campaign-level acceptance rides the ancestor-known dedup gates (no `theorems.txt` row lost, verifier 0 failures).
<a id="d-265"></a>
## D-265 — an output-collision conjecture deposits a variable-copy axiom at the second colliding premise LB (2026-08-10,, maintainer-specified)


**The problem.** A conjecture can only state an equality between two compound terms by fusing their result binders into ONE name — B8 (row 42) encodes a·c = b·c as `(>[10,11](in3[10,9,11,5])(>[12](in3[12,9,11,5])…`: both products share output name 11. A pool rule written with two distinct result variables for that premise pair (B5's `(in3[9,11,12,5])`/`(in3[10,11,13,5])`) can then never match: request matching only renames, it never binds two rule variables to one statement name, and the partition copies that would legalize the collapse come from `multiplyImplication` — disabled outside the incubator (`allow_multiplication: false`, RT). Trap-proven consequence in the fix7 dataset: B5's demand marker qualifies and installs at the reductio twin (116 QUAL verdict=1 entries) but never fires, the demand `(strictOrder[1,4,10,12])` never mints, and the or10 cohort parked in `rejectedMapOrdis2` under exactly that key never wakes — B8 stalls at 41/42.

**The choice (maintainer-specified).** When `addTheoremToMemory`'s disintegrated chain contains exactly two positive premises of the same operator whose non-input/output arguments are all byte-equal and whose single output slot carries the same name r (inputs differing), the SECOND colliding premise LB receives the dead-end variable-copy axiom `(=[r,r_copy])` — status 0, `main`, `variableCopy` origin with zero dependencies, the LB-creation paired mailOut write. This is the FIFTH emission site of the established `(=[Y,Y_copy])` free-axiom contract ([D-235](#d-235) is the fourth, in the same function); detection is the pure helper `detectOutputCollisionCopyVar` ([`prover.cpp`](../../GL_Quick_VS/GL_Quick/src/prover.cpp)), config-classified via each operator's `inputIndices`/`outputIndices`.

**Why the second colliding premise LB, not the first carrier (maintainer decision, same day, after the full-run Peano breach).** Mail flows only ancestor-to-descendant ([I-57](30_invariants.md#i-57)), so the deposit LB's whole subtree receives the copy. The first carrier is typically an anchor-adjacent chain prefix SHARED by foreign conjectures — in the full Peano pool the cancellation family's first premise `(in3[7,8,9,5])` is also the first premise of single-`in3` conjectures the detector can never fire on, and a first-carrier deposit mailed `(=[9,9_copy])` into their disproof twins, where it fused with the twins' assumed-head/premise merges until an admission template breached `prepareIntegration`'s one-changeable-arg contract (`tempKept <= 1`, `(in3[marker,marker,marker,4])`, trap-proven: deposit inventory + breach chain + breach copy-class,  / `run_B8_full4.log`). Every genuine consumer — the deeper premise LBs, the contradiction twins primed under the innermost premise, the recursion auxiliaries — sits at or below the SECOND colliding premise, so the copy still reaches them all while foreign prefix-sharing subtrees never see it. D-235 sits at the innermost because its trigger involves the head.

**Why it closes B8.** The class {r, r_copy} generates the all-distinct statement variants (registered rows with non-canonical members persist, [I-58](30_invariants.md#i-58) — empirically confirmed side by side in the fix7 twin dump); B5's marker then binds injectively, the demand mints, the park-side rendezvous key is already filed, route (c) opens the strict split, and each branch derives r<r against irreflexivity — the reductio discharges. Cost is proportional to formulation collisions (rows 12 and 42 in the current ladder), not to pool size — the opposite scaling of blanket multiplication.

**Boundaries.** Trigger is the conjecture's syntactic shape at theorem load — nothing fires at burst time; non-matching conjectures are byte-unaffected. Exactly-two by design: a third premise matching the same (operator, non-input/output args, output name) signature suppresses the fire — extendable later. Single-output operators only; theorem chains never carry `u_` arguments (asserted, not gated). **Anchor guard (the I-24 analogue, added same day after the full-run Peano crash):** the shared output name must not be an anchor argument — an anchor-slot name is a theory CONSTANT (Peano's `s(a)=0 ∧ s(b)=0 → a=b` family shares output `2` = zero), and duplicating a constant variant-fans every statement carrying it grid-wide (observed as `(in3[marker,marker,marker,4])` admission templates at a Peano disproof twin, then aborting on `prepareIntegration`'s former `tempKept <= 1` assert — now the skip gate below). Family sibling rows sharing the deposit LB re-run the deposit; the add door dedups.

**One-changeable-arg gate (maintainer decision, same day).** `prepareIntegration`'s former `tempKept <= 1` assert is now a GATE: a template with more than one changeable argument is not integrable, and skipping it is a defined result of the integration contract, not a failure (the Rule-19 bivalent-flow test — both branches intended). The prepared-marker mint precedes the gate, so a skipped template is memoized and never re-enters. Incubator mode keeps its historical multi-changeable processing.

**Verification.** Full rebuild (Release x64) + `gl_quick.exe --unit-tests` green (`output_collision_copy` suite: detection positives/negatives incl. the exactly-two, non-input/output-arg, and anchor gates + the second-premise deposit + the no-deposit control); shortcut acceptance: 42/42 with B8's row in `theorems.txt`, verifier airtight, non-colliding rows byte-identical, row 12 as the overhead canary; full-pipeline acceptance: the Peano batch completes (the first-carrier leak breach gone) with verifier 0 failures.

## D-267 — the ordis2 demand/park pair `admissionMapOrdis2` / `rejectedMapOrdis2`, one key language, algebra-style rendezvous (2026-08-10,, maintainer-directed)

**The problem.** Part 2 of the B8 design needs a rule's hunger ("matched everything except one ground compound premise") to OPEN the parked or cohort whose disjunct supplies that premise. The attempt built the demand map (`compoundDemandMap`) but wired its wake as a key lookup into `rejectedMapOrdis` — whose keys are disjunct PRODUCT TEMPLATES (for existence-bodied operators like `preorder`/`strictOrder`: the witness-marker body fact), never disjunct text. Key-language mismatch: the wake could never fire for the order family B8 needs. The 3X post-mortem also left the or8/or10 never-park anomaly open (suspected: algebra key-gain wakes consuming parks through the shared witness-template key).

**The decision (maintainer, this branch).** Complete the pair: rename the recovered demand map to `admissionMapOrdis2` and create the missing rejected counterpart `rejectedMapOrdis2` — a SECOND park index filed at the same park site, keyed by each eligible disjunct's clean GROUND text (polarity verbatim, [I-175](30_invariants.md#i-175); eligible = operator with a compiled non-atomic entity, arity ≥ `kOrdis2DemandMinArity`) at the cohort parent's validity. The two maps speak ONE key language, so the wake is a plain key rendezvous, and they complete each other exactly as algebra's `admissionMap`/`rejectedMap` do: whichever side arrives second wakes the other. Or-first: the head parks in BOTH ordis maps (the old filing is untouched, [I-178](30_invariants.md#i-178)); the demand drain (`drainAdmissionKeysOrdis2`) mints the key, RMW-inserts, and calls `revisitRejectedOrdis2` — snapshot, erase key, un-know (`resetParkedOrStatementRegistries`), re-mail on `sameIterationInternalMail`; the re-consumption's route (c) reads the fresh demand and opens. Demand-first: the deposit-time route-(c) probe of `admissionMapOrdis2` precedes the park in `consumeOrLeavesCohort`'s probe/park chain, so the cohort opens without parking. Opening consumes the matched demand keys (`eraseBlobIf`); the pair self-liquidates.

**Full machinery parity (maintainer directive).** Every subsystem surrounding the older admission/rejected pairs is reproduced: equi-class hooks at BOTH `applyEquiClasses` seams (`applyEquivalenceClassToAdmissionMapOrdis2` drop-and-rekey; `applyEquivalenceClassToRejectedMapOrdis2` I-37 drop-and-mail), I-68 staging + post-fixpoint drain, `wipeHashMem` lines, deload band (`admissionMapOrdis2` base+63..66, `rejectedMapOrdis2` base+67..70, `ordis2RevisitInProgress` guard base+71), CE-clone/discharge survival via the band, and TWO appended EXTENDED-block dump sections (Rule 14 consent granted 2026-08-10; the 3X demand map had none — gap closed).

**Deliberate non-parity (each with its reason).** No `varsIn*Keys` caches (keys fully ground; both maps stay far smaller than the algebra map — the sibling ordis hook already walks uncached). No consumed-key twin (route (c) is the single consumer; the cohort bootstrap guard makes double-opens structurally impossible; erase-on-open suffices and post-open re-demands are legitimate fresh hunger). The algebra key-gain seams (`drainAdmissionKeysAlgebra`, `updateAdmissionMapRecursion`) do NOT touch the new pair — different key language, and a cross-probe would double-wake operator-application disjuncts whose old-map product template IS the disjunct text; only `drainAdmissionKeysOrdis2` wakes `rejectedMapOrdis2`, which also makes the new park immune to the suspected or8/or10 consumption path.

**Amended by [D-287](#d-287) (2026-08-18):** the subset test below treats an anchor-slot argument as ground (it can never be bound by a substantive premise), so a slot naming a constant — B9's `1 ≤ d` — qualifies; a slot the anchor alone binds still mints nothing.

**Filter decision (maintainer, 2026-08-10 — B5-only, the 3X sharpening KEPT; MINIMUM PREMISE COUNT added same day).** A rule installs demand variants only with at least `kOrdis2DemandMinPremises` (= 4) NON-anchor premises, qualifying slot included — the first post-eligibility-fix acceptance run exploded in runtime because every short rule with a qualifying compound slot installed demand-marker families across all LBs; 4 admits exactly the premise-rich B5 shape. The demand branch also carries the I-171 iteration-depth mirror (maintainer-approved same day): a ground demand text whose maximum `it_` iteration number exceeds `maxIterationNumberVariable` is not staged — the admission side gates depth identically, and each deeper witness generation would otherwise mint a fresh distinct demand key. Also recorded: the eligibility predicate consults the `compiledEntity` fence ONLY — gating on the input-AND-output `operators` set (the 3X form) silently disqualified the whole order family (predicates have empty output args), which was the root cause of the first two 41/42 acceptance runs. The demand qualifying-slot analysis keeps the non-anchor subset test — premise P qualifies iff args(P) ⊆ args(the rule's other NON-anchor premises). A14 (whose only other premise is the seed `!(=[a,b])`) therefore mints no demand, and that is now deliberate: with `rejectedMapOrdis2` in place, or10 (the Part-1 strict split fired directly from the seed) parks reliably in the NEW index — immune to the old map's suspected consumption anomaly — so B5's strictOrder demand alone opens the strict route, which closes B8 without A14 ever firing (Part 1 exists precisely to bypass it: a strict branch feeds B5 directly). The alternative literal filter (anchors available, A14's preorder demand additionally waking the parked or7 totality cohorts — the design's "accepted redundancy") was provisionally chosen earlier the same day on the pre-pair framing that or7 was the only family that parks, and reverted by the maintainer for the leaner single-route run once the pair made or10's park reliable. A stall on the strict route re-opens this choice with dump evidence, not by default.

**Value-type reuse.** `rejectedMapOrdis2` reuses `RejectedMapOrdisValue` (semantic content identical: or-statement valueInterner id + seed levels), inheriting the whole codec family; `admissionMapOrdis2`'s `AdmissionMapOrdis2Value` `{sourceImplId, levels}` is its own struct because `sourceImplId` is a ruleInterner id.
