## D-269 — flat or consumption also emits the subset-exclusion rule family (j = 1..k−2 negated disjuncts) with reduced or-compact heads, park-first (2026-08-07,; generalized from single-exclusion 2026-08-09,; maintainer-approved plans)

**The problem.** The K full-exclusion rules (`!D_others -> D_i`) each need k−1 NEGATIVE premises. In B8's reductio twin only ONE negative fact exists (the seed `!(=[10,12])`), and negative order facts have no producer — flat consumption alone can never split a trichotomy. The step no K rule can take is `!D_excluded -> (D_rest as a disjunction)`: fewer negative premises than k−1, a genuinely disjunctive conclusion.

**The choice (maintainer-approved plans, Part 1 of the B8 design + the subset generalization).** When a k-ary cohort with k ≥ 3 is flat-consumed AND its signature resolves to a registered or-operator (`compiledEntity` on the instantiated cohort signature — REGISTRY ORS ONLY, the maintainer's approved scope; I-179 De-Morgan negated-AND cohorts keep K-rules-only behavior), `consumeOrLeavesCohort` emits, in addition to the K rules, one subset-exclusion rule `!D_i1 &.. & !D_ij -> or(D_rest)` per excluded index subset with 1 ≤ j ≤ k−2 (size-j subsets in lexicographic order — deterministic, and the j = 1 family keeps the original per-leaf order): premises = the excluded leaves' negations in parent order (`negateScratch`, I-175 double-negation cancellation — a negated disjunct's exclusion premise is its positive core), head = the pre-minted reduced (k−j)-ary or-compact ([D-268](#d-268), whose single-elimination closure already registers every leaf subset of size ≥ 2; registry miss = hard assert), head instance args mapped through the parent's signature positions in the reduced list's first-appearance token order (the same order the reduced operator's u_-renumbering used, so the head instantiates exactly the surviving instance leaves). Flat hash rules — no scope creation — so emitted at every or depth like the K rules (D-211), same `disintegration` origin row citing the parent's expansion record. j = k−1 is not emitted — that IS the K rule family.

**Park-first (the load-bearing decision).** The rules install with the shape-detected `subsetExclusion` tag ([I-184](30_invariants.md#i-184) — detection deliberately ORDER-FREE in the premises, because the mail-compact round-trip permutes premise order): a fired reduced-or head never rides route (b) — it parks in `rejectedMapOrdis`; opening comes only from the Part-2 compound-demand map. Parts 1+2 are jointly the closing set for B8.

**Verifier surface (I-16 consent, plan approvals 2026-08-07 / 2026-08-09).** `_check_or_subset_exclusion` accepts the row shape as a fallback inside `_check_or_disintegration_implication`: j premises (1 ≤ j ≤ k−2) matched as a MULTISET against the negations of the excluded disjuncts, head an or-compact whose flattened disjunct list embeds in the parent's list as an order-preserving subsequence (the complement multiset is unique even with duplicate disjuncts, so a greedy walk decides). The De-Morgan branch of `check_disintegration` is unchanged.

**Growth.** 2^k − k − 2 extra flat rules per k ≥ 3 cohort consumption (k = 3: 3, k = 4: 10), bounded by `kMaxReducedOrLeaves`; a fired reduced head that is itself flat-consumed emits its own family (arity ≥ 3 only).

**Code.** `prover.cpp::consumeOrLeavesCohort` (section 1b, subset odometer + `emitExclusion`), `memory.cpp::flattenRegistryOrLeavesScratch`; `verifier.py::_check_or_subset_exclusion`. Tests: `tests/test_rejected_ordis.cpp::single_exclusion_rules_emitted_for_registry_or` / `single_exclusion_not_emitted_for_binary_or` / `subset_exclusion_rules_emitted_for_quaternary_or`; `tests/test_verifier_structural.py` (7 single-/subset-exclusion cases).

<a id="d-264"></a>
## D-264 — one admission door; levels rows always non-empty with the {-1} non-derived tier; the marker demoted to bookkeeping (2026-08-09,, maintainer-designed)

**The problem.** The B8 known-without-levels crash (`ordisMerge`'s refutation probe, burst 16): `intKnownStatements` carried two accidental membership bits (`known`, `registered`), level-row presence doubled as an admission verdict (so `addStatement`'s gates deliberately withheld rows), and the full-disintegration marker — vacuously true for atomics — created `known` rows for statements the admission gates refused, without levels. A `known` statement without a levels row crashed every probe that trusted the `known ⇒ levels` contract (three such asserts in the tree).

**The decision (maintainer's design, this session).** One concept, one door. (1) Every statement that reaches the kernel is offered to the ONE admission door (`addStatement`); known ⟺ it passed ⟺ it has a row ⟺ that row has a NON-EMPTY levels set. (2) The not-self-returned exemption is removed: a fully disintegrated deposit (e.g. a broadcast theorem compact decomposed into its rule) rides the same statements channel to the door (the channel's composite-key dedup makes the self-returned case a no-op); a PARTIALLY disintegrated deposit is deliberately not offered — it must stay re-processable. (3) The marker creates no rows and grants no `known`: it ORs `fullyDisintegrated` onto the row admission created, else does nothing. (4) Every non-derived statement (loaded fact, anchor, broadcast compact, assumed premise element, compressor premise) carries the `{-1}` tier — chosen over `{0}` because it fabricates no anchor provenance, makes an accidental empty/missing set unambiguously a bug, and (with transparency) keeps every union and the `allLevelsInvolved` arithmetic verdict-equivalent to the former empty-run behavior. (5) The `known`/`registered` bits die (follow-on commit): row presence carries the meaning; `StatementFlags` keeps exactly `local` and `fullyDisintegrated`.

**Rejected.** A new `admitted` flag preserving the old gate verdicts (a preservation shim — "old spaghetti replaced with new spaghetti"); `{0}` as the non-derived fill (fabricated ground provenance, byte-drift in every union); marker-side `known` gating (a writer patch on an incoherent contract); the registry merge (withdrawn earlier — the two containers stay).

**Consequences reported in advance.** Filter-suppressed texts lose their marker-faked visibility to the negation scans and ordis probes (the equivalence filter is suppress-and-drop, so some refutations may fire later — the acceptance `theorems.txt` row-diff arbitrates); suppressed compacts lose the request-firing privilege the marker smuggled; Site F no longer blocks re-deposits of refused fully-disintegrated texts (an RT watch item, gated at ~10% over the 461-483 s shortcut baseline); locally derived full-form implications that fully disintegrate now enter working memory as statements (uniformity — the same door, no exemptions).

**Code.** `prover.hpp::addStatement` (the door + `{-1}` substitution), `prover.cpp::addExprToMemoryBlock` (the offer + the demoted marker), `memory.hpp::insertLevelSorted` / `coldIntRunNonNegAt` (transparency), `memory.cpp::addToHashMemory` / `prover.hpp::updateEquivalenceClasses` (empty-set mapping at the rule/class boundaries), `filter.cpp::releaseCEBatchMemory` (the paired full reset — the former keep-loop was a proven no-op on the empty `ceBody` sentinel). Invariant: [I-182](30_invariants.md#i-182).

<a id="d-268"></a>
## D-268 — reduced (k−1)-ary or-operators are pre-minted at single-threaded seams, never mid-burst (2026-08-07,, maintainer-approved plan)

**The problem.** Part 1 of the B8 three-extension design emits single-exclusion rules `!D_i -> or(D_rest)` whose head is a genuine (k−1)-ary or-compact — an operator that may not exist yet. The emission site (`consumeOrLeavesCohort`) runs mid-burst inside the parallel phase, and registry writers are single-threaded seams only ([I-137](30_invariants.md#i-137); the [D-76](#d-76) compaction race is why compaction drains at the barrier) — so the reduced operator can never be minted at the point of use.

**The choice (maintainer-approved plan).** Pre-mint the single-elimination closure at the seams where registry writes are legal: `ExpressionAnalyzer::preMintReducedOrs` walks a deterministic snapshot of the or-category registry entries, flattens each to its ordered non-or leaves (`flattenRegistryOrLeaves`, the registry twin of `flattenOrLeaves`), and for every entry with k ≥ 3 flattened leaves registers the k leaves-minus-one operators (u_-renumbered to the canonical first-appearance scheme, [I-23](30_invariants.md#i-23) dedup through the factored `findOrMintOrOperator` — now the ONE or-mint site, shared with `constructOrTheorem`). Fresh mints join the worklist so chains close in one call. Call sites: `proveKernel` entry (covers GL-binary-loaded and precompile-minted ors before any burst), the tail of `constructOrTheoremsInRun` (covers in-run ors), and after the phase-4 deferred-compaction drain (covers drain-minted compacts). Idempotent — a re-run dedups to zero mints — so the overlapping seams cost one registry scan each. Runs in compressor mode too: the mints are a pure function of or-registry content, keeping the audited run and the compressor re-derivation registry-aligned.

**Growth bound.** k reduced operators per k-ary or, recursively — the full single-elimination lattice. Current pool tops out at k = 3 (trichotomy `or7` → three 2-ary reductions); `ExecutionParameters::kMaxReducedOrLeaves` (8) asserts loudly on a runaway leaf count (Rule 19 tripwire, widen with evidence).

**Consequence for the emission site.** The single-exclusion emission resolves its reduced head through the read-only `compiledOrByElements` fence (the `compiledEntity` sibling) and treats a registry miss as a hard assert — pre-minting is the guarantee that makes the assert sound.

**Code.** `prover.cpp::preMintReducedOrs` / `flattenRegistryOrLeaves` / `findOrMintOrOperator` / `renumberULeaves`; `prover.hpp::compiledOrByElements`. Tests: `tests/test_or_theorem_construction.cpp` (`find_or_mint_reuse_and_mint`, `premint_three_ary_closure_and_idempotence`, `premint_four_ary_worklist_closure`, `premint_nested_or_flattens_and_reuses_child`, `renumber_u_leaves_first_appearance`). Invariant: [I-185](30_invariants.md#i-185).

<a id="d-270"></a>
## D-270 — `prepareIntegrationCore` unfolds one entity per distinct instantiated signature (2026-08-07,, maintainer-picked variant)

**The problem.** The first pipeline run with in-run or broadcast ([D-266](#d-266)) aborted at burst 15 on `flattenOrLeaves: duplicate signature differs`. Trap evidence (): inside a scope where an assumed equality holds (the B8 disproof contradiction twin assumes the head `a=b`), equivalence-class single-representative collapse ([D-106](#d-106)) rewrote a totality instance into the degenerate `(or6[u_1,u_4,X,X])` — both disjuncts textually identical. `prepareIntegrationCore` re-unfolded the repeated element per occurrence, and each unfold of the existence-category `preorder` template minted its own fresh `pi_lev_` placeholder (`pi_lev_4_2362` vs `pi_lev_4_2363`): two entities, one signature, divergent element lists — exactly the ambiguity the flattenOrLeaves duplicate-identity assert exists to catch. Latent for the machine's whole life; armed the first time a degenerate or became reachable in-run.

**The choice (maintainer).** Skip the duplicate unfold entirely ("Variant 1"): compute the instantiated signature from the `u_`-argument pairs BEFORE the fresh-`pi_` mint (byte-identical — signatures carry only `u_` arguments and `replaceKeysScratch` is token-boundary), probe the committed entities, and on a hit return without minting, committing, or recursing. One entity per distinct signature; the table becomes the unfolded definition graph. A full consumer audit (29 sites) found no positional or index-persisting reader — every child resolution is a first-match signature scan that lands on the retained record, and `prepareIntegrationCore2`'s per-entity emitter was already signature-gated (`integrationPrepared` probe-then-mint), so occurrence count never carried meaning.

**Rejected alternative ("Variant 2").** Committing a byte-identical duplicate (reuse the first unfold's placeholder assignment, keep per-occurrence records) — rejected by the maintainer as another duplicate with no consumer that wants it; the audit confirmed nothing positional needs the second record.

**Accepted consequences.** (1) The dropped occurrence's subtree stops emitting: previously its divergent-`pi_` children passed the signature gates and emitted redundant alpha-variant work (extra hash rows, admission keys, a second stored instruction the admission replay re-ran) — a strict, logically sound reduction. (2) `pi_lev_` numbering shifts wherever duplicates existed (deterministic; golden bytes move). (3) `memory.hpp::cleanInstructionWork`'s orphan reference count is the one count-sensitive consumer: duplicate records used to inflate an element's count and suppress the cascade erase; at both live call sites the erase target is an atomic marker-form admission key, so no cascade runs.

**Code.** `prover.hpp::prepareIntegrationCore`; the invariant is [I-186](30_invariants.md#i-186). Test: `tests/test_memory.cpp::prepare_integration_core_dedups_duplicate_signature` (degenerate or unfolds once + flattenOrLeaves crash regression; non-degenerate control keeps per-occurrence unfolds).

<a id="d-266"></a>
## D-266 — OR theorems are constructed and broadcast IN-RUN on the phase-4 barrier (A16 Phase 2) (2026-08-07,, maintainer-approved plan)

**The problem.** OR theorems were built strictly post-run (`constructOrTheoremsFromPairs` at the export seam), so no grid could ever consume an or theorem derived from the same run's proved implications — and the shortcut wiring never feeds the or forms back as externals, so they were unreachable on ANY run. The B8 stall pinned the consequence exactly: totality is proved (its implication form is installed as a rule in every LB) and its or-form `or6` exists in the export, but in-run no or-shaped statement exists, so the `{a≤b, b≤a}` case split the multiplicative-cancellation reductio needs has no producer (`docs/fta_ladder/B8/current_proof_state.md`).

**The choice (maintainer-approved plan, preserved from the A16 campaign).** A new single-threaded seam `constructOrTheoremsInRun` on `proveKernel`'s phase-4 barrier — after `revertVacuousGlobalTheorems` (a row retracted this iteration is never scanned as a source), before the [D-76](#d-76) deferred-compaction sort + drain. It walks `globalTheoremList` for unscanned rows (`orInRunScannedRows`, string-keyed — an index cursor would slide on vacuous-reversion erases), licenses each via `headSwitchOne`, folds via the existing `constructOrTheorem` ([D-260](#d-260) n-ary fold, [I-23](30_invariants.md#i-23) registry dedup), registers via `appendGlobalTheorem(…, "or theorem", …)` + `fullTheoremList`, and queues the or theorem on `recordPendingCompaction` so the SAME iteration's compaction drain broadcasts its implication compact through the root's mailOut (empty level set; status-3 rule door at every receiver, two-iteration delivery). Where the rule's premises hold it fires, the `(or<N>[…])` head deposits locally at status 0/1, disintegrates, and the cohort machinery opens under its normal demand gates — no gate widening, no new consumption machinery. Registry mints at this seam are legal for the same reason the compaction drain's are (single-threaded, post-join).

**Cross-seam idempotence — the canonical pair ledger.** Mirror pairs `(x, y)` / `(y, x)` describe one disjunction but mirrored element ORDERS are distinct registry identities, so constructing both double-mints `or<N>`. The shared member `orBuiltByPair` (sorted-pair → constructed or string) is the single gate: the in-run seam skips a pair whose mirror was already built (first-scanned side builds — deterministic, append-order), and the export seam recovers the stored string for its return vector + parent-subsumption bookkeeping WITHOUT reconstructing (a rebuild from the other side would mint the mirrored operator). The export seam keeps a walk-local emitted set so within-walk mirror duplicates still skip outright. Unit coverage: `test_or_theorem_construction.cpp` (`in_run_constructs_registers_and_queues`, `in_run_rescan_is_idempotent`, `in_run_mirror_scanned_later_no_double`, `export_seam_idempotent_after_in_run`, `in_run_compressor_mode_noop`).

**Scope.** All proving batches, no config flag (maintainer decision in the preserved plan). Compressor mode is a defined no-op — its internal re-derivation is a redundancy probe whose theorem list must stay byte-identical to the audited run; the export seam builds the ors on the survivor list. A premise-free or theorem registers but is not broadcast (no implication-compact shape). Known accepted residual (shared with every broadcast theorem): a vacuous reversion cannot un-install an already-broadcast rule from LB hash memories.

**Companion obligation.** In-run consumption of ≥3-element registry ors becomes reachable (trichotomy `or7`, positivity `or5`), which arms the [D-260](#d-260) latent polarity defect in the two or-EXPANSION twins (`expandSignature` OR case; the verifier's `_build_or_from_elements`) — fixed in this same campaign under explicit [I-16](30_invariants.md#i-16) consent (plan approval 2026-08-07).

<a id="d-263"></a>
## D-263 — the per-chapter anchor-handling uniqueness check is retired; the trace check roots every handling row (2026-08-06,, maintainer-ordered)

**The problem.** The B3-campaign twin lemma (`a≥2 ∧ b≥1 ⟹ a·b≥2`, first pool row whose proof cites two anchor numerals at two premise-chain depths) produced the campaign's first verifier failure: `anchor handling uniqueness` demanded at most one `anchor handling` row per chapter, and the twin's induction-condition chapter carried two — the slot-7-only copy variant `(AnchorFTA[…,i1,2_copy,…])` cited by rows fired at the first premise LB, and the both-slots variant `(AnchorFTA[…,1_copy,2_copy,…])` cited by deeper rows. Dump evidence (): the producer's real guarantee is one copied-anchor variant per LB — `prehandleAnchor`'s copy set is a function of the LB's upward path, no LB ever registers two variants (the axed-variable deposit gate even drops a mailed foreign variant), and the chapter-level doubling is aggregation across LB depths, not duplicated state. The check's founding assumption (one handling event per proof; a second row = walker duplication) no longer matches the producer's design.

**The choice (maintainer).** Two `verifier.py` edits under explicit I-16 consent: (1) the `count > 1` uniqueness failure is deleted — several handling rows per chapter are legal; (2) the `anchor handling trace` check collects its copy variables from the union of ALL handling rows' args instead of the first row's only (the first-row-only collection had silently left the second variant's vars untraced). The trace machinery itself was already multi-root-correct: its target accepts any `anchor handling` row, and the same-variable follow restriction forces every chain to terminate at a root that mints the variable.

**Rejected alternative.** Producer-side convergence (compute the copy set once per theorem from the whole premise chain so every LB mints one maximal variant, keeping the chapter single-rooted) — rejected as fixing documentation shape by changing prover state; the per-LB copy sets are healthy.

**Code.** `verifier.py::verify_chapter` (meta-check 4), tests `tests/test_verifier_meta.py::test_anchor_handling_trace_two_roots_both_vars_traced` / `test_anchor_handling_trace_second_root_var_orphaned`. Full investigation: `docs/fta_ladder/B3/current_proof_state.md`.

<a id="d-261"></a>
## D-261 — `changedClassesThisStep` consumed keep-last by (validity, member set) (2026-08-06,, maintainer-approved)

**The problem.** `updateEquivalenceClasses` pushes one snapshot into `changedClassesThisStep` per class CHANGE, so a class updated N times in one step appears N times in the delta — and `applyEquiClasses` Pass 1 runs a full registry sweep per entry. In the A20 hot burst ~11 of the 16 delta entries were snapshots of one class with an identical member set, each sweep producing only downstream-dedup'd duplicates; the pattern is generic (any chatty class-update step pays it), independent of the dead-branch pathology the same burst exposed.

**The choice (maintainer).** Dedup at the CONSUMER, keep-LAST: Pass 1 skips entry k when a later entry j > k carries the same validity id and the same member-id run (member runs are decoded-lex sorted per [I-88](30_invariants.md#i-88), so run equality is set equality). Keeping the last snapshot preserves the most complete pair-level and origin state at apply time; consuming at the reader leaves the buffer, its single push site, and its deload bytes untouched (the append-only CSR columns would need a splice to dedup at push). Pass 2's `deltaIds` snapshot is unaffected — duplicate entries mint the same class key. Contingency recorded at the review: should the verification battery ever surface a level-dependent divergence, the narrower fallback is full-blob byte-equality as the dedup key (strict-duplicate removal only).

**The scan shape (incident-corrected).** The verdicts are computed by ONE LINEAR pre-pass per Pass-1 round (`prover.hpp::fillDeltaKeepLastFlags`): a descending walk interns each entry's packed `(validity, members)` key (`encodeEqClassKeyFromViewScratch`, the same builder Pass 2's `deltaIds` uses) into a per-round scratch `ColdHashSet`; a key already seen means a later entry owns it, flagging the current entry in a per-round flag column the k loop reads. Entries pushed mid-round carry no flag and apply unfiltered; the next round's pre-pass covers them. The FIRST landed form compared entry pairs on demand — O(n²) view assemblies per round — and the full-run verification battery caught it grinding the Peano incubator's chatty-class steps (hundreds of same-validity delta entries; `AnchorIncubator3` grid bursts 0.03–5 s baseline → 42–124 s, the whole batch ~30–100× slower) while the shortcut corpus (deltas ≤ ~16) never noticed. Same verdicts, linear cost.

**Code.** `prover.hpp::fillDeltaKeepLastFlags`, consumed in `prover.hpp::applyEquiClasses` Pass 1. Test: `tests/test_memory.cpp::fill_delta_keep_last_flags`.

<a id="d-262"></a>
## D-262 — equi-class Pass 1 skips delta classes at or below a refuted `_ordis_` branch (2026-08-06,, maintainer-approved)

**The problem.** The A20 shortcut run exploded 14× (331.6 s vs A18's 25 s): one hash burst spent ~294 s in phase 3's `applyEquiClasses`, back-applying 16 delta classes across the statement registry — and 14 of them lived inside the `rec = 0` disjunct of a predecessor case split whose assumption contradicts the row's `9 ≠ 1` premise. The branch's refutation (`rec ≠ 0` at `main`, derived by ordinary main-scope phase-2 rules in the SAME burst) was absorbed milliseconds BEFORE the apply started, but nothing consulted it: the dead-branch drain (`drainDeadOrBranches`) runs at end-of-burst sanitize, AFTER `standardProcessing`, so the whole grind happened inside a branch the machine could already prove dead — ~7,830 committed rewrites of ex-falso content, all wiped the same burst.

**The choice (maintainer; trap-verified before landing).** Before applying a delta class, `applyEquiClasses` Pass 1 resolves the class's validity scope through the new `refutedOrBranchAtOrAbove` helper: walk the ancestor chain; a scope already staged in `pendingDeadOrBranches` is dead; at an `_ordis_` disintegration scope, run the exact `ordisMerge` staging probe ([D-242](#d-242) — negate(asserted disjunct) `known` at the branch scope or an ancestor, non-minting). On a hit the branch is minted into `pendingDeadOrBranches` — the drain's own inbox — and the class is skipped; the SAME burst's drain then retires the branch exactly as if `ordisMerge` had staged it. No seam reorder, no new refutation semantics, no new registry: the shortcut registry the skip consults is the one the drain already consumes. Pass 2 stays ungated (the delta skip alone removed the explosion; new-statement volume collapses with it).

**Rejected alternatives.** (a) Distinct-numerals tripwire at the class-merge site (flag `0 = 1`-class collapses as contradictions) — rejected by the maintainer: where such collapses matter, provided lemmas will cover them. (b) Running the dead-branch drain BEFORE the phase-3 apply — an [I-63](30_invariants.md#i-63) seam reorder with broader blast radius than consulting the predicate in place.

**Measured effect (experiment on the RT branch; production form identical minus instrumentation).** Overall 331.6 s → 55.8 s; the hot burst 296.9 s → 4.6 s (phase 3: 294 s → 0.26 s); verifier 2546 / 0 airtight with per-category tallies byte-identical; statement counts at every sacred-dump boundary identical; branch lifecycle identical. Only origin-history VOLUME differs (the never-minted dead-branch `equality1` lines — process documentation, Rule 16 / [I-44](30_invariants.md#i-44)).

**Code.** `prover.hpp::refutedOrBranchAtOrAbove` (the probe + staging), `prover.hpp::applyEquiClasses` (the Pass-1 skip). Test: `tests/test_memory.cpp::refuted_or_branch_at_or_above_probes_and_stages`.

<a id="d-260"></a>
## D-260 — OR-theorem assembly folds EVERY binder-free negated premise into one n-ary head (2026-08-05,, maintainer-ordered)

**The problem.** `constructOrTheorem` folded exactly ONE negated premise (the first found) with the head into a fixed two-element or. A proved hypothesis chain with several binder-free negated premises — the A16 trichotomy `¬(a<b) → (¬(a=b) → b<a)` — assembled into the incomplete `¬(a=b) → (a<b ∨ b<a)`: the second negated premise survived as a hypothesis instead of becoming the middle disjunct, so the pool carried a guarded two-branch or where the mathematics is the three-branch trichotomy `a<b ∨ a=b ∨ b<a`. The fold was also asymmetric with its own licensor: `headSwitchOne` licenses the pair on the RIGHTMOST binder-free negated premise, the constructor folded the LEFTMOST.

**The choice (maintainer).** Fold them all: classically `¬d_1 → (¬d_2 → h)` ⟺ `d_1 ∨ d_2 ∨ h`, so every binder-free negated premise becomes a disjunct (chain order, un-negated), the head last (verbatim — TRUE polarity, [I-175](30_invariants.md#i-175)). A negated premise that binds variables stays a shared premise: folding it would orphan its binder. The registry entry is n-ary — dedup ([I-23](30_invariants.md#i-23)) compares the full ordered element vector — and `expandToBaseForm`'s or-branch emits the FLAT De Morgan form `!(&!D_1!D_2!D_3)`, the same flat n-ary `&` the anchor definition bodies parse (byte-identical output for every existing 2-element or). Direct unit coverage: `test_or_theorem_construction.cpp::chain_of_negated_premises_folds_all_branches`.

**Round-trip note.** A later batch loading the flat base form recompiles it as a negated AND-bodied compact, which the D-258 De-Morgan door consumes n-ary — no or-operator name needs to survive the file boundary.

**Latent sibling — RESOLVED 2026-08-07.** The two in-run or-EXPANSION twins for k ≥ 3 — span `expandSignature` OR case and the verifier's `_build_or_from_elements` — shared a mirrored polarity defect (they nested the or-so-far un-negated as a conjunct). Fixed as the companion obligation of [D-266](#d-266) (which makes ≥3-element in-run consumption reachable), verifier half under explicit [I-16](30_invariants.md#i-16) consent; details in [`07_or_branching.md`](20_core_concepts/07_or_branching.md).

<a id="d-258"></a>
## D-258 — negated AND-bodied applications feed the or machinery through a runtime De-Morgan door, no operator minted (2026-08-05,, maintainer-designed)

**The problem.** An asserted `!(op[args])` whose compiled definition body is an AND registered flat and stayed inert — no constituent, no rule, no case split. The A16 stall's decisive gap: the premise `!(strictOrder[1,4,9,10])` is logically `¬(a≤b) ∨ (a=b)`, whose flattening `¬(a=b) → ¬(a≤b)` fires on the standing premise and closes the proof forward, but no mechanism ever decomposed the negated compound (trace-proven: the statement sat flat at `main` for all 15 bursts).

**The choice (maintainer).** A runtime De-Morgan door in `disintegrateExprCore2`'s no-instruction region (beside the negated-existence block): recognize `!(op[args])` with an AND-category compiled entity (read-only `compiledEntity` probe), instantiate the definition elements with the instance arguments (the light `getArgsSpans` + `replaceKeysScratch` idiom — the WorkInstruction path's polarity guard returns empty for negated inputs), negate each element with `negateScratch` so every disjunct carries its TRUE polarity (a negated conjunct's disjunct is its bare positive core — I-175, the G-65 lesson), and run the ordered leaves through `consumeOrLeavesCohort` — the or arm's whole downstream (expansion history, K mutual-exclusion rules, depth gate, two-route cohort machinery), extracted verbatim into a shared member. The cohort signature is the negated compound itself (an interned string — the machinery never requires an or-operator name). **No precompilation and no operator minting** (maintainer constraint): the registry is only read, so the door is parallel-phase safe; the rejected alternative — pre-minting an `orN` twin per AND-bodied operator at load — would have reused the compiled-or pipeline wholesale but adds registry surface (GL-binary rows, verifier registry, compile-checker exposure). The flat negated statement keeps registering as before; the door is additive.

**Why the or machinery and not bespoke flattened implications.** The K rules ARE the flattening — emitted at every or depth, before any gate — so the premise-decided case (A16) closes flat; and when premises do not decide, the same deposit parks or opens a genuine ordis cohort (sequenced release, dead-branch retirement) instead of leaving a second, parallel case-analysis mechanism to maintain.

**Scope note.** The door runs where disintegration runs (status 0/1 deposits). The status-3 mail-absorb gate still admits only compact implications and negated existences to disintegration — a mailed negated-AND registers flat, as before; widening that gate is a separate decision.

<a id="d-259"></a>
## D-259 — hypothesis constituents ride internal mail with a terminal internal-only `hypothesis` origin (2026-08-05,, maintainer-designed)

**The problem.** The A16 trichotomy campaign crashed the shortcut run on `addNegatedEquality`'s mirror-absence assert: `disintegrateExprHypothetically`'s registration loop direct-`upsertStatementKey`'d every disintegrated hypothesis constituent, so a bare negated-equality constituent (`strictOrder` disintegrates into `preorder` plus `!(=[a,b])`) registered ONE-SIDED at the hypothesis scope — breaking the gateways' pair invariant ([I-180](30_invariants.md#i-180)) when the mirrored orientation later arrived through the gateway.

**The choice (maintainer).** Constituents ride `sameIterationInternalMail` like the I-176 or-branch seeds — the absorb runs the full kernel pipeline, whose `addStatement` door dispatches equality shapes to the pair-registering gateways. Because the mail channel is provenance-carrying ([D-45](#d-45): every mailed statement pairs an origin; the kernel's history consumers assert presence downstream too, e.g. the disintegration-products front-origin walk), each deposit pairs a **terminal `hypothesis` origin line: one internal-only tag, zero dependencies, written at the hypo validity ONLY**. Hypothesis constituents steer proof direction but are not part of any proof: no walk continues through the line, chapters never carry the tag, and the verifier never sees it — enforced by a `buildStack` emission assert. An interim scope-keyed D-45 exemption (deposits with NO origin at `_hypo_` validities) was implemented, verified to fix the absorb, and then replaced by this design when the next presence-asserting consumer fired; exemption-spreading was rejected. A per-record no-history mail flag (schema change) and a blanket assert relaxation (Rule 19) were also rejected.

**The constraint history teaches.** The tag must never be written at the parent or main validity: the 2026-04-10 incident (commit, Gauss chapter-72 marathon) had the hypothetical-disintegration path write an `expansion` origin for its goal at `v=main` with no registered statement behind it — `buildStack` followed the orphan and aborted with "no origin found". `trackHistoryLocal=false` and the sentinel validity exist to prevent exactly that contamination; the `hypothesis` line respects it by living at the hypo scope, terminal.

**Trade-off.** A new `OriginTag` enumerator that by contract never reaches the processed proof graph — the closed-vocabulary tag machinery now contains one internal-only member (precedent: the retired `reaction to hypo` / `necessity for equality (hypo)` labels, which also never appear in chapter rows). `exprOriginMap` gains hypothesis-scope lines the old flat registration never wrote; the walker reaches them only if a real chain cites a hypo-scope statement, which the emission assert turns into a loud failure instead of a silent leak.

**Code.** `memory.hpp::OriginTag` (+ name table), `prover.cpp::disintegrateExprHypothetically` (the mail-deposit loop with the paired terminal origin), `visualizer.cpp::buildStack` (the emission assert).

<a id="d-253"></a>
## D-253 — the shortcut corpus is EXPANDED BASE FORM; the run exports load-time compiled twins for the verifier registry (2026-08-04,, maintainer-designed)

**The problem.** The shortcut's externals snapshot was compiled form (rows of `compiled_theorems.txt`). Compact names (`existence<N>` / `or<N>` / `implication<N>`) are registry-relative: once a completed full standard run regenerated `GL_binary_shared.json` with the branch's own content, the snapshot's names pointed at different or shifted operators — one expression flipped at hash burst 2 of A15's grid and the proof stalled (pool 15 rows, A15 lost). A code bisect proved the regression fix-independent: identical code yields 16 rows on the snapshot-era registry and 15 on the regenerated one. Worse, the compiled snapshot was itself a masked crash: refreshing it naively from the base-form pool first exposed the `!!` writer bug ([G-65](50_gotchas.md#g-65)).

**The choice (maintainer).** The corpus crosses RUNS, so it must be registry-independent: rows of the main `theorems.txt` in expanded base form, refreshed manually from the last full run. `prove2` compiles them at load against the live registry (`precompileStructuralOperators`) — immunity is by construction, nothing in the input can be reinterpreted. The verifier complement: chapter citations necessarily carry the run's compiled names, so `prove2` keeps the load-time compiled twins (`precompiledExternalsExport`), `run_modes.cpp::fullRun` writes them to `<theorems folder>/precompiled_external_theorems.txt`, and `process_proof_graphs.py` unions that file into the processed graph's `external_theorems.txt` — derived per run, never stored across states. Contrast [D-40](#d-40): the incubator's cross-BATCH seed stays compact because it is produced and consumed within ONE run under one registry; base form is for artifacts that cross run boundaries.

**Measured effect.** Shortcut pool byte-identical to the 16-row baseline including A15 on BOTH the snapshot-era state and a freshly regenerated state, verifier airtight in both.

<a id="d-254"></a>
## D-254 — both big runs wipe `GL_binaries` + `simple_facts` at start; the unit-test gate is disk-independent (2026-08-04,, maintainer-designed)

**The problem.** Cross-run disk state produced a bug family: a killed run's conjecturer-intermediate `GL_binary_Peano.json` failed the next run's unit-test gate (the gate runs BEFORE `full_run`'s CLEAN_RUN wipe — circular); the shortcut required a populated registry + Gauss fact tables as asserted preconditions and inherited whatever a previous run left; recovery required manual restores from the release snapshot.

**The choice (maintainer: "each big run starts from a clean/empty position").** (1) `shortcut_run` gains the same CLEAN_RUN-gated wipe `full_run` already had: `files/simple_facts` emptied, `files/GL_binaries` removed and recreated, before the batch; its two stale preconditions (populated shared registry; Gauss CE fact tables + the gauss→fta mirroring) are retired — the base-form corpus references no spontaneous names, and the shortcut's CE stage is explicitly skipped (`ConfigFTA.json` `numberIterationsConjectureFiltering: 0`; with zero fact tables it was already a defined no-op). (2) The ordis park unit test seeds an ARTIFICIAL registry entry (`existence97`, config-level operator cores, the `test_memory` synthetic-seed pattern) instead of reading the on-disk spontaneous `existence3` — the gate passes on completely empty `GL_binaries` + `simple_facts`. Every run is now a pure function of the git-tracked inputs.

**Measured effect.** Unit tests 1373/1373 on empty state; clean-start full run byte-consistent with the pre-clean-start runs; full-then-shortcut sequence produces a shortcut result identical to the standalone clean-start shortcut.

<a id="d-251"></a>
## D-251 — or-compact elements store each disjunct's TRUE polarity; every consumer negates with double-negation cancellation (2026-08-04,, maintainer-approved)

**The problem.** The or-compact registration (`prover.cpp::constructOrTheorem`) stripped the leading `!` from a negated disjunct before storing it as a `LogicalEntity` element, because elements were assumed positive end to end ("Elements are positive disjuncts"). Safe while every constructed OR had positive disjuncts (or0's `n=0 ∨ ∃pred`); broken the moment D-255 licensed ORs from directions with NEGATED heads — successor functionality's OR is `(a=b) ∨!(c=d)`, its element B was stored as `(=[c,d])`, and every expansion regenerated the FALSE compound `(a=b) ∨ (c=d)`. Broadcast into the Gauss incubator, the false rule derived an equality between two distinct anchor numerals; the equality-class rewrite then contradicted the anchor's successor fact and the I-173 anchor-contradiction tripwire killed the run.

**The choice (maintainer: "plain bug", Option A over a positive-only construction gate).** Elements carry the disjunct's real sign — registration stores the direction's head verbatim — and every consumer that rebuilds a conjunct from an element negates WITH double-negation cancellation (a negated element contributes its bare positive core). Audited every or-element consumer; the ones that assumed positivity and were fixed: `expandSignature` CASE 4, the ordis K-rule exclusion premises (`negateScratch` replaces the blind `prefixBang`), the verifier's `_build_or_from_elements` / `_build_or_subimpls_from_elements` / `_check_or_disintegration_implication` / `check_or_branch_assumption` (I-16 edits under this approval), and the HTML renderer's GL-binary or-branch. All other consumers were already polarity-safe (verbatim compares, `negateScratch`, or the cancelling `expandToBaseForm`). Byte-identical output for all-positive ORs.

**Measured effect.** The full standard run passes the Gauss incubator; combined verifier 137,656 checks / 0 failures; unit tests 1373/1373 (new mixed-polarity contract test) and verifier or-suite 64/64 (three new regressions).

<a id="d-256"></a>
## D-256 — `updateGlobal` promotes the FullBind form on every outward channel (2026-08-04,, maintainer-directed)

**The problem.** The induction-promotion path kept the as-scheduled conjecturer shape — outer binder omitting anchor slots unused beyond the anchor premise, those slots left as bare free variables (an I-4 violation in flight) — for compaction and the `theorem` origin row, FullBind-rebuilding only the registry copy. Compacting the partial-bind form lifted the unbound anchor slots into template parameters, minting `(implicationN[4,5,6])` whose elements carry the forbidden `(AnchorPeano[…,u_1,u_2,u_3])` shape (an anchor expression never holds `u_` arguments — maintainer directive) and whose verifier-mandated `compilation` citation (I-52) is a canonical body no origin row anywhere covers. Latent on `main` (no chapter walked a theorem-compact chain); exposed when the A15 negated-compound contradiction integration proved the or0-companion reverse direction by reductio instead of induction — the first walk to descend that chain died on the `buildStack` no-origin assert.

**The choice.** Compute `exprFullBind` first; compaction, the `theorem` origin row, and the registry all take it. The as-scheduled `expr` survives only where the pre-FullBind shape is required verbatim: `checkOrCompletion` (or_pairs.txt matching) and `reformulateTheorem` input (its outputs rebind themselves). `updateGlobalDirect` already promoted FullBind. A walker-side patch (treating `compilation` rows as terminal) was tried first and REVERTED by maintainer verdict — it treated the symptom.

**Measured effect.** The theorem's compact is `(implicationN[])`, its citation the FullBind body carrying the broadcast `theorem` row; the Peano chapter export runs clean.

<a id="d-255"></a>
## D-255 — OR construction runs in every save path and a single proved direction licenses the OR (2026-08-04,, maintainer-designed)

**The problem.** A15's or-headed variant (`a≤b ∨ b≤a`) never materialized despite A15 being proved, for two independent reasons. (1) The OR-construction loop lived only in `run_modes.cpp`'s compression branch; the Shortcut batch sets `skip_compression` and takes the incubator-style direct save, so the loop never ran there — the run log showed the head-switch walk recording pairs (including one whose both directions were proved rows) with zero `OR theorem constructed` lines. (2) The loop required BOTH the theorem and its head-switched companion in the proved pool; A15's companion is an alpha-variant of A15 itself, is deliberately never scheduled as its own grid (the mirror-pre-emit alpha skip), and therefore can never satisfy the membership filter.

**The choice (maintainer-directed).** (a) One shared walk — `ExpressionAnalyzer::constructOrTheoremsFromPairs` — called from BOTH save branches: after the compressor when compression is active (proved pool = survivors), directly on the raw batch output when not (proved pool = `globalTheoremList`). In the skip path the constructed OR joins `globalTheoremList` before the direct save and before `generateRawProofGraph`, so the `or_theorem` chapter and manifest row emit as in the compression path; consumed parents are filtered from the file but stay in the list so their chapters render; the OR row is written through `expandToBaseForm`; no `compiled_theorems.txt` is created in that mode. (b) Single-direction sufficiency: only the pair's source theorem must be proved. Classically `!a → b` IS `a ∨ b` (excluded middle on `a`), the companion `!b → a` is derivable from it (contraposition + double-negation elimination), and GL's reductio discharge already commits it to double-negation elimination while its predicates are decidable arithmetic statements — so the both-directions gate of [D-55](#d-55) added no logical content; it was an artifact of the head-switch grids happening to prove both mirrors. A source theorem missing from the pool (compression-pruned or vacuity-retracted) still skips — a defined pipeline state, not a failure.

**Measured effect.** See the branch commit: the Shortcut run constructs the totality OR from A15 alone (its companion unproved) and the strictOrder-or-equality OR from the antisymmetry mirror pair, with parents subsumed, verifier airtight, and runtime unchanged.

## D-257 — compound relations never install marker demand templates; fully-bound both-polarities integration retained (2026-08-04,, maintainer-designed)

**The problem.** The negated-compound integration commit is a bisected 4× shortcut regression (11.1 s at its parent → 44.9 s at it, identical inputs): it widened `updateAdmissionMap`'s demand qualification to compound relations through TWO routes — fully-bound `prepareIntegration` (both polarities, recursion-owned) and the `wrN == 1` positive marker template. The traced culprit (`(in2[rec1,12,3])` in the addition-cancellation grid, 13,224 statements, 90% `existence1` operation-totality facts) rode the marker route: its `(preorder[1,4,11,marker])` template is re-instantiated inside the integration engine for every arriving witness, and the per-witness subproof cascade admits the totality-existence witness pump in every recursion LB. Prep-attribution traps (six `prepareIntegration` callers, preorder-filtered) showed: 254/341 preorder preps come from the OLD `checkNecessityForEquality` (also on `main`, harmless); the branch-new producers are the fully-bound route (39 positive / 2 negated — the negated pair is A15's IH) and the marker route (10, all positive). A negated-only qualification gate was tried first and REJECTED: it kills the pump (12.1 s) but regresses A15, whose reductio chain also consumes positive fully-bound preps (its LB preps the dual pair `!(preorder[1,4,9,rec])` AND `(preorder[1,4,9,rec])`).

**The choice (maintainer-directed).** Compound relations participate in the demand machinery ONLY through the fully-bound route, both polarities, `partOfRecursion` — a one-free-arg compound-relation premise is a defined non-participant (`isCompoundRelation → continue` in the `wrN == 1` branch; the marker route stays operators-only, as before the integration branch).

**Measured effect (shortcut pipeline, identical inputs, traps still in for the attribution run).** 52 s → 13.5 s; `theorems.txt` 17 rows including A15; verifier 2876 checks / 0 failures airtight; unit tests 1369/1369; zero compound-relation marker templates installed. The ~3 s over the 10 s no-A15 `main` baseline is A15's genuine or-cohort and reductio work.

<a id="d-252"></a>
## D-252 — or-cohorts open on demand: route (b) product-of-disintegration unconditional, route (a) admission-map probe; everything else parks in `rejectedMapOrdis` (2026-08-03,, maintainer-designed)


**The problem.** [D-250](#d-250)'s eager admission (`allowOrDisintegration = !doNotDisintegrate` at the kernel door) proves A15 but costs 3.2× shortcut runtime (45.5 s → ~149 s): every or head opens its cohort, and the two heavy pre-emit mirror grids carry the whole gap through cohorts whose splits never contribute. RT is the campaign's main enemy; eager cohort admission is the wrong polarity.

**The choice (maintainer-designed, three reviewed blocks in `docs/fta_ladder/A15_pre/current_proof_state.md`).** Park-by-default, admit-on-demand — the same polarity the algebra/integration admission machinery uses, consuming the demands that machinery already registers:

1. **Ordis-only qualification route** in `makeNormalizedKeysForAdmission`: rules failing the regular (A)/(B)/(C) gates still install marker rules when every non-anchor element and the head are operator applications, ≥ 4 of them (head counted, anchors excluded — the maintainer-confirmed boundary; A15's corpus row 34 passes exactly at it); candidates sit at config INPUT slots, gated by head-input-slot presence (the adopted extra filter), confinement, and concreteness. Fired keys carry `ordisOnly` in the admission value; general Pass-B admission skips tagged values ("untagged wins" emergent — see [I-177](30_invariants.md#i-177)).
2. **Two-route cohort opening** at the or arm: route (b) — the restored [D-32](#d-32) product-of-disintegration signal opens unconditionally (rungs 1+2 preserved; the dominant branching source of the upper ladder); route (a) — some disjunct's product template (existence disjunct → its definition body's witness fact in marker form; operator disjunct → itself; equalities/negated → none) is already an algebra `admissionMap` key, tagged or untagged. The probe is `isAdmitted`'s prologue, read-only — the admission maps' ONE ordis touchpoint; never I-6 (`isAllowedAsOperatorInput` would admit every exists-predecessor cohort and kill parking). Route (a)'s admitted disjunct is the release STARTER (one-shot `orStarterPick` row); sequenced release is RETAINED for both routes — the only RT lever on route (b).
3. **`rejectedMapOrdis`** parking + mail revival, the full rejected-map mirror ([I-178](30_invariants.md#i-178)): park under each operator-based disjunct product template, value = the or statement + levels; `revisitRejectedOrdis` at every admission key-gain seam re-deposits the parked statement on `sameIterationInternalMail` so the absorb re-runs the whole consumption (the parked thing is a DECISION, not a fact). The re-deposit is preceded by the maintainer-approved un-know (`resetParkedOrStatementRegistries`) because the parked statement is a known local statement Site F would otherwise dedup away.

**Deliberately deferred, add-on-demand (maintainer framing: the plan grows over time).** The integration-side probe (`admissionMapIntegration`); negated disjuncts; validity-comparability widening beyond exact matching; the branch-quiescence release trigger (block 2 decision 5). The head-gate of block 1 decision 8 is the documented tightening knob if the route proves too loose.

**Measured effect (shortcut pipeline, identical inputs).** Runtime 155 s → 56.3 s with `theorems.txt` byte-identical (all 17 rows including A15 — the m-cohort admits through row 34's `ordisOnly` demand `(in2[marker,m,3])` and revives from the park), verifier 2876 checks / 0 failures airtight; the dump shows parked cohorts shrinking 5 → 2 as demands land, the surviving two parked forever — the reclaimed RT.

<a id="d-250"></a>
## D-250 — or-disintegration admitted for every real deposit; branches released one at a time in ranked order (2026-08-02,, maintainer-designed)


**The problem.** A15 (totality) stalls at the `m ≠ 0` case split: `(or0[1,int_lev_4_249,3,2])` sits at the triad LB's main but the [D-32](#d-32) admission gate requires the firing rule to be a product of disintegration, and the corpus or0 rule is not — no `_ordis_` branches mint, and the flat K-rule consumption waits forever for a negated-atom fact nothing produces. Opening branches everywhere in PARALLEL is the known explosion (D-31's history; the reverted negated-equality contradiction-scope experiment reproduced the same pathology — an assumed equality near main replicates the comparable statement population per primed witness).

**The choice (maintainer-designed).** Two coupled changes, applied uniformly to ALL cohorts:

1. **Admission everywhere.** *(SUPERSEDED by [D-252](#d-252): the override is removed, the D-32 signal is restored as route (b), and non-productOfDis heads open only on the route-(a) demand probe or park.)* `addExprToMemoryBlock`'s entry coupling becomes `allowOrDisintegration = !doNotDisintegrate` — every real deposit (corpus-fired, assumed, mail-recovered) admits or-disintegration; D-241's intro-fired suppression and every other `doNotDisintegrate` context keep blocking it, and the hypothetical-disintegration path (which calls `disintegrateExpr2` directly with a sentinel validity, bypassing the door) keeps its default `false` so no cohort ever mints at a sentinel scope. The D-32 `productOfDisintegration` plumbing stays in place, dormant (the D-241 justification-field precedent).

2. **Sequenced release.** A cohort no longer mints all K branch scopes at once — it mints NONE at creation: the bootstrap registers the full structural leaf count, queues EVERY flattened leaf in a new deloadable pending queue (`orPendingBranches`, cohortId → unreleased disjunct payload ids, tags 805..810 with the cohort's seed level run in `orPendingLevels`), and stages the cohort on the persistent `pendingOrReleases` inbox. (The bootstrap runs inside `standardProcessing`'s internal-mail drain; its step-3 `internalMailIn.clear` wipes any seed inserted into the channel being drained — the first shortcut run demonstrated exactly that silent loss — so every release, including the first, happens at the end-of-burst drain, after the clear.) `drainPendingOrReleases` (after `drainDeadOrBranches`, before the wipe drain) ranks the pending disjuncts — tier 0: everything that is not a positive equality, by descending token count (most structurally complicated first), byte-lex ties; tier 1: bare equalities; tier 2: equalities with an anchor-slot argument, dead last — and mints exactly one branch per staged cohort per burst. After the first release, the next branch releases when the live branch RESOLVES: it derives an expression matching a `toBeProved` goal on its parent chain (`ordisMerge`'s goal probe stages the cohort), or it retires refuted ([D-242](#d-242)'s drain stages it). An undecided live branch stalls its cohort — accepted degradation, no timeouts, no caps.

3. **Seed channel.** Branch seeds (the first branch at mint time and every released branch) ride `sameIterationInternalMail` — the `ordisMerge` promotion channel — with an `or disintegration` mail origin, instead of the former `orBranchStatements` → `out.statements` channel whose consumer ran `addStatement` only. The absorb runs each seed through the full kernel pipeline, so a COMPOUND disjunct (A15's `(existence3[1,m,3])` predecessor branch) decomposes like any deposited statement — under the old channel it would have sat inert.

**Why sequencing kills the explosion.** At most one branch per cohort is live; the expensive equality shape opens only after the productive branch already resolved (a free relevance gate — a useless split never reaches its equality branch); and when the equality branch does open in a descent context it refutes within a few bursts and retires + wipes (D-242) — one bounded rewrite pulse, not a standing population. `orDisjunctCount` still registers the FULL structural leaf count at mint, so convergence semantics are unchanged: a cohort converges only when every counted branch has derived the expression (retirement reduces the count in place). A15's intended closure: or0 disintegrates sequenced → branch 1 = ∃pred(m) derives the goal under the branch → releases branch 2 = `(=[m,2])` → refuted against the theorem premise → retired, count 2 → 1 → reduced-count convergence promotes the goal to main.

**Rejected alternatives (maintainer-decided).** An `it_`/`int_` argument gate on top of sequencing: the concrete-args form blocks A15's own split (m IS the witness `int_lev_4_249`); the template-chain form admits A15 but does not limit witness-instantiated firings of clean corpus rules — protection comes from sequencing + ranking, measured by the full-run comparison. Sequencing only newly-admitted cohorts (legacy productOfDisintegration cohorts staying parallel): rejected for uniformity — one code path, one semantics.

**Verification contract.** Unit tests: ranking (tiers / token count / byte-lex / negated-equality tier-0), anchor-arg collection from the LB chain, goal-probe staging, retirement staging, release drain (top-ranked release, level run, queue update, defined skips). Batch acceptance: the shortcut run proves A15 (verifier 0 failures, pool intact) and one full standard `main.py` run keeps the `theorems.txt` count at baseline with verifier 0 failures — the full run is the explicit measurement of the relaxed gate's runtime cost.

<a id="d-249"></a>
## D-249 — the FTA batch owns its anchor, tag, and registry; the corpus activates via proved connection lemmas (2026-07-31,, maintainer-specified)

**The problem.** Shortcut chapters were Gauss-anchored ([D-248](#d-248)) while the batch's new spontaneous compacts minted into the batch's own binary. The verifier's anchor-substring binary resolution (`VerifierState::binaries_for_chapter` path 1) therefore pinned every shortcut chapter to the stale `GL_binary_Gauss.json` — surfaced as 4 integration-tag failures on the first shortcut lemma to mint new compacts (A14's `strictOrder` and its inlined-existence compact). Incubator batches escape the same trap only because their anchor substrings (`Incubator3`/`Incubator8`) are not binary keys and fall into the family fallback.

The Gauss/Peano corpus stays in its original anchors and activates through TWO CONNECTION CONJECTURES at the top of the shortcut list — `(>[1..8](AnchorFTA[1..8])(AnchorPeano[1..6]))` and the AnchorGauss analog — pure slot projections the prover proves itself; anchor-headed conjectures and a derived second anchor exercise cleanly across prover, chapter export, and verifier (anchor-handling meta-checks pass). `run_modes.shortcut_run` mirrors `simple_facts_gauss*` → `simple_facts_fta*` each run because the CE filter derives fact-table filenames from the anchor name and `full_run` regenerates the folder. Supersedes D-248's naming in its item (3): `ConfigShortcut.json` / `AnchorGauss` / tag `Shortcut` → `ConfigFTA.json` / `AnchorFTA` / tag `FTA`.

<a id="d-248"></a>
## D-248 — shortcut mode: corpus-as-externals proving of a hand-written conjecture list (2026-07-31,, maintainer-specified)


**The choice.** A new pipeline mode implementing the FTA-shortcut strategy (`docs/fta_ladder/fta_shortlist.md`): the prover receives the already-proved Peano + Gauss corpus as external theorems plus a hand-maintained list of true conjectures, and proves them autonomously. Four pieces: (1) the exe's batch path accepts `--conjectures-file <path>` / `--externals-file <path>` (parsed in [`main.cpp`](../../GL_Quick_VS/GL_Quick/src/main.cpp), applied by `run_modes::fullRun` after the config sniff onto `THEOREMS_FILE` / `COMPRESSED_EXTERNAL_THEOREMS_FILE`; relative paths resolve against the project root; unknown batch-path arguments assert). (2) A new `prover_parameters.skip_compression` boolean, read only by `fullRun`'s config sniff, routes to the existing compressor-skip branch WITHOUT `incubator_mode`'s prover-semantics side effects. (3) `ConfigShortcut.json` — a copy of `ConfigGauss.json` (both anchors + full operator vocabulary) plus `anchor_name: AnchorGauss` (the prover derives the anchor as `Anchor<tag>` unless `anchor_name` overrides it — the incubator-config pattern; without it the `Shortcut` tag trips `initAnchor`'s missing-anchor assert), `theorems_folder` / `raw_proof_graph_folder` pointing into `files/shortcut/`, and `skip_compression: true`. (4) `main.py --shortcut` dispatches to `run_modes.shortcut_run` (sibling of `full_run`), which cleans the shortcut tree like any other GL folder, re-mirrors the externals snapshot (`files/shortcut/theorems/externally_provided_theorems.txt` — rows of the main `theorems.txt` in EXPANDED BASE FORM per [D-253](#d-253); the original compiled-form snapshot was retired after it silently changed meaning under a regenerated registry), runs the prover with the two file flags, and produces processed graph + HTML + verifier report inside `files/shortcut/`.

**Why.** The rung-by-rung ladder grind is over (maintainer pivot, 2026-07-31 blog *To Be or Not to Be*): GL now proves the exhaustive shortlist of human-granularity lemmas up to FTA one by one, with the previously proved corpus supplied externally rather than rediscovered. The compressor is skipped because the shortlist is deliberately granular — later lemmas cite earlier ones, so eliminating "redundant" lemmas would defeat the corpus-building purpose, and the skip also keeps `saveProvedTheoremsFiltered`'s hardcoded canonical write path from clobbering `files/theorems/` (the main pool). The grid starts anchored at `AnchorGauss`: Gauss-anchored corpus rows fire directly and the corpus's anchor-connection theorem (`AnchorGauss` premise, `AnchorPeano` head) makes the Peano rows applicable too.

**Boundaries.** `full_run` and `ceOnlyRun` are untouched; `ConfigShortcut.json` never matches `_discover_configs_for_tag`'s Peano/Gauss globs, so the main pipeline never picks it up. The externals snapshot is refreshed only by a deliberate manual step. The conjecturer does not run in shortcut mode — `conjectures.txt` is hand-maintained input.

**Verification.** Full rebuild + unit tests; baseline `main.py` full run (verifier airtight); `main.py --shortcut` proves shortlist A1 (`0 <= n`, Gauss-anchored) with the HTML proof graph and an airtight verifier report under `files/shortcut/`, main `files/theorems/` untouched.

<a id="d-247"></a>
## D-247 — cleanup retains `intStatementLevelsMap` rows; the levels row is immortal like the registration record (2026-07-31,, maintainer-approved)


**The choice.** `cleanUpExpressions`' class-canonicalization sweep drops non-canonical statements from the runtime registries (`intEncodedStatements`, `intLocalEncoded*`) ONLY. The `intStatementLevelsMap` erase that accompanied the drop is removed — a dropped statement keeps its levels row, exactly as it keeps its `intKnownStatements` registration ([I-58](30_invariants.md#i-58)). Context: an external-review finding showed the erase's scratch membership sets truncated the packed 64-bit statement keys to 32 bits (the validityId half), which suppressed almost every erase; widening the keys to int64 (the reviewer's recommended fix) made the erase effective for the first time and IncubatorGauss3 died by stack overflow on the next full run. The levels-row erase, not the key width, was the bug — retention is the contract, and the scratch sets are deleted with it.

**Why.** The registered bit is immortal and every registration path (`addNegatedEquality` / `addEquality`) skips row re-creation while it is set; the negated-equality expansion's emit gate (`emitNew`'s `lookupStatementLevels` probe) reads the levels row as its permanent already-emitted memory. An erased row with a surviving registered bit is therefore re-emittable but never re-registrable: two dropped sibling variants regenerate each other unboundedly (`addStatement` ⇄ `applyEquivalenceClassToNegatedEquality`, minidump-confirmed ~2,700 frames into the 16 MiB stack), and a dropped equality's re-arrival would trip the post-loop `intStatementLevelsMap` assert ([D-93](#d-93)). The truncation had shipped since the cleanup's statification, so retention — not erasure — is the behavior every airtight release actually ran; the levels map's growth stays bounded by the same order as the immortal registration record.

**Boundaries.** The wholesale teardowns (`wipeSubtree` / `eradicateImplicationFromLB` / `resetResentExpressionRegistries`) still erase levels rows — they retire whole items, registration included. The registry sweeps and the `intLocalEncodedStatementsSet` rebuild are unchanged.

**Verification.** `test_cleanup_levels_retention.cpp` pins the contract (the dropped row leaves the registry; both levels rows survive); full rebuild + unit tests; full-pipeline Windows run compared against the previous complete reference log.

<a id="d-232"></a>
## D-232 — the admission depth IS the witness-generation cap; `standardMaxAdmissionDepth` retired (2026-07-30,, maintainer-approved)

**What.** The standalone `standardMaxAdmissionDepth` parameter is deleted. Every site that stamped it into an admission value (`memory.cpp` Pass-B staging, the four `prover.cpp::addToHashMemory` install calls, `compressor.cpp`, `filter.cpp`) now stamps `parameters.maxIterationNumberVariable`, so `isAdmitted`'s per-value depth verdict (`mn <= v.depth`) enforces the same ceiling as request building and revival. The per-value field `AdmissionMapValue::standardMaxAdmissionDepth` keeps its name and codec layout (deload bytes untouched); only what is stamped into it changed. The config key is removed from all seven `Config*.json`; `ConfigIncubatorGauss3.json` simultaneously returns `maxIterationNumberVariable` from 5 to 1 (the 2/3/5 raises were compensating through the wrong parameter). `inductionMaxAdmissionDepth` is untouched — it remains the induction-category override.

**Why.** The rung-1 regression root cause (trap rounds 1–6, concluded 2026-07-30): the witness-generation wire stamps second-layer sum witnesses `it_1_lev_...`, and `isAdmitted` rejected every generation ≥ 1 constituent because admission values carried depth `standardMaxAdmissionDepth = 0` — the facts parked in Pass B, were correctly revived (`DRAIN-REPLAY-status` / `DRAIN-REVISIT-fire` / `REVIVE-PASS` all trap-confirmed), and were re-rejected by the same gate on absorb, forever. The `[0,1]` or-intro branch froze at 245 statements from ES2 dump burst 9 through 17 while the reference state (all witnesses `it_0`, depth 0 vacuously wide) closed rung 1 at burst 12. Two parameters answering "how deep may witness generations go" at two stations of one conveyor have no coherent split configuration: admission tighter than generation produces mint-park-revive-re-reject standing waste; admission wider is dead headroom. Pre-wire the split was invisible because every witness was generation 0.

**Operational consequence.** One knob per batch bounds the witness-generation economy end to end: request building (`filterIntEncodedStatements`), revival (`revisitRejected2` doors), and admission (`isAdmitted`). Raising it opens one additional totality layer per step at all three stations at once — a deliberate per-batch cost decision. See [I-171](30_invariants.md#i-171).

<a id="d-243"></a>
## D-243 — a Pass-B rejection commit fires the revival itself when the parked key's admission demand is already live (2026-07-29,, maintainer-approved)


**The choice.** The rejectedMap/admission machinery is a rendezvous with two arrival orders. The demand side fires `revisitRejected2` exactly once, at the moment an admission-marker key is written; the parking side (`disintegrateExpr2`'s rejection-commit loop → `updateRejectedMap`) lands whenever Pass B drains. Before this decision only one order worked: park first, demand second. The commit loop now probes `overallHashMemory.admissionMap` for the parked key's template (`mintTemplateKey(markedExpr, validity)` — the exact key the demand side writes) and, on a hit, calls `revisitRejected2` itself — whichever side arrives second wakes the other. A consumed demand was deliberately not probed (until 2026-08-22 there was a consumed-key ledger to probe; there is none now): its constituent was admitted through another route and needs no wake.

**Why.** The lost-wakeup order was latent for as long as every witness minted at generation 0: parking and demand landed in the same burst neighborhood with parking first. The witness-generation wire's honest pacing ([D-233](#d-233)) defers firing-fed parkings by a mail hop, and rung 1's ES2 route hit the reversed order: the demand for the totality-sum body probed one burst before Pass B parked it (trap evidence: `REVISIT-ENTER`/`REVISIT-nocohort` at log lines 5-6, `PARK-COMMIT` of the same key at line 46, no later demand), the cohort slept forever, no successor web formed, and rung 1 froze — the sole surviving mechanism after the generation caps (3 and 5 both measured ineffective), the revival gates, the request gates, and the disintegrationAllowed flag were each exonerated by measurement.

**Correction (2026-07-30).** Trap round 6 falsified the "cohort slept forever" mechanism claim: the sum-demand records replay and revive normally (`DRAIN-REPLAY-status` / `DRAIN-REVISIT-fire` / `REVIVE-PASS` all observed). Rung 1 froze because the revived generation-1 facts were re-rejected by `isAdmitted`'s depth verdict against `standardMaxAdmissionDepth = 0` — see [D-232](#d-232). The rendezvous hook itself is harmless and stays.

**Boundary.** Algebra side only. `updateRejectedMapIntegration` / `rejectedMapIntegration` has the same theoretical race shape but no measured instance; mirroring the probe there is a recorded option awaiting a case (its revival function and demand container differ and were not verified for this fix).

<a id="d-233"></a>
## D-233 — the firing's max-premise-iteration + 1 stamp reaches the witness mint through the disintegration-signal column (2026-07-29,, maintainer-approved)


**The choice (maintainer-specified semantics).** The witness-name generation slot (`it_<iteration>_lev_...`) means: max iteration inside the firing premises, plus one. The wire that was lost is restored end to end: `checkLocalEncodedMemoryStatic` stamps `req.maxIteration + 1` — a value it already computed as a dead local — on the head `FiringRecord` (new `iteration` field, -1 for markers; NOT part of the canonical record sort, being a pure function of the premises the comparator already orders through `originDeps`); `applyFiringRecords` writes it into the internal-mail disintegration-signal column, which widens from a packed uint8 to a packed int32 (bits 0-1 the two bools, bits 2+ `iteration + 1` so all-zero still means "nothing carried"); the absorb drain reads it back and passes it into `addExprToMemoryBlock` instead of the constant -1; `disintegrateExprCore2`'s existing `-1 → 0` mapping keeps every non-firing deposit (seeds, branch assumptions, discharge emissions, routing mail) at generation 0. On a duplicate signal write for one (expression, scope): bools keep last-write (the canonically sorted record apply fixes the order), the iteration min-merges — order-free, and a fact derivable at a lower generation IS that generation. Cross-LB propagation needs no mail change: the name itself is the carrier and receivers parse argument names.

**Why.** The IncubatorGauss3 post-proof runaway (2026-07-29, ~400-second bursts): totality rules firing on membership pairs at branch scopes minted witnesses of witnesses without bound — 33,311 witness names, every one labeled `it_0`, because the absorb pinned iteration to -1 and the mint's generation slot never moved. The containment was designed and shipped long ago — the name slot, the encoder's `argIteration`/`maxIteration` parse, `filterIntEncodedStatements`' drop of over-cap statements from request building, and the per-batch `maxIterationNumberVariable` knob — but the constant label made the cap vacuous exactly where the cascade lives. Two brakes had masked the gap historically: demand-parking (derived witness bodies revive only against marker-written admission keys, and markers rarely completed before the x-anchor exception) and budget starvation (the fact-rich phase used to arrive at bursts 14-15). The `addTheoremToMemory`-family iteration arguments are grid-building remnants with no generation content (maintainer ruling).

**Boundaries.** Only the firing path stamps; everything else legitimately mints at generation 0. The cap value stays per batch (currently 1 everywhere) — the acceptance run measures, and a chain needing deeper generations (rung-2's descent chained witness-of-witness) is a maintainer cap decision, never a bypass. The signal facet bytes (bases 455/505, values facet) widen; run-scoped, no cross-run persistence. Witness NAMES shift (`it_0` → `it_1+` for firing-derived mints), so statement identities and search trajectories move — the corpus diff is part of acceptance.

**Verification.** Full rebuild (Release x64) + `gl_quick.exe --unit-tests` green (extended cold-mail signal tests incl. min-merge and the deload round trip; new `apply_firing_records_carries_iteration_min_merged` and `deposit_iteration_reaches_witness_mint`); full-pipeline acceptance per the rung-2.1 state document (IncubatorGauss3 completes, the rung-2.1 negation theorem lands, verifier airtight, corpus diff reviewed).

## D-241 — one per-rule install-time flag decides whether fired heads may disintegrate; integration and or-intro installs derive false (2026-07-29,, maintainer-approved)


**The choice (maintainer-specified).** `LocalMemoryValue` gains `disintegrationAllowed` — may heads FIRED BY this rule be disintegrated (the rule itself is never disintegrated). Derived once, inside `addToHashMemory`, from rule-intrinsic inputs only: false when the justification is `integration` OR when the install is or-INTRO-shaped (`isOrIntroInstall`: exactly one premise, byte-equal to one flattened leaf of the or-category head — the same compiled-map flattening the emission uses); true otherwise. The firing site's rule-intrinsic read collapses to `doNotDisintegrate = !lmv.disintegrationAllowed` — the former `justification == integration` peek is deleted (that line was the justification's ONLY behavioral consumer; the field remains as provenance metadata for the history word and the sacred dump's `just=`). The D-29 firing-context clauses (anchor LB, premise locality) stay at the firing site and can only further restrict.

**Why.** The or-intro rules (D-237) installed indistinguishably as "implication"-justified rules whose `u_`-carrying premises pass the D-32 `productOfDisintegration` gate — so every intro-fired `or<N>` head opened a full `_ordis_` branch cohort. An intro-derived or is stated FROM a true leaf at the same scope: its designed consumption is FLAT (the membership-intro clause, the K rules), and a case split over it is redundant by construction while acting as a recursive fan-out multiplier (branch assumptions breed equalities ex falso; equalities re-fire the intro rules; or statements appear inside branch scopes) — the amplifier behind the killed `D-234` acceptance run's runtime explosion. Shape detection at install — never a plumbed emission flag — is load-bearing: intro rules travel cross-LB as compact `(implication<N>)` statements and re-install receiver-side via status-3 recovery through the same drain, where an emission flag would be lost.

Markers install with the default `true` (never read on their path). The LMV blob's fixed prefix grows 18 → 19 bytes (`Codec<LocalMemoryValue>` / `appendLmvIdsRecord` / `LmvBlobView` / `lmvBlobValidityId` edited together per their layout-coupling contract); run-scoped only, the sacred dump format unchanged. Known trajectory effects: the FiringRecord sort includes `doNotDisintegrate`, so apply order moves for affected records (deterministic), and proofs that closed only via convergence over intro-fired branches may shift — the acceptance run's emission-level diff decides.
