<a id="d-234"></a>
## D-234 — a positive anchor-category statement passes the axed-variable deposit filter; flag-gated, default OFF (2026-07-28,, maintainer-approved; disabled 2026-07-29, maintainer-directed)


**Status.** DISABLED by default. The mechanism is preserved behind `ProverParameters::axed_anchor_exception` (config key `axed_anchor_exception`, default `false`, set by no shipped config). The maintainer disabled it for the rung-2.1 branch closure: a live x-anchor does not open just the one rule the rung needed — it opens the external anchor's ENTIRE rule universe at x-arguments (an x-ed anchor triggering another anchor), and the acceptance runs exploded IncubatorGauss3's runtime (~80 s class → ~30 min prover phase, runs killed or crashed; see the rung-2.1 state document). Re-enabling for a future rung is a config-key flip on a successor branch.

**The choice (maintainer-selected from the rung-2.1 analysis).** `addExprToMemoryBlock`'s axed-variable containment — the entry gate dropping every deposit that carries an `intAxedVariables` x-copy name in any argument slot — gains one exception: a POSITIVE anchor-category expression (`IntEncodedExpr::isAnchor && !negation`) deposits normally. The consequence: when an anchor-bridge rule (`AnchorIncubator3[1..9] ⟹ AnchorPeano[1,2,3,4,5,6]` and kin) fires on the x-copied batch anchor, its conclusion — the EXTERNAL anchor's x-form, e.g. `(AnchorPeano[1,x2,3,4,5,x6])` — becomes a live statement instead of surviving only as an `exprOriginMap` history line. External-anchor-premise rules (the antisymmetry theorem and every future cross-anchor external) can then bind element arguments at anchor slot values, exactly as batch-anchor-premise rules already do through `prehandleAnchor`'s copy.

**Why.** The rung-2.1 closure trace proved the element-vs-anchor-slot collision: an anchor-premise rule's normalized request key treats the anchor slots as positional variables of the same key as the element variables, so an instance binding an element to an anchor value (numeral 1 = `AnchorPeano` slot 6) can never match — zero antisymmetry firings on the (1,2) pair at any scope, while 5,672 firings cite the x-copied incubator anchor with elements at anchor numerals. The copied-anchor mechanism is the engine's designed answer to this collision class, the bridge firing that extends it to external anchors ALREADY runs (its history row is in both traced LBs), and the sole blocker was this filter's early return. The alternatives — extending `prehandleAnchor` to synthesize external-anchor forms in the pre-pass, or the contra-LB x-set inheritance contract — reach further for the same rung result; the exception is one bounded gate change with the honest implication origin already being exported.

**Boundaries.** Positive anchor statements only. Negated anchor forms stay filtered: a derived `!(AnchorXxx[…,x…])` at `main` would pair against the live positive form as a spurious premise inconsistency under [D-236](#d-236). Non-anchor x-carrying deposits stay filtered — the containment against derived x-fact breeding is unchanged. Growth is bounded at one statement per external anchor per LB (Site F dedups re-derivations). The contra-LB x-set inheritance contract (x-set = parent's ∪ seed variables) remains an open direction, orthogonal to this change.

**Verification.** Full rebuild (Release x64) + `gl_quick.exe --unit-tests` green (`axed_anchor_exception` suite: non-anchor x-deposit filtered, positive x-anchor deposits when enabled, positive x-anchor filtered at the default, negated x-anchor filtered even when enabled, x-free control unaffected); full-pipeline closure runs with the flag at its default off.

<a id="d-236"></a>
## D-236 — a normal LB's main contradiction deactivates its subtree and suppresses every emission below it (2026-07-28,, maintainer-approved)


**The choice (maintainer-specified).** `dischargeContradiction`'s formerly inert normal-LB fall-through becomes the fourth discharge role: when an LB with no special role (not primed, not CE, not recursion) holds a full E / !E pair at exact `main`, its premise set is inconsistent — the LB sets the new `Memory::mainContradiction` flag, deactivates, and stages its subtree on `pendingSubtreeDeactivations`; the post-join `drainSubtreeDeactivations` (next to the twin drain) deactivates every descendant. Emission is gated at the single-threaded seams: `UpdateGlobalDirectRec` now carries its producer LB, `drainUpdateGlobalDirect` and the induction promotion in `updateGlobal` suppress any theorem whose producer has a flagged self-or-ancestor (`hasContradictedAncestor`). At the batch root or an anchor premise LB the state asserts — the axioms are consistent, so it can only mean a broken definition set.

**Why.** The antisymmetry unlock produced conjectures with jointly inconsistent premises (the chapter-167 limitSet × interval cross-pair): their negated-head reductio LBs discharged on premises-only contradiction pairs, exporting vacuous theorems whose records cite a seed the proof never used — exactly what the verifier's `contradiction trace` check flags. The suppression is the GL-native form of the ATP world's `ContradictoryAxioms` verdict: a refutation that never consumed the negated goal must not be reported as a theorem. The discrimination is exact and Rule-16-clean: a genuine reductio's parent holds NO contradiction (the seed lives only in the child), while a premises-only pair is derivable at the parent from the same mail commits and broadcast rules — and with no burst caps the parent completes its chain no later than any child. Decision inputs are live statement state (`intKnownStatements`), never the origin map.

**Boundaries.** The contradicted LB's descendants are deactivated with the twin-drain flip contract (`isActive` + `contradictionTheoremId` cleared; `dischargedForever` untouched, so no barrier assert). Genuine reductio proofs, the CE filter, and the recursion vacuous-truth branch are byte-unaffected. The sort key of the emission drain is unchanged (`(theorem bytes, coreId)`), so surviving emission order is identical.

**Verification.** Full rebuild + `--unit-tests` green (new `vacuous_premise_suppression` suite: flag + deactivation, no-pair control, subtree drain over both contradiction polarities, ancestor-walk cases); full-pipeline acceptance per the rung-2.1 antisymmetry state document (vacuous limitSet rows drop from the corpus, the chapter-167 `contradiction trace` failure disappears, both graphs airtight).

**The choice (maintainer-specified).** When `addTheoremToMemory`'s disintegrated chain contains two positive premises of the same operator whose argument lists are equal except exactly two swapped positions (`P[..,x,..,y,..]` / `P[..,y,..,x,..]`) and the head is an equality over exactly that pair, the innermost premise LB receives one dead-end variable-copy axiom `(=[x,x_copy])` (status 0, `main`, `variableCopy` origin, the LB-creation paired mailOut write) — `x` being the swapped argument that appears first left-to-right. Detection is the pure helper `detectAntisymmetryCopyVar` ([`prover.cpp`](../../GL_Quick_VS/GL_Quick/src/prover.cpp)); the deposit reuses the exact `checkNecessityForEquality` pattern and is the FOURTH emission site of the established `(=[Y,Y_copy])` free-axiom contract (`variable copy` verifier tag, unchanged).

The copy equality re-names one occurrence: the equivalence class generates all-distinct statement variants (both members are ordinary-tier and apply equally), the associativity marker completes within the standard distinct-secondary cap (premise witnesses are `int_lev`-family and cap-invisible), the parked witness revives, and the copy equality itself serves as cancellation's equality premise. No matching-engine change, no configuration change, no multiplication.

## D-237 — an or-shaped implication premise emits per-leaf intro implications (2026-07-27,, maintainer-approved)


**The choice (maintainer-specified).** When `disintegrateExprCore2`'s implication branch installs a compiled implication whose premise element is a disjunction (the compiled-map probe `compiledEntity(core)->category == "or"`), it also emits one INTRO implication per flattened disjunct — `(>[bound](D_k)(orPremise))` — through the same `collected.insertImpl` channel as the main rule. The leaves come from a compiled-map twin of `flattenOrLeaves` (per-level signature→instance argument substitution on the string tier, recursing into or-category elements only), and both leaf and head are fed to `reconstructImplicationFullBindScratch` in RAW element form so every argument keeps its `u_` status — `u_` arguments stay free, the changeable element variable binds. History: each intro rule carries an `expansion` origin whose dependency is the compact implication statement itself, the same chapter-capable antecedent the main rule's expansion record cites.

**Why.** The K mutual-exclusion implications ([D-211](#d-211)) are the flat elimination half of an OR's consumption; nothing supplied the introduction half, so a single true disjunct could never state the disjunction as a fact. Rung 2.1's reductio stalls exactly there: the enumeration description's membership-intro rule (`or ⇒ w∈M`) is installed but can never fire, because the disjunction statement for the concrete element ("2=0 ∨ 2=1 ∨ 2=2") has no producer — its only true disjunct is reflexive, and the flag-off engine consumes reflexive facts solely through equality1 witness aliasing. With the intro rules, the already-live alias fact `2_copy = 2` states the disjunction at the copy, membership follows, and the reductio's remaining chain (verified installed) runs at rung-1-era cost — no implication multiplication anywhere. The intro rule `D_k ⇒ (D_1 ∨ … ∨ D_n)` is propositionally valid unconditionally, so the family adds no soundness surface.

**Boundaries.** Premise elements only — an or-shaped implication HEAD emits nothing new (the elimination direction already handles it). The emission preserves the instruction graph untouched (`prepareIntegrationCore` still recurses only into existence/and/or); the or premise resolves through the compiled map because implication elements have no graph entities. An I-4 tripwire asserts every changeable head variable occurs in the leaf premise (the current or family repeats the element variable in every disjunct; a shape that does not is a new design, never a silent emission). The verifier accepts the new expansion shape additively (companion change, same commit series).

**Verification.** Full rebuild (Release x64) + `gl_quick.exe --unit-tests` green (new `or_intro_rules.es3_membership_intro_conjunct_emits_per_leaf_intros` — the three ES3 intro chains install with `u_` status preserved — and `or_intro_rules.atomic_premises_emit_no_intro`). Full-pipeline acceptance: the rung-2.1 negation theorem emits, verifier zero failures, tracked theorem artifacts unchanged.

<a id="d-240"></a>
## D-240 — a contradiction-LB disproof wipes the parent goal's entire integration machinery at the parent's next end-of-burst drain (2026-07-30,, maintainer-proposed)


**The problem.** A primed `__contradiction__` LB that proves `negate(seed)` emits the disproof as an ordinary negated theorem — but nothing removed the parent's now-dead goal from `intToBeProved`, so every piece of integration machinery the goal spawned (subproof scopes, orint branches, hypo scopes, admission/rejection rows, hash rules, internal-mail revival traffic, origin history) kept running every burst forever. Measured on the Gauss-incubator-3 disproof of `(interval[1,4,2,7,10])`: the dead tree was ~57% of the `(EnumerationSet2[2,6,10])` LB's final statement population.

**The mechanism.** Two seams, both single-threaded:
1. **Deposit** — `drainUpdateGlobalDirect` (the post-join theorem drain): for every emitting producer with `primedForContradiction`, the contradiction seed (the `__contradiction__` exprKey suffix, I-165) is minted into the parent's new `Memory::pendingDisprovedGoals` (a byte-key set on the never-deloaded persistent arena, the I-108 pattern — writable while the parent is cold, no claim) and the parent's `hasWork` is raised (I-153). The deposit is unconditional for primed producers: a complement-twin seed or an already-closed goal misses the probe below — a defined no-op, and exactly one twin ever fires (D-224 retirement). *(The complement-twin no-op is superseded: the drain now settles the PROOF direction too — [D-279](#d-279).)*
2. **Drain** — the new `ExpressionAnalyzer::drainDisprovedGoals`, running in `performElemPhase3` immediately BEFORE the `pendingWipeScopes` drain (so the wipes land the same burst). Per seed that hits a MAIN goal: erase the goal row; enumerate every MAIN-level scope whose payload embeds the goal (the `<goal>_subproof_` shapes plus the two hypo shapes) onto `pendingWipeScopes` + `intValidityNamesToFilter` — EXCEPT a subproof root whose product (bare compact / OR signature) is already a REGISTERED statement at main: that subproof CLOSED before the disproof, its scope was wiped by the success path, and its product + preserved history are load-bearing for other proofs (skipping it fixed a `buildStack: no origin found` chapter-export abort in verification); erase the goal-template gates (`integrationPrepared` / `integrationPreparedMarker` MAIN rows matching the goal / its marker forms / a goal-prefixed template — `templateMatchesGoalWithMarkers` — and `integrationStartIntMap`); erase `exprOriginMap` rows keyed in the wiped subtrees plus MAIN rows whose key CONTAINS the goal text (excepting the products: `negate(goal)` and anchor-rooted theorem rows — a first-draft "cites a dead compact" rule was unsound because per-goal duplication lets a dead subproof share its bare compact text with a CLOSED subproof of another goal); erase internal-mail ORIGIN runs at wiped scopes (`ColdMail::filterOrigins` — `wipeSubtree` filters only statements, and orphaned origins would sit in the discharge-surviving container forever); erase `orDisjunctCount` / `orBookkeeping` cohorts whose parent validity lies in a wiped subtree. Subtree membership for the origin / cohort sweeps is the decoded-validity TEXT gate against the wiped root names — origin keys pack originInterner ids in BOTH halves (I-91), never NameMap ids.

**Two deliberate deviations, disproof-path-only.** (a) The origin-map erase deviates from `wipeSubtree`'s I-44 preserve rule — maintainer-approved at session planning: a dead goal's integration history documents a process that produced nothing, and the disproof's own record lives in the `__contradiction__` LB (D-51). (b) The cohort erase deviates from I-167's cohort-key retention. Both run ONLY in `drainDisprovedGoals`; `Memory::wipeSubtree` and the success path are untouched.

**What is deliberately NOT wiped.** The disproof products (the negated statement at main, its origin rows, the compacted disproof rule, the global theorem), `integrationStartIntMap`'s monotonic-counter siblings (G-43), interner dictionary rows (append-only id stability), and NameMap `idToName`/`idToSub` entries.

**Known limitation (flagged).** Seeds match MAIN goals verbatim; a goal rewritten by equivalence classes between spawn and disproof would miss the probe indistinguishably from the complement-twin miss. Incubator batches (the only ones running the contradiction pipeline today) skip equivalence classes, so the path is not exercised; see the validity-stack chapter's Weaknesses entry.

**Verification.** Full rebuild + unit tests green (`prover.drain_disproved_goals_wipes_goal_machinery`, `prover.template_matches_goal_with_markers`, `cold_mail.filter_origins_scope_sweep`); the branch acceptance is the before/after hashburst-trace comparison on the Gauss-incubator-3 disproof — zero remnants of the dead goal's integration machinery in the final EXIT dump outside the sanctioned product/dictionary classes.

<a id="d-239"></a>
## D-239 — goal-driven integration scopes minted on MAIN embed the root goal in their payload; prep gates are goal-qualified; per-goal subproof duplication accepted (2026-07-30,, maintainer-proposed)


**The choice (maintainer-proposed design).** When a contradiction LB disproves a `toBeProved` goal, the parent LB must wipe every piece of machinery the goal's integration spawned — but the sub-implication and OR-integration scopes carried no link to the goal that triggered them (`main_boundary_(implication22[1,4,2,7,10])` names the compact, not the owner). The link now lives in the validity payload: `prepareIntegrationCore2`'s Case A / Case OR mints on MAIN with a non-empty `rootGoal` produce `<goal>_subproof_<bare>` payloads (`<bare>` = the legacy shape), parsed by `ExpressionAnalyzer::splitSubproofPayload` / `stripSubproofPrefixView`. The root goal threads down as a new `prepareIntegration` / `prepareIntegrationCore2` parameter: the status-2 goal insert and `checkNecessityForEquality`'s premise preparations pass the goal; admission / marker replays and the load-time prefill pass pass empty (statement-driven machinery stays bare — a defined bivalent contract, not a fallback). Deeper mints need no embedding: they nest inside a main-level scope in the `validityNodes` forest and ride its subtree wipe (verified against the Gauss-incubator-3 diagnosis dump: the dead goal's entire machinery hangs off four main-level scope families).

**Gates goal-qualified.** The Case A / Case OR `integrationPrepared` gate templates use the SAME goal-prefixed string, so a second goal needing an equal compact preps its OWN subproof — otherwise wiping the first goal's scopes would leave the second goal gated off with no machinery. Consequence, explicitly accepted by the maintainer: two goals sharing a subimplication duplicate its subproof work (per-goal scopes). The `registered` product check stays on the BARE compact: a compact already proven as a statement needs no subproof under any goal.

**Consumers taught the prefix (same commit).** `classifyOrScope` / `classifyOrScopeView` classify by the bare half; `closeScopedGoal`'s NotOrScope closure deposits the stripped bare compact at main. Verifier / postprocessing / visualizer learn the format in the companion commit of the same branch.

**Alternatives rejected.** A statified goal→scope side registry (no artifact churn, no duplication) — rejected by the maintainer: the goal link belongs in the auditable artifact, not in invisible prover state, and a registry adds a deload-enrolled container the name already provides.

**Verification.** Full rebuild + `gl_quick.exe --unit-tests` green (`str_ops.split_subproof_payload_grammar`, `prover.core2_goal_carrying_scope_payloads`, extended `classify_or_scope_view_twin`); full-pipeline disproof-cleanup gate per the cleanup decision of the same branch.

<a id="d-242"></a>
## D-242 — an `_ordis_` branch whose asserted disjunct is refuted retires at end-of-burst: subtree wiped, cohort shrunk in place, convergence re-checked at the reduced count (2026-07-30,, maintainer-directed)


**The problem (the OPEN-1 acceptance case).** Contradiction discharge is main/main only (D-222), so an `_ordis_` branch whose asserted disjunct is provably false was never closed — it ran the full machinery under an inconsistent premise, breeding equality-class merges and argument variants ex falso, and its cohort's convergence count could never be reached. Measured on the rung-2.1 reference run (`(EnumerationSet3[2,6,7,10])`, IncubatorGauss3): the two numeral cohorts' four dead branches (`0=2` / `1=2` under the `p≤1` clause subproof, `0=1` / `2=1` at main) held 9,086 of 13,354 final live statements — 68% — while the two true branches held one statement each, and `orBookkeeping` carried 8,472 rows dominated by absurd booked products (`!(=[x,x])` shapes).

**The mechanism.** Two seams, both single-threaded, both heap-free (Rule 28):
1. **Detection** — a probe inside `ordisMerge` (the canonical per-`_ordis_`-deposit function, reached from both deposit paths): when the deposit scope classifies `Disintegration`, the branch's asserted disjunct (the payload's wrapped body) is negated on string-scratch and probed `known` at the branch scope and each ancestor (`parentOf` walk to main; non-minting lookups on every path). A hit stages the branch vid on the new `Memory::pendingDeadOrBranches` (pod-key set on the never-deloaded persistent arena, the `pendingDisprovedGoals` pattern). `known` is the sound bit: the record is immortal (I-58) and a scope's fact set is monotone, so a once-derived refutation stays a refutation. Already-staged and already-filtered branches skip the probe.
2. **Drain** — `ExpressionAnalyzer::drainDeadOrBranches`, running in `performElemPhase3` after `drainDisprovedGoals` (wholesale-retired cohorts are gone first; a staged branch whose cohort has no `orDisjunctCount` row is the defined disproof-retired skip) and before the `pendingWipeScopes` drain (the branch wipes land the same burst). Per staged branch: queue the subtree wipe + `intValidityNamesToFilter` (a filtered branch never receives a deposit again, so it never re-stages — retirement is permanent); decrement the cohort's `orDisjunctCount` in place; rebuild every `orBookkeeping` run of the cohort without the dead branches' disjunct entries via the existing `eraseSetIf` + `insertSorted` doors (an only-dead run leaves the container); then re-check convergence — a surviving row whose run reaches the reduced count re-fires through `ordisMerge` itself, the canonical promotion path (a missing levels row at the survivor branch is the already-converged defined skip). **Zero survivors** (every disjunct refuted — the acceptance run hits it inside the primed reductio LB at IncubatorGauss3 burst 4) retires the cohort wholesale: the count row leaves the container and every bookkeeping run empties in the surgery; the joint contradiction the fully-refuted disjunction implies is surfaced by the pre-existing machinery — the parent-scope K mutual-exclusion rules hold all the refutations, fire the last disjunct as a fact, and the resulting statement/negation pair drives the primed discharge (a reductio LB) or the vacuous-premise flag + global-theorem reversion ([D-244](#d-244)) for a normal LB at main. The third outcome is maintainer-confirmed: a cohort under a DEEPER hypothetical scope of a normal LB can also lose every branch — the refuted disjunction only proves that scope's assumption unsatisfiable, the enclosing clause is vacuously true, the pair never reaches main/main, and the LB and its theorems stay valid; the retirement still deletes the ex-falso factories.

**Run-cleaning is a soundness requirement, not tidiness.** A stale dead entry inflates a run against the reduced count, so a convergence could fire that no surviving branch ever derived — a fact promoted to the parent on ex-falso evidence alone. Dead entries are removed before any count comparison.

**In-place reduction, not a successor cohort.** The chapter's older design sketch ("retire the old cohort, mint a successor over the survivors") was not taken: cohort identity stays the `(parentValidity, originalOrSignature)` pair (I-167 untouched), the count and runs shrink in place, and no new identity appears in any artifact.

**No parent-scope reductio emission.** Detection requires the refutation to already be `known` at the branch or an ancestor — the reductio product pre-exists with its own history, so emitting a duplicate would add no information and would need a new origin-tag surface for nothing.

**History kept (I-44).** Branch-subtree `exprOriginMap` rows survive: an earlier full-cohort convergence cites dead-branch derivations as `or convergence` ingredients, and the chapter walker must still resolve them (the disproof drain's origin-erase deviation does NOT extend here).

**Verifier surface — closed by [D-238](#d-238).** The deferral ended when the activation run exported the first reduced-cohort convergence row and `check_or_convergence` rightly rejected it; the follow-on decision makes the retirement artifact-visible (retired-disjunct record + reductio ingredients in the row) with the maintainer-consented checker extension (I-16).

**Verification.** Full rebuild + 1344/1344 unit tests (`prover.drain_dead_or_branches_retires_refuted_branch` — staging, dedup skip, wipe + filter, count 3→2, run surgery incl. only-dead row removal, reduced-count re-fire promoting to main, disproof-retired no-op, zero-survivor wholesale retirement); branch acceptance is the before/after hashburst-trace comparison on the ES3 LB (reference ).

<a id="d-244"></a>
## D-244 — an unintentionally contradictory LB retracts its already-submitted global-theorem rows (2026-07-30,, maintainer-directed)


**The problem (maintainer-raised during the dead-branch acceptance).** The vacuous-premise machinery suppresses a contradicted LB's theorems **at emission** (`hasContradictedAncestor` gates at `drainUpdateGlobalDirect` and the induction promotion) — but an LB can submit theorems in earlier iterations and only later derive its main-scope statement/negation pair. Those rows were already in `globalTheoremList` (and `fullTheoremList`), would ship in `theorems.txt` / the chapters, and nothing retracted them.

**The mechanism (maintainer-directed: "revert the entry in the global theorem list").** Producer attribution + a post-join sweep:
1. `appendGlobalTheorem` gains a `producer` parameter recorded in the parallel `globalTheoremProducers` vector (same mutex, same door, cleared with the export rebuild). Threaded at the direct path (`drainUpdateGlobalDirect` → `updateGlobalDirect` → the direct / reformulated / back-reformulated appends), the induction promotion, and the already-derived-head registration; producer-less paths (or-theorem construction, debug export) record `nullptr` and are never retracted.
2. `revertVacuousGlobalTheorems`, called once per iteration in the post-join seam right after `drainUpdateGlobalDirect`: every row whose producer has a contradicted self-or-ancestor leaves `globalTheoremList` + `globalTheoremProducers`, its string leaves the `globalTheoremStrings` dedup set (a later legitimate prover of the same statement may re-append), and matching `fullTheoremList` rows leave. Prints `[VACUOUS-REVERT] <theorem>` for observability. Grid LB pointers are address-stable for the whole batch (I-109; discharged LBs persist for the chapter export), and a normally-discharged LB can never flip afterwards (no new facts), so the attribution stays readable exactly as long as it is needed.

**Primed LBs are exempt by construction.** A `__contradiction__` LB's contradiction is the intended reductio; it never carries `mainContradiction`, so disproof theorems are never retracted.

**Known residual (flagged, not silent).** The theorem's earlier broadcast as a hash rule into other LBs is NOT undone — the retraction covers the proved-theorem record and everything derived from it downstream of the run (artifacts, exports, next-batch pools). Undoing in-run rule contamination would need rule-level provenance eradication; raised as out of scope for this decision.

**Verification.** `theorem_sink_dedup.vacuous_producer_rows_are_reverted` (self + descendant retraction, clean/producer-less rows stay, dedup string freed for re-prove, `fullTheoremList` swept); full-pipeline acceptance run of the dead-branch branch.

<a id="d-238"></a>
## D-238 — a reduced cohort's `or convergence` row cites the retired branches' refutations, and `check_or_convergence` accepts the two entry forms (2026-07-30,, maintainer-approved incl. the I-16 verifier change)


**The forcing case.** The axed-anchor activation run exported the first convergence of a dead-branch-shrunk cohort: incubator chapter row `(preorder[N,+,i2,v1]) main or convergence (or2[i0,v2,i1,i2]) main` with ONE branch entry — the survivor `v2=2` — for a three-disjunct OR. `check_or_convergence` rightly rejected it (`or convergence: success 5, failure 1`, the only red check of the run): the row asserted a case analysis without accounting for two of the three cases. The row was semantically sound (the two dead branches' assumptions are refuted at main, with their own derivations) but evidentially incomplete.

**The design (maintainer-approved, both halves).**
1. **Producer.** `drainDeadOrBranches` records each retired disjunct with the SHALLOWEST scope where its negation is `known` (re-running the staging probe's ancestor walk; shallowest so the row cites the fact where it genuinely lives, typically `main`, not an inherited rewrite inside the dead branch) on the new `Memory::orRetiredDisjuncts` — cohortId → sorted packed `(disjunctId, refutationScopeVid)` pairs, persistent arena, reclaimed at discharge. `ordisMerge`'s convergence history then appends, per retired disjunct, the reductio ingredient `(negate(D_i), refutationScope)` after the survivor ingredients — the exported row again has one entry per flattened disjunct.
2. **Verifier (explicit I-16 consent).** `check_or_convergence` steps 4-7 become per-entry classification: each of the K entries is EITHER a survivor entry (`C` at that branch's exact `_ordis_` scope, matched to its disjunct via the scope payload) OR a retired entry (`negate(D_i)` at a parent-visible scope — the parent, an ancestor, or the retired branch itself for an ex-falso self-refutation), with exactly-once coverage of all K disjuncts and per-entry chapter evidence. Full-cohort rows validate exactly as before (all-survivor entries).

**Why the negation, not the branch scope, is the retired entry.** A retired branch has no derivation of `C` at its scope (it was wiped, and citing an ex-falso derivation would be evidentially worthless anyway); the true justification for dropping the case is the refutation of its assumption, which has its own chapter-capable derivation. The row now reads as the textbook case analysis: prove `C` in every live case, discharge every dead case by reductio.

**Verification.** Python verifier suite 373/373 (7 new or-convergence tests: mixed-row positive, self-refutation-in-branch positive, negation-not-a-disjunct, non-visible scope, double-cover, missing evidence, plus the old contract intact); C++ 1344/1344 (drain test extended: retired record content + the re-fired convergence origin citing survivors and the reductio ingredient); the branch acceptance is the full-pipeline run returning to 0 verifier failures.

<a id="d-245"></a>
## D-245 — vacuous truths are classified post-batch and filtered out of the deliverable pool (2026-07-30,, maintainer-directed)


**The judgment (maintainer).** A vacuously true theorem — one whose premise set is unsatisfiable — carries no mathematical content and must not ship: it is classified as vacuous and filtered/compressed out after the batch, the same way the compressor removes redundant theorems. The precedent is the vacuity-detection judgment of model checking (a property passing by antecedent failure is a warning, not a result — Beatty & Bryant's antecedent failure; Beer/Ben-David/Eisner/Rodeh and Kupferman/Vardi's vacuity detection), combined with dependency-directed retraction in the Truth-Maintenance-System sense (Doyle's JTMS, de Kleer's ATMS): GL's proof graph already IS the justification structure, so retraction is a post-batch artifact pass.

**Two certificates seed the class, one closure completes it:**
1. **Producer-flag retraction** ([D-244](#d-244)): theorems whose producer LB derived its own main-scope contradiction — retracted in-run; now also recorded (`ExpressionAnalyzer::retractedVacuousTheorems`).
2. **Premise-contradiction pairs** (`ExpressionAnalyzer::classifyVacuousPremisePairs`, run in `fullRun` post-prove BEFORE compression and every proved-theorem save): two proved theorems with the same premise-chain multiset (sorted `ce::disintegrateImplication` chains) and heads `X` / `negate(X)` jointly refute their shared premise set — no single LB need ever hold the contradiction, so the producer flag cannot catch this class; every theorem on the certified chain leaves the pool (`[VACUOUS-PREMISE-PAIR]` print), never reaches `theorems.txt` / `compiled_theorems.txt`, never feeds a later batch, and never receives a chapter.
3. **Taint closure** (`run_modes.py::_filter_vacuous_tainted`, run after every batch before the next batch reads the pool): a theorem whose proof cites a vacuous theorem — directly or transitively through the chapter citation graph (`theorem` / `externally provided theorem` rows) — is itself classified `tainted` and filtered from the deliverable pool; its chapter is KEPT (the derivation is honest and auditable, it merely rests on a vacuous fact). This closes the flagged broadcast residual of the reversion decision.

**Artifact.** `files/theorems/vacuous_theorems.txt` (cleared at run start with its siblings): `<theorem>\t<label>` rows, labels `retracted producer` / `premise contradiction` / `tainted` — the classification record and the taint pass's seed set.

**Care point (soundness of certificate 2).** The pair certifies vacuousness only for genuinely identical premise chains — same multiset after the pipeline's canonical forms; fuzzy matching across reformulated variants is deliberately out of scope.

**Verification.** `theorem_sink_dedup.vacuous_premise_pairs_classified_out` (chain-group classification incl. the non-contradictory third head, unrelated chain survives, dedup frees, aligned vectors follow; no-contradiction no-op); `tests/test_vacuity_filter.py` (direct + transitive taint retire the dependents, paired pool files shrink in lockstep, `tainted` labels land, missing/empty seed set is a no-op — the citation graph rides `verifier.load_global_theorem_list` / `build_chapter_theorem_map` over the RAW tree, read-only, I-16 untouched); full-pipeline acceptance run on the branch.

<a id="d-246"></a>
## D-246 — Peano main formulates `preorder` and two-`=` conjectures; the dichotomy filter rejects relation-only arguments instead of asserting (2026-07-27,, maintainer-approved)


**The choice (maintainer-specified).** Rung 2.1's two missing lemmas — antisymmetry `a≤b ∧ b≤a ⇒ a=b` and the cancellation family `a+n=b ∧ a=b ⇒ n=0` — are formulated by the main Peano batch through config alone: `ConfigPeano.json` gains a `preorder` entry (count cap 2, leaf caps 3/3) and raises `=`'s count cap from 1 to 2. Containment keeps the emission delta small: `preorder` may co-occur only with `=` and itself (`prohibited_combinations`), never as a head (`prohibited_heads`), never with numeral element arguments or the `*` slot (`patterns_to_exclude` pins, Gauss-adapted); two-positive-`=` chains are barred alongside `in`/`in2`/`preorder`, restricted to a variable-variable premise, and when equality-headed forced to the canonical ascending `(=[2,…])` head. The patterns are written to the linear-scan idiom (`^`-anchored, `[^=]*` hops between equality atoms — the `=` character occurs only inside `(=[` atoms); the first-draft unanchored `(?=(?:.*X){2})` lookahead forms cost ~10x Peano conjecturer wall time (200 s vs 47 s) for identical semantics. Measured: the Peano pool grows 937 → 1001 rows (+4 preorder rows including the antisymmetry target, +60 cancellation-family rows including negated-premise variants), zero baseline rows lost.

**The companion code change.** `evaluateOperatorExprs2`'s end-operator dichotomy block asserted that every relation argument is classifiable from operator/property/anchor membership — a precondition true only while a conjecture could hold at most one relation-bucket-only atom. Two `=` atoms can share an argument that appears in relations alone; the block now classifies such an argument as neither-input-nor-output and **rejects** the candidate (the pre-existing `classify` lambda already yields exactly that), replacing the assert. The rejected class is pure variable-aliasing junk, and neither target is affected (the block requires ≥2 end-operators; cancellation has one operator, antisymmetry none).

**Why config over template.** [D-215](#d-215)'s warning against raising the `=` cap batch-wide targeted the unconstrained space; the pattern set above bounds it, and `=`'s `max_size_expression_after_existence` cap of 3 independently keeps every equality-carrying conjecture at three atoms — D-215's own 4-atom injectivity shape stays addon-only regardless, so the template addon and this cap raise are complementary, not competing.

**Verification.** Full rebuild (Release x64) + `gl_quick.exe --unit-tests` 1312/1312 green; conjecturer-only A/B on Peano (937 → 1001, both targets byte-verified present, zero baseline loss); full-pipeline gate + verifier per the rung-2.1 trail entry of the same date.

<a id="d-231"></a>
## D-231 — the LB split is gated by the per-config `lb_split` flag; the hard incubator exclusion is retired (2026-07-26,, maintainer-approved)


**The choice (maintainer-approved).** Whether a batch runs the statistics-driven LB split ([D-201](#d-201)) is a per-config decision. A new `prover_parameters` bool `lb_split` (default `true`) replaces the `!parameters.incubator_mode` term in `proveKernel`'s gate, which becomes `mainPath = parameters.lb_split && !parameters.disable_lb_split`. The four small-LB incubator configs (`ConfigIncubatorPeano1/2`, `ConfigIncubatorGauss1/2`) set `false`, keeping their previous unsplit behaviour; `ConfigIncubatorGauss3` — the AnchorIncubator3 FTA-rung batch with heavy enumeration LBs — sets `true` and now splits; `ConfigPeano`/`ConfigGauss` carry no key and split by default. A permanent one-line `[SPLIT] straggler:` report (work, `T`, parts, exprKey) prints on each unsplit → split transition next to the existing `[SPLIT] ineffective` line — pure observation, no control-flow effect.

**Why.** The incubator exclusion was hardcoded on the wrong axis: the reason to run unsplit is a grid of thousands of small LBs whose per-part request-generation setup is redundant, not incubator-ness itself. IncubatorGauss3's rung LBs are exactly the heavy straggler shape the D-201 trigger was built for, yet the mode coupling made splitting them impossible. Same decoupling pattern as `ban_disintegration` ([I-7](30_invariants.md#i-7)). The default is `true` so a future main-batch config cannot silently regress to unsplit by forgetting the key; opting out is explicit.

**Boundaries.** The trigger itself (`isStraggler`, `min_split_work`) is unchanged — the flag decides only which batches run the split path. IncubatorGauss3 inherits the full D-201 semantics, including the preemptive split of newly activated induction-zero LBs. `disable_lb_split` keeps its separate diagnostic / RT-profiling meaning ([D-110](#d-110)); the two flags are independent. No config sets `min_split_work`; every batch runs the 20000 default.

**Verification.** Full rebuild (Release x64) + `gl_quick.exe --unit-tests` green (new `lb_split_defaults_true`, `lb_split_config_wiring`). One full pipeline run: `[SPLIT] straggler:` present in the IncubatorGauss3 portion of the log, verifier failure 0 in every category, `theorems.txt` unchanged. Incubator proof-graph artifacts may legitimately differ from the unsplit baseline (D-201: split vs unsplit is not byte-identical at the proof-graph level); any such diff is reported, not silently absorbed.

**Current configuration.** [D-328](#d-328) later enables the same statistics-driven eligibility in all five production incubator configurations. The per-config ownership introduced here and the trigger itself remain unchanged.

<a id="d-230"></a>
## D-230 — twin retirement at emission + per-iteration deactivation sweep (2026-07-26,, maintainer-approved)


**The choice (maintainer-approved: "try a and b").** Two timeliness fixes to the LB-deactivation machinery, found by an instrumented investigation of Peano main's slowness. (a) `deactivateUnnecessary` retires both `__contradiction__` twins of the settled head at the theorem's final chain node, right after its path walk resolves — every emission drain (`updateGlobalDirect` both polarities, the auxy path) now retires twins at emission instead of waiting for [D-224](#d-224)'s goal-closure staging, which for a theorem proved by induction or in another LB fires only on the broadcast re-fire one or more bursts later. The staged path remains as the second trigger; the flip is idempotent, same single-threaded post-join seam. (b) `prove` runs `deactivateRecursively` once per iteration after the drains — formerly the global sweep ran only from `deactivateUnnecessary`'s tail (emission-only), so LBs whose last main-scope goal closed after the batch's final emission stayed active to batch end. Same I-48 predicate, evaluated every iteration.

**Evidence (per-iteration audit, pre-fix).** Induction auxiliaries of proved theorems: never late (the emission-time `deactivateUnnecessary` walk already covers them, [D-223](#d-223)). Contradiction twins: 2–44 live twins of already-proved theorems on nearly every Peano main burst, 280 twin-burst units total, each twin carrying tens of thousands of submatches per lingering burst. Sweep orphans: 12 goal-free, child-free, unprimed chain LBs (deep `in3[..,*]` nodes) active from ~burst 15 to batch end. Not touched by this decision: the dominant heavy-burst cost (burst 13's 296 s) is genuine in-progress induction proof work (`(=[13,2])_induction_rec2_` at 2.7M work), proved in that same burst — intrinsic, not a leak.

**Boundaries.** Both changes only ADVANCE deactivations the existing machinery already performs (same predicates, same seams); no new deactivation criterion. The retired verbatim twin of a proved head could never fire (its assumed head is consistent with the proved theorem); the retired negated twin could only re-derive the already-emitted theorem (sink-deduped, D-216). Gate: full pipeline, `theorems.txt` unchanged, verifiers airtight, per-iteration audit shows lateContra = 0 and idle = 0.

<a id="d-229"></a>
## D-229 — a CE-refuted operator-only conjecture refutes its pool mirror too (2026-07-26,, maintainer-approved)


**The choice (maintainer-specified).** The CE filter gains a mirror-refutation pass: after each fact-file pass's worker pool joins, every conjecture the CE bursts refuted seeds a flip of its mirror partner's `contradictionTable` slot to refuted, so the partner never reaches the prover. Pairing comes from a new conjecturer artifact, `files/theorems/mirror_pairs.txt` — one `source<TAB>mirror` row per operator-only conjecture whose mirror entered the pool, both columns captured at pool admission and therefore byte-identical to `conjectures.txt` lines. The emission gate (`Conjecturer::consistsOnlyOfOperators`) requires every non-anchor constituent, premises and head, to be a plain non-negated operator application. The flip is symmetric (either member's CE refutation dooms the other), non-cascading (only CE-confirmed refutations seed, so the outcome is a pure function of the CE verdicts plus the pairs file), and gated on the new `prover_parameters` flag `mirror_refutation` (default `true`).

**Why.** Since [D-112](#d-112) every conjecture's reverse direction rides the pool as a real conjecture. A counterexample refuting the forward direction never witnesses against the reverse (it satisfies the reverse's premise side only vacuously), so the false reverse routinely survives the finite-model CE boundary and burns prover runtime — warm-up plus main iterations — on a statement that is false for the same semantic reason its source is. The heuristic: for operator-only conjecture pairs, one direction's ground counterexample is treated as refuting both. This is deliberately not deductively clean — a true reverse of a false source would be wrongly discarded — accepted by the maintainer as a theoretical corner case outside the explored arithmetic (zero FTA relevance), in a stage that is already heuristic (the CE oracle is the incubator's re-encoded output with j-copy heuristics).

**Boundaries.** Refutation-side only: no mirror ever re-enters as a proof step ([I-81](30_invariants.md#i-81) and D-112 untouched); refuted conjectures leave no proof artifacts, so no verifier or tag work. Pair recomputation inside the filter was rejected: the two `createReshuffledMirrored` twins (conjecturer member vs `compiler.hpp` free function) have diverged internally, so a filter-side recompute risks silent byte-mismatch lookup misses; the sidecar file pins the pairing to the strings the pool actually carries. Incubator batches write an empty pairs file (their pool lines are rewritten post-capture by `reformulateOperatorHead`) and skip the CE filter anyway.

**Verification.** Direct unit tests on the gate, the row builder, the loader, and the flip pass; then one full pipeline run — verifiers airtight, `theorems.txt` unchanged vs the committed state, per-pass flip counts in the log, overall runtime at or below the 1489.5 s baseline.

<a id="d-210"></a>
## D-210 — the distinct-secondary cap widens only inside a single shared `_orint_` scope (2026-07-25,, maintainer-approved)


**The choice (maintainer-specified).** `requestGatesPass` gains a scoped widening of its distinct-secondary gate: a request whose distinct `it_*_lev_*` count exceeds `maxNumberSecondaryVariables` is still admitted when (a) it does not exceed the new `maxNumberSecondaryVariablesOrint`, (b) every premise sits at ONE shared validity scope, and (c) that scope is an `_orint_` branch (`containsSpan(decodeView(v0), "_orint_")`). The decode runs only on the rare over-standard-cap path. The rung-2 batch config sets the standard cap back to 2 and the `_orint_` cap to 3.

**Why.** The rung-2 root cause (previous entry's diagnosis) is that the second predecessor level's successor-addition firing needs 3 distinct `it_` witnesses inside the reverse clause's `_orint_` branch — and both measured global widenings exploded: cap 4 reached 457-second bursts (6,982 firings of the all-variable class) and flat cap 3 reached 198-second bursts with the batch's expression count tripling per burst. The predecessor-descent chain lives entirely at one `_orint_` branch scope (all four premises of the needed instance are at the branch, verified in the trap and trace), so conditioning the extra budget on "all premises at one shared `_orint_` scope" grants it to exactly the descent chains while every mixed-scope and non-branch request keeps the standard cap — including the broad anchor-rule fan-out that drove both explosions.

**Rejected alternatives.** Global cap 4 and flat cap 3 (measured explosions, runs stopped); counting predecessor witnesses like products of recursion (a wider exemption — weakens the cap in every scope, not just where descent needs it).

**Safety and verification.** The gate stays a sound over-approximation in the same sense as before (it only ADMITS more, never drops a previously admitted request); the widening is default-off (`maxNumberSecondaryVariablesOrint` defaults equal to the standard cap), so every batch that does not set it is byte-identical. Direct unit coverage: positive (3 distinct secondaries, one shared `_orint_` scope, widened cap), and negatives for unconfigured widening, mixed scopes, non-`_orint_` shared scope, and count above the widened cap. Full-pipeline measurement is the acceptance gate.

<a id="d-211"></a>
## D-211 — K mutual-exclusion implications emit at every OR depth; only branch opening is depth-gated (2026-07-25,, maintainer-approved)


**The choice (maintainer-approved).** In `disintegrateExprCore2`'s OR case, the expansion record and the K mutual-exclusion implications (for each leaf `d_i`: `!d_0 ∧ … ∧ !d_{i-1} ∧ !d_{i+1} ∧ … ⇒ d_i`) are emitted unconditionally, at every OR depth. Only the per-branch case-split — the part that mints `_ordis_` scopes — remains gated on `currentOrDepth < parameters.max_or_depth` (and on the D-32 admission flag). Previously the depth gate wrapped the whole OR case, so an OR statement landing inside an existing `_ordis_`/`_orint_` branch was inserted inert: no expansion row, no K implications.

**Why.** The rung-2 reverse clause stalled exactly here: in the true clause's atomic `_orint_` branches, `q∈N`, the derived `q≠0`, and the predecessor disjunction `or0[1,q,3,2]` ("∃pred(q) ∨ q=0") were all live for nine bursts with no rule able to combine them — the disjunctive-syllogism rules the depth-0 scopes get were suppressed by the depth gate. The gate conflated two different consumptions of an OR statement: opening nested branch scopes (the scope explosion `max_or_depth` exists to prevent) and emitting flat hash rules that create no scopes. The human proof's step "`q≠0` ∧ (∃pred(q) ∨ q=0) ⟹ ∃pred(q)" needs only the flat rules.

**Rejected alternative.** Branch-local nested case analysis (`_ordis_` inside `_orint_` with contradictory-branch rejection) subsumes the syllogism but is a much larger machine; it remains the general fallback track if flat rules alone cannot close the remainder of the chain.

**Safety and verification.** The moved block is byte-identical logic, dedented; the K implications carry the same `disintegration` origin citing the same expansion row, so `check_disintegration`'s `or` branch verifies the new rows unchanged. Gate: full pipeline run, verifier airtight, baseline theorems (Gauss summation included) intact.

<a id="d-213"></a>
## D-213 — Peano main runs both contradiction-LB polarities (2026-07-25,, maintainer-approved)


**The choice (maintainer-approved after a measured trial).** `ConfigPeano.json` sets `try_contradiction` AND `try_contradiction_negated_head` — the first main-path (non-incubator) contradiction activation. Both flags deliberately: the CE filter's finite boundary is not 100% effective, so the verbatim disprover has value in main too (its firing emits the negation of a false CE-surviving conjecture as a real theorem), and the reductio complement proves heads the direct machinery cannot reach.

**Measured outcome (the acceptance evidence).** Peano main proven 54 → 60; the globally essential set 46 → 48, including the injectivity contrapositive `s(a)=b ∧ s(c)=d ∧ b≠d ⇒ a≠c` now proved at AnchorPeano itself, negated vacuous-family forms, and a mirror-form additive identity. Three previously essential theorems were compressed out as newly derivable (a mirror swap and two subsumptions) — content preserved by compression's own derivability proof. Runtime unchanged (598.5 s vs ~600 baseline; the [twin deactivation](#d-224) and [induction cleanup](#d-223) absorb the ~250 extra contradiction LBs). Existence-headed conjectures took contradiction LBs — including positive-existence seeds, live for the first time — without anomaly; the whole pipeline verified airtight (133098 checks, 0 failures).

**Context.** The same activation across all five incubators was separately tried and rejected (no yield, massive slowdown) — main batches profit because their pools are CE-filtered toward plausible, hard conjectures; incubator pools are exhaustive and their direct machinery already saturates them.

**Gauss main (same decision, follow-on trial).** `ConfigGauss.json` sets both flags too — kept by maintainer decision after a successful null-result run: 10 proven unchanged, all 48 essential theorems retained, zero new lines, runtime 333.5 s vs ~320-330 baseline (flat), pipeline airtight (133104 checks, 0 failures). No yield today — Gauss main's survivors are deep structural fold/interval theorems, not reductio-shaped — but the activation is harmless and keeps both mains uniform for future pools.

<a id="d-223"></a>
## D-223 — every emitted theorem retires the recursion auxiliaries of both head polarities (2026-07-25,, maintainer-approved)


**The choice (maintainer-approved).** `updateGlobalDirect` adds one call beside its existing `deactivateUnnecessary(theorem, root)`: the same walk on the head-negated twin form `reconstructImplication(chain, negate(head))`. Uniform for every emitted theorem — no contradiction-specific gating; a twin form matching no `originalAuxyMap` entry is a defined no-op walk on a single-threaded seam.

**Why.** A verbatim contradiction LB's fire emits the *negation* of its registered conjecture; that string matches no `originalAuxyMap` entry, so the disproved conjecture's induction triads idled to batch end. Prepared for the main-path contradiction activation (Peano main is where induction auxiliaries are heavyweight). The complement direction needed nothing: its emission IS the registered conjecture, which the existing call already matches. Bonus coverage: a proved head also settles the opposite-head conjecture wherever both were registered.

<a id="d-224"></a>
## D-224 — a settled conjecture retires its contradiction LBs (2026-07-25,, maintainer-approved)


**The choice (maintainer-approved).** Contradiction LBs deactivate when their purpose is fulfilled, not only when they themselves fire. Two triggers: a firing contradiction LB stages its polarity sibling (same parent, key `__contradiction__` + negate(own seed) — the two are logically mutually exclusive, so a fire settles both); an ordinary goal closure in a chain LB stages both of the closed head's contradiction twins (a primed closer stages its sibling instead, never itself). The stage runs at the discharge sites (worker phase); the `isActive` flip is deferred to a post-join drain directly after the theorem drain (I-28), idempotent and order-free. Twin keys are built on the scratch arena and probed through a new `SimpleMapStore::findChild` span overload, keeping the statified discharge functions heap-free.

**Why.** A primed LB is exempt from the deactivation survey by design (it has no goal, so the goal-based "done" test would kill it before its facts arrive) — but that exemption also meant a *redundant* twin idled to batch end, absorbing mail and running bursts for nothing, and could then fire a duplicate emission of an already-proved theorem. With the reductio complement doubling the contra-LB population, the idle cost and the duplicate firings scale with the pool. The [sink dedup](#d-216) makes the artifacts correct regardless; this decision removes the wasted runtime at its source and keeps the `deactivateRecursively` bubble-up unblocked (an eternally-active child pins its parent chain alive — the reason main-batch contradiction activation, the roadmap's next step, needs this in place first).

**Rejected alternative.** Widening the deactivation survey with a "theorem already proved" criterion — the survey is a per-iteration tree walk with no linkage from conjectures to their contradiction children; the discharge sites have that linkage in hand for free.

<a id="d-216"></a>
## D-216 — globalTheoremList insertion is insert-if-absent on the theorem string (2026-07-25,, maintainer-approved)


**The choice (maintainer-approved).** All nine `globalTheoremList` writers (the four `updateGlobalDirect` rows, the two `updateGlobal` rows, `addTheoremToMemory`'s pre-registered-head row, the OR construction in `run_modes.cpp`, and the export rebuild's debug rows) route through one guarded door, `ExpressionAnalyzer::appendGlobalTheorem`: under `theoremListMutex`, probe the companion `globalTheoremStrings` set and append only on first sight of the theorem string. First emission wins — the retained tuple keeps the first-drained method label. The export rebuild's `clear` clears both containers. Side effects at the emission sites (console print, `checkOrCompletion`, pending compaction) are unchanged — the dedup governs the list, which is what the theorems files and the chapter export iterate.

**Why.** The [complementary reductio LB](#d-214) made double emission systematic: a theorem proved by a contradiction LB is broadcast, re-fires on its own conjecture's premises, and closes the goal a second time — 56 of IncubatorPeano2's theorems landed twice in `theorems.txt` and produced duplicate proof chapters. The incubator save path and the chapter export iterate `globalTheoremList` with no dedup of their own, and `drainUpdateGlobalDirect`'s index-sorted replay makes first-wins deterministic. Opposite-polarity conjecture pairs could already double-emit before the reductio work; the sink closes that class too.

**Accepted consequence.** A cross-method string collision (the same theorem string reachable as `direct` and as `reformulated statement`) keeps only the first-drained row and its chapter — deliberate under first-wins.

<a id="d-214"></a>
## D-214 — a config flag gives every registered conjecture a complementary reductio LB (2026-07-25,, maintainer-approved)


**The choice (maintainer-approved, user-specified design).** New `ProverParameters` flag `try_contradiction_negated_head` (default false; currently true only in `ConfigIncubatorPeano2.json`). When set, conjecture registration (`addTheoremToMemory`, innermost chain node) creates for EVERY registered conjecture — uniformly, no head-shape filter — a second contradiction LB, the complement of the `try_contradiction` one: key `__contradiction__` + `negate(head)`, seeded with `negate(head)` as status-0 main-scope fuel, `contradictionTheoremId` = the conjecture itself. The existing discharge machinery is polarity-agnostic, so a main-scope contradiction in the complement proves the conjecture (reductio), where the verbatim LB — which assumes the head — can only ever disprove it. Same skip-on-exists dedup; the collision with an opposite-head conjecture's verbatim LB on the same chain is byte-identical in seed and theorem, so the skip is lossless in either registration order.

**Why.** The [template addon](#d-215)'s injectivity contrapositive (head `!(=[a,c])`) was formulated in the incubator batches but unprovable: the verbatim contradiction LB assumes an already-true negated head and targets the false positive equality — inert — and no other prover path proves a variable-level negated-equality head registered already-negated. The complement assumes the positive equality, the equivalence class collapses the two `in2` premises, functional uniqueness contradicts the `!(=[b,d])` premise, and the discharge emits the needed theorem at `AnchorIncubator3`, from which it propagates to the rung-2 batch as a loaded proved theorem.

**Consequential polarity generalizations (same decision, maintainer-consented incl. the I-16 verifier edit).** Three consumers were hard-wired to the verbatim polarity and generalize symmetrically, byte-identical for all previously exercised shapes: `dischargeContradiction`'s origin-record key becomes `negateScratch(cleanOp)` instead of an unconditional `'!'` prefix (also fixes the latent `!!X` record a fired negated-seed LB would have produced); `buildStack`'s two contradiction fallbacks probe `__contradiction__` + `negate(provedHead)` for either head polarity; `verifier.py`'s `check_task_formulation` / `check_contradiction` accept the seed/record relation symmetrically (explicit maintainer consent per [I-16](30_invariants.md#i-16), no weakening — the checks still require exact negation pairs).

**Rejected alternatives.** Emitting negated variants of every conjecture into the conjecturer pool (doubles the pool and re-triggers head-switch machinery). Dual theorem ids on the verbatim LB (breaks the fire-once discharge contract). In-code head-polarity special-casing without a config flag (cost decision belongs in the batch config; uniform treatment per conjecture is simpler and general).

**Scope caution.** `negate` on a compact `existence<N>`/`or<N>` head produces a negated compact seed — an exercised statement shape, but the flag has only been validated on equality-headed pools (`only_in_head` restricts IncubatorPeano2 to `=` heads); enabling it in an OR-headed batch should revisit that path.

<a id="d-217"></a>
## D-217 — headSwitchOne cancels the double negation of an already-negated head (2026-07-24,, maintainer-approved)


**The choice (maintainer-approved, option 1 of the presented fix space).** `headSwitchOne`'s contrapositive construction builds the new premise from the old head as `head.substr(1)` when the head already starts with `!`, instead of the former unconditional `"!" + head`. Mathematically identical (`!!X == X`); byte-level it emits `(=[a,c])` where the old code emitted `!!(=[a,c])`.

**Why.** The [template addon](#d-215) put the first conjecture with BOTH a negated premise and a negated head into the pool (`...!(=[b,d]) implies!(=[a,c])`). The pre-emit head-switch pass, which folds the contrapositive of every structurally-qualifying pool conjecture, blindly prefixed `!` to the negated head and produced a raw `!!(=[..])` premise. GL has no universal double-negation normalizer (OPEN-MPL-1), so the malformed mirror survived to `prepareIntegration`, whose compiled-core assert stopped the run (trap-verified: `expression='(>[]!!(=[15,17])(=[16,18]))'`, IncubatorPeano1). Every pre-existing pool conjecture had a positive head, so the blind prefix was previously unreachable — the assert surfaced a latent construction bug, not a new one.

**Rejected alternative.** Returning empty from `headSwitchOne` for negated-head theorems (no mirror) — conservative, but it withholds a legitimate, provable contrapositive: for the template conjecture the corrected mirror is the operator's functionality direction `op(a)=b and op(c)=d and a=c implies b=d`.

<a id="d-215"></a>
## D-215 — conjecturer template addon emits the injectivity contrapositive per single-input operator (2026-07-24,, maintainer-approved)


**The choice (maintainer-approved).** The conjecturer gains a template addon — the first case of a template-conjecture technique intended to grow. For every operator with exactly one input argument, one output argument, and a positive `max_count_per_conjecture`, and only when `=` also carries a positive `max_count_per_conjecture` in the batch config, `Conjecturer::generateTemplateConjectures` builds the stump `op(a)=b and op(c)=d and b!=d implies a!=c` (for `in2`: `(>[1,2](in2[1,2,5])(>[3,4](in2[3,4,5])(>[]!(=[2,4])!(=[1,3]))))`). The stump binds its element variables itself, so `findArgMap` leaves only the operator slot(s) free, and the stump rides the standard string-path anchor attachment `singleExprAnchorConnection` — every coupling of the free slots to type-matching anchor slots, the standard filter tail, reshuffle, and mirror lane. Survivors fold into `run`'s result sets with the preliminary-pass dedup before sorting, so they participate in the mirror merge and the `conjectures.txt` write like any enumerated conjecture. No new config fields: batches qualify or not from their existing entries (Peano main and IncubatorPeano1/2 emit for `in2`; all Gauss batches emit nothing because their `=` has `max_count_per_conjecture` 0).

**Why.** Rung 2's reverse interval clause stalls because the second predecessor split needs `q!=0` *derived* and no loaded rule produces a variable-level negated equality; the contrapositive of successor injectivity manufactures exactly that. The main enumeration can never assemble the shape — it needs two `=` atoms while the `=` per-conjecture count cap is 1 (raising the cap batch-wide would explode the pool; the addon sidesteps the cap for one fixed, known-sound shape). The theorem proved in Peano main then propagates to later batches as an external.

**Rejected alternatives.** Emitting through the int lane (`singleExprAnchorConnectionInt`) — `encodeExpr` parses only positive leaf chains and cannot represent `!(` premises; the stump must never reach `encodeExpr`. Hand-attaching the anchor like the OR addon (`generateOrConjectures`) — would hardcode the operator-slot→anchor-slot mapping instead of reusing the coupling enumeration ("in all possible ways" was the requirement). Raising the `=` count cap in config — pool explosion, see above.

<a id="d-227"></a>
## D-227 — equivalence-class history cites each justifying equality at its origin scope (2026-07-24, extended 2026-08-14)


**The choice (maintainer-approved, option A of the presented fix space).** `applyEquivalenceClassToNegatedEquality`'s `equality1` history line cites the synthesized justifying equality `(=[b,d])` at the scope where that equality's `exprOriginMap` row actually lives, not at the negation's own scope. The emitter threads the class's scope from the `emitFromClassesAt` walk into the emission and probes non-minting (`lookupOriginKey` span twin + `exprOriginMap.lookup`) at the class's scope first, then the class scope's strict ancestors deepest-first (class content can be inherited from ancestor-scope merges, I-33). A probe that misses everywhere asserts at the emission (Rule 19). The source negation stays cited at its own scope; the rewritten row still deposits at the negation's scope.

The same producer-side rule applies to ordinary `applyEquivalenceClass` rewrites. Its class may sit inside an `_ordis_` branch while containing equality content absorbed from an ancestor class. Each justifier is probed at the class scope and then its strict ancestors deepest-first; the resulting `equality1` dependency names the first scope whose body origin row exists. The rewritten statement still deposits at `deeperOf(class scope, expression scope)`; only the provenance citation is corrected.

It also applies independently to both bridge dependencies of `mergeTwoEquivalenceClasses`'s `equality2` rows. A cross-scope merge can derive a branch equality through one branch-local bridge half and one equality absorbed from `main`; each dependency keeps the first actual origin scope found from the merge scope upward. The derived equality remains branch-scoped.

**Why.** The `_orint_` branch peer negations expanded by [D-226](#d-226) sit inside a branch while the witness-binding equality justifying the rewrite lives at the integration scope above the branch boundary. The old citation named the branch scope; the chapter walker resolves a dependency at its cited validity and `liftToShallowestOriginAncestor` deliberately refuses to lift across an `_orint_`/`_ordis_` boundary, so the citation could never resolve — the rung-2 chapter-export crash (`buildStack: no origin found` on `(=[repl_lev_1_2,int_lev_1_5])`). The equality's body rows exist (both orders, written at arrival by `updateEquivalenceClasses`' trackHistory block and the mirror machinery) — only the citation pointed where they are not. The verifier's `check_equality1` namespace rule explicitly accepts each cited equality at any strict ancestor of the row's namespace, so the corrected citation is verifier-legal.

**Rejected alternatives.** Emission-time materialization of a body row copied from the class's `equalityOriginMap` (unnecessary — trap evidence showed the body rows already exist; the class-side record is redundant with them). Folding class `equalityOriginMap` into the body map at class teardown (same reason, plus it would retain dead-scope history wholesale). Relaxing the walker's or-branch lift boundary (unsound direction — a branch-scope fact must not lift above its branch; the boundary is correct, the citation was wrong). An existence-gate that silently skips the expansion on probe miss (defensive; would starve the rung-2 K mutual-exclusion rules again and hide the next producer gap — the assert surfaces it at its origin instead).

<a id="d-226"></a>
## D-226 — negated-equality expansion fires on class formation, not only on negation arrival (2026-07-24,, maintainer-approved)


**The choice (maintainer-approved).** `applyEquiClasses` Pass 1 (delta classes × all registry statements) no longer skips negated equalities wholesale: when a delta class touching either argument of a registered `!(=[a,b])` sits at or above the negation's scope, the row is routed to `applyEquivalenceClassToNegatedEquality` — the same one-sided expander the arrival-time hook uses (I-12's rule unchanged). Pass 2 still skips negated equalities (a new statement always had its arrival-time expansion), and positive equalities remain the class-merge machinery's.

**Why.** The expansion previously ran at exactly one moment — negation arrival — so a negation inserted BEFORE its variable's class formed was never expanded: the general pass filtered negated equalities by design, and nothing revisited them on class growth. FTA rung 2 sits exactly on that hole: the `_orint_` peer negations are seeded at branch creation, the interval witness-binding equality (element = witness) arrives bursts later, and the or-theorem K mutual-exclusion rules — keyed to the witness form after cFE suppressed the element form's disintegration — could then never fire. The fix is the exact mirror of what Pass 1 already does for every non-equality statement; negated equalities stop being the one shape with an insertion-order dependency. Idempotence rests on the expander's `lookupStatementLevels` dedup; the member pre-check keeps the pass linear.

**Rejected alternatives.** Restoring the consumed or-theorem parents (maintainer: parents must not be necessary — the or head's K-implications play their role). Exempting OR shapes from cFE suppression (treats the symptom; any consumer needing a bridged negation would hit the same hole again). Making the arrival-time expansion two-sided (unrelated to the ordering hole; I-12's one-sided rule is load-bearing).

<a id="d-225"></a>
## D-225 — status-3 absorb admits negated compact existences as the second rule-carrier shape (2026-07-23,, maintainer-approved)


**The choice (maintainer-approved).** The external-mail absorb (`addExprToMemoryBlock`, `status=3`) admits exactly TWO shapes to `disintegrateExpr2`: the compact implication `(implication<N>[…])` (per [D-84](#d-84--status3-external-mail-absorb-routes-recovered-implications-to-overallhashmemory--workingmemory-recovered-facts-to-externalstatementsintexternalstatements-2026-05-18-branch-sandboxhashburst_reshuffle-commit-4f7a8668)) and, new here, the negated compact existence `!(existence<N>[…])`. Every other mailed expression stays a bare statement. The call-site tripwire assert states the same two-shape contract.

**Why.** A negated compact existence is a universal in De-Morgan clothing — disintegrating it installs its universal rule and mints NO witnesses (witness minting belongs to the positive existence opening), so the `MAX_NAME_IDS` / runaway concern that motivated the narrow gate does not apply to it. Left statement-only, an inherited universal premise is inert at every descendant: the ancestor's rule copy can never see descendant-local facts because mail flows only parent→children ([I-57](30_invariants.md#i-57)). Concretely, the Peano OR-companion theorem "no predecessor ⇒ n=0" lost its proof this way — its induction step sub-LB inherited "7 has no predecessor" as a bare statement, the vacuous-truth contradiction never formed, the companion failed, `constructOrTheorem` was starved of one parent, and the predecessor OR theorem disappeared from every artifact (early-May regression window, the absorb-path existence-suppression era).

**Result.** The companion closes by vacuous truth at its second burst; `or0[N,v1,s,i0]` is constructed again (`or theorem` method row), registered in the shared operator registry, and exported to the incubator externals. Full pipeline: 131,827 verifier checks, 0 failures; Gauss summation intact; runtime 1448 s (baseline ≈1650 s). The batch additionally disproves the false cross-pair `EnumerationSet2 ⇒ interval[0,2]` outright (a sound negated-head theorem). Sacred-dump evidence:  (broken state),  (repaired state).

<a id="d-221"></a>
## D-221 — close descendant goals from the strongest visible ancestor fact (2026-07-23,, maintainer-approved)


**The choice (maintainer-approved).** After exact statement-delta discharge, `dischargeToBeProved` snapshots the unresolved goals in decoded lexical order. For each non-main goal whose scope is not already scheduled for removal, it walks that goal's canonical `NameMap` ancestry from root toward the goal. The first known statement for the goal expression is the strongest visible proof source. Its statement-level row supplies the emitted levels; its exact validity is cited by provenance. The goal's own validity still controls `_orint_` / implication classification, parent-scope emission, and cleanup. The ancestor fact is never inserted again at the child.

**Why.** GL facts are visible from an ancestor validity inside every descendant validity, but the old scoped-goal discharge reacted only when a new statement's validity exactly equalled the goal validity. FTA rung 2 therefore held the needed reverse-membership fact at an ancestor while the atomic `_orint_` goal remained open below it. The inference engine already honoured this lexical visibility for premise matching; goal closure did not.

**Rejected alternatives.** Copying the ancestor fact into the child would create a redundant local statement and misleading provenance. Using the proof-source ancestor to choose cleanup would wipe the wrong cohort. Choosing the nearest known ancestor would make a weaker duplicate override the canonical shallow source. Scanning goals in registry-id order would expose interning order as proof order.

**Safety and verification.** The scan uses the canonical root-to-self ancestor list, the existing decoded-lex goal sorter, fixed level storage, and the existing string scratch tier. Every chosen source must have its statement-level row. Direct tests cover both fact-before-goal and goal-before-fact arrival, shallowest-source levels and provenance, sibling rejection, exact-goal cleanup, and absence of a redundant child fact. See [I-164](30_invariants.md#i-164).

<a id="d-218"></a>
## D-218 — flatten every contiguous nested OR into one case-split cohort (2026-07-14,, maintainer-approved)


**The choice (maintainer-approved).** OR disintegration recursively walks every compiled child whose category is also `or` in the already-instantiated `WorkInstruction`, in the same `disintegrateExprCore2` call. It preserves left-to-right element order and stops at the first non-OR expression, even when that expression has its own children. The resulting non-OR leaves form one flat cohort: they define the De Morgan expansion, the K mutual-exclusion implications, the K asserted branch seeds, and the registered disjunct count. The outer compiled OR signature remains the sole provenance and namespace identity for all of those rows and for the parent-scoped cohort; no intermediate OR-valued branch is minted for a later hashburst. `max_or_depth=1` therefore admits the whole contiguous OR tree as one logical disjunction rather than one syntax level. The verifier recursively reconstructs the same ordered leaves for `expansion`, OR `disintegration`, `or disintegration`, and `or convergence`; the matching reverse contract is [D-220](#d-220).

**Why.** FTA rung 2 compiles three-way membership as `(D1 or D2) or D3`. The old runtime opened only the outer pair and installed `D1 or D2` as an opaque asserted branch seed through `addStatement`; that path never re-entered disintegration, so the two dependency-complete atomic cases were absent from the trace. This was an execution/representation gap, not a missing mathematical dependency or a convergence failure. One flat logical cohort matches the meaning of nested disjunction and makes every alternative visible in the same hashburst.

**Rejected alternatives.** Recursively opening the intermediate OR in a later hashburst would create nested branch namespaces, split provenance between two signatures, consume depth per syntax node, and make three logically peer alternatives arrive in different execution rounds. Flattening definitions across a non-OR boundary would instead change the meaning of that intervening operator. Both are outside the approved contract.

**Safety and verification.** The producer walks only the prepared read-only instruction graph, allocates nothing, asserts cycles, structurally inconsistent duplicate signatures, recursion overflow, and leaf-cap overflow, and preserves the outer signature byte-for-byte. Direct C++ coverage proves both left/right nested flattening and the non-OR stop boundary. Verifier tests accept a three-leaf flat branch, convergence, De Morgan expansion, and mutual implication, while rejecting the former intermediate-OR branch. The full rung-2 Windows pipeline and trace are the end-to-end gate.

<a id="d-220"></a>
## D-220 — flatten reverse OR preparation into one atomic-leaf cohort (2026-07-23,, maintainer-approved)


**The choice (maintainer-approved).** Reverse OR preparation uses the same `flattenOrLeaves` traversal as disintegration. `prepareIntegrationCore2` identifies integration-eligible OR entities referenced directly by another eligible OR, validates every eligible OR through the shared flattener, and prepares only maximal roots. Each root is flattened before one renaming pass. The K ordered atomic leaves then define K sub-implications and K `_orint_` scopes: branch `i` has leaf `D_i` as its goal and the negations of every `D_j`, `j!= i`, as assumptions. The outer signature remains the only namespace and provenance identity.

**Why.** FTA rung 2 reached the reverse membership boundary with the outer `p=2` branch carrying only `!(p=0 ∨ p=1)`. Immediate-child integration treated the compiled inner OR as one opaque alternative, so the branch never received the atomic `!p=0` and `!p=1` exclusions needed to mirror the already-working forward split.

**Rejected alternatives.** Preparing the nested entity again creates two semantically overlapping cohorts and leaves proof progress dependent on a later hashburst. Special-casing the rung expression would encode a theorem shape in the engine. Flattening through a non-OR child would change the intervening operator's meaning.

**Safety and verification.** Production uses fixed stack arrays plus the existing string scratch arena, preserves leaf order and the outer signature, and asserts malformed cycles or capacity excess. Native tests require three atomic branches with both peer negations and no intermediate OR branch. Verifier tests accept atomic integration expansion/proven/assumption rows and reject their opaque-inner counterparts. See [I-168](30_invariants.md#i-168).

<a id="d-219"></a>
## D-219 — key every OR cohort action by parent validity plus original OR signature (2026-07-14 / 2026-07-23, /, maintainer-approved)


**The choice (maintainer-approved).** Treat each OR family as a cohort identified by `(parentValidity, originalOrSignature)`. On `_ordis_`, the two component strings are interned in the existing append-only `lbStateInterner`; `mintOrCohortId` packs their ids into eight canonical bytes and interns that pair as one scalar cohort id. The existing cold containers and deload tags stay unchanged: `orDisjunctCount[cohortId]` stores the branch count, while `orBookkeeping[(conclusionId, cohortId)]` stores the decoded-lex branch payload set. `ordisMerge` therefore fires only after all branches belonging to the same conclusion, parent, and original signature have deposited. On `_orint_`, `cleanUpOrIntegrationBranches` receives the exact parent id of the proving goal and queues only direct integration children with both that parent and outer signature; its `wipeSubtree` drain covers their descendants. Per the maintainer's explicit Rule-14 approval, the sacred hashburst format changes only the disintegration rows: `orBookkeeping` adds `parent=...`, and `orDisjunctCount` prints `parent=... | orSig=... | count=...`; target selection, sections, ordering, call sites, and path are untouched.

**Why.** The old convergence key was `(conclusion, orSignature)`, the old count was by bare `orSignature`, and reverse cleanup also selected victims by bare signature. A compiled signature can exist under multiple validity-stack parents, so deposits from separate case splits could collectively reach the count and proving one reverse cohort could erase another.
